_rec.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS (Cycle 2 only; the full FSMSI path is 4 years / 240 ECTS including Cycle 1)
_rec.focus: Music Production + Recording/Engineering + Immersive/Spatial Audio + Sound Design (option) + live sound
_rec.institutionType: Public conservatoire national supérieur (Ministère de la Culture), member of Université PSL
_rec.language: French (interviews are held in French); an 'Anglais : métiers de l'audiovisuel' module is compulsory
_rec.whatYouStudy: Two individualised years with a chosen professional specialisation among PRODUCTION MUSICALE, SPECTACLE VIVANT or CRÉATION, under personal tutors. Compulsory modules with ECTS: Technologie audio (12), Projets de production / 'Book' (24), Projet de recherche (22), Prise de son classique (9), Prise de son jazz et musiques actuelles (9), Mixage musiques actuelles (9), Mixage musique acoustique (9), Travaux pratiques FSMSI, Communication et gestion de projet (4), Stage FSMSI (20), plus law/regulation and live-performance safety modules. Optional 5-ECTS modules include Design sonore, Mastering, 'Réalisation et mixage en musiques actuelles', 'Vidéo 360, Audio 3D, nouveaux médias', 'Réalisation en informatique musicale : développement, création, répertoire', Direction artistique, Sonorisation, Son à l'image, Arrangement (chanson ou jazz), Création/composition/production pour la musique à l'image. Compulsory two-month placement with the Conservatoire's audiovisual department; research themes include Audio 3D, spatialisation for live performance, augmented reality, 360 video. Optional joint Licence Musique et Musicologie with Sorbonne Université.
_rec.entryRequirements: 'No age limit for this competition.' Prerequisites as published for the 2026-2027 entry: 'BAC+3 diploma (European bachelor's degree or bachelor's degree from a scientific, technical or audiovisual training course) or international equivalent' AND 'D.E.M level from a Conservatoire for music. Applicants must have a very good knowledge of music theory, a sound musical culture, a knowledge of composition (harmony and/or counterpoint) and musical analysis.' French: candidates admitted to the 2nd cycle who are not nationals of francophone countries must present CEFR B1 before 30 June preceding first enrolment and B2 before 10 December following first enrolment.
_rec.portfolioSpec: Eligibility stage: 'Review of each candidate's project portfolio, CV and covering letter. Candidates will be required to submit 3 personal musical, sound or audiovisual projects demonstrating a degree of originality or creativity, or simply showing a certain level of technical mastery. The projects are free and may take any form: score, recorded music, model, sound recording, sound fiction, soundtrack for images, film music, sound design, video creation, audiovisual music clip, short film, video sequence of filmed music, etc.' Each project must carry an explanatory note on artistic aims, choices, constraints, locations and tools used plus an assessment of the result, stating what the candidate personally implemented — 'This note must be concise and may not under no circumstances exceed 3 pages.' Projects uploaded to the registration platform by midnight on 24 May 2026.
_rec.auditionSpec: Jury pre-selection of applications 4 May 2026; eligibility selection 1 June 2026. Admission tests, all on site: oral test in musical training (16 June 2026); oral test in sciences (17 June 2026); critical listening test on recordings OR comparative analysis test on films/videos/film-repertoire extracts (17 June 2026); interviews in French with the jury on the submitted personal projects and professional experience (18-19 June 2026). Roughly 8 places per year at FSMS level (per Onisep) — UNVERIFIED against the school's own page.

The bachelor requirement explicitly welcomes a non-music degree: 'European bachelor's degree or bachelor's degree from a scientific, technical or audiovisual training course'. A software-engineering BSc satisfies this literally. HOWEVER the same prerequisite block demands 'D.E.M level from a Conservatoire for music' and 'a very good knowledge of music theory, a sound musical culture, a knowledge of composition (harmony and/or counterpoint) and musical analysis', and there is an oral test in musical training. Without conservatoire-level musicianship this is the hard blocker, not the degree.

_rec.fundingLevel: UNVERIFIED (likely low-fee public; no stipend found)
_rec.scholarship: The Conservatoire has a 'Bourses et aides' section (seen in site navigation) but its content was not read — UNVERIFIED. None found specifically for non-EU candidates.
_rec.facilities: 'L'enjeu de cette formation, originale et sans équivalent en France' — trains 'musicien·nes-réalisateur·trices'. Access to the Conservatoire's centre audiovisuel and to the whole musical life of the institution (orchestras, ensembles, jazz and musiques actuelles departments) as recording material. Research partnerships on Audio 3D, spatialisation for live performance, augmented reality and 360 video. Sorbonne Université partnership for a joint musicology licence. Department renamed from 'métiers du son' to 'Musique Son Image'.
_rec.fitNotes: Curriculum-wise this is the closest thing in France to a genuine music-production and mixing master: prise de son classique/jazz/musiques actuelles, mixage musiques actuelles, mastering, design sonore, Audio 3D, plus a production 'Book'. It is also nearly free and has NO age limit. The realistic obstacle is severe: DEM-level music theory, harmony/counterpoint, musical analysis and an oral musical-training test. Without several years of formal music training he will not clear the admission tests, however strong his engineering background. Worth a long-shot application only if he spends 2026 doing serious formation musicale.

_rec.program: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master DIGICREA — Digital Creativity, Art & Science (SOUND-MUSIC specialization path)
_rec.university: Consortium coordinated by Université Jean Monnet Saint-Étienne (France), with Universidade Católica Portuguesa Porto (Portugal) and University of Silesia Katowice/Cieszyn (Poland)
_rec.degree: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master (EMJM) — multiple degrees from the three consortium universities
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters, ending with an internship. Total ECTS not stated on the official pages read (EMJM standard is 120) — CONFIRMED duration, ECTS figure UNVERIFIED.
_rec.focus: Electronic Music / Music Production + Sound Design + digital creation. A dedicated SOUND-MUSIC specialization path exists, distinct from the IMAGE path; candidates apply to one only.
_rec.institutionType: Public university consortium, Erasmus Mundus Joint Master co-funded by the EU
_rec.language: English — the entire programme is taught in English. Certified English test required: minimum B2, C1 recommended (IELTS 6, TOEFL iBT 90+, TOEFL ITP 550, TOEIC 650+; or a university letter confirming a 100% English-taught degree).
_rec.whatYouStudy: Audiovisual new media, emerging technologies in the film industry, music, graphic design, artificial intelligence, virtual/extended reality and their applications. Two specialization paths (SOUND-MUSIC and IMAGE); the Selection Board assesses 'predispositions for professions related to the production of audio-visual and musical forms, including the production of Extended Reality films'. Mobility Saint-Étienne to Porto to Katowice, then an internship with public and private partners. The Saint-Étienne semester shares teaching with the UJM CCNT/RIM programme, which provides a music studio, video studio and multimedia prototyping studio. Detailed module-by-module list is not published — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED: 'A Bachelor's degree of at least 180 ECTS is the minimum requirement to enrol', with NO field restriction stated anywhere on the official pages. Candidates holding at least 150 ECTS at application may apply with a sworn statement that 180 ECTS will be completed before the programme starts. Documents: Europass CV in English; ID/passport; certified copies (with certified English translations) of higher-education and high-school diplomas and complete transcripts showing courses, grades, ECTS and final marks; at least two letters of recommendation in English on official letterhead with referee contacts; a 'Science qualification and experience in New Technology' self-assessment form covering level in mathematics, digital signal processing and computer science, and skills in JavaScript, Python or C, HTML, real-time graphics programming, geometry, trigonometry and algebra; certified English test at B2 minimum (C1 recommended); signed application notice. Applications go through the UJM eCandidat portal, explicitly NOT through Études en France.
_rec.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED and exact: an Artistic or Professional Portfolio presenting productions related to the chosen specialization path. 'All projects included in the portfolio must not be more than 5 years old.' Submit EXACTLY 3 to 5 works or projects (video/audio/images) with metadata — title, short description, public link, and the applicant's role — numbered 1 to 5. For Sound-Music applicants this may be a composition project (orchestral or electronic), a sound design project, a sound concept project, a music piece cycle, a demo, etc. The PDF is capped at 5 MB, so media is supplied via online links. ALSO required in place of a cover letter: a VIDEO PRESENTATION of maximum 2 minutes covering, in order, current situation, motivation for applying, understanding of the programme, why the candidate can succeed, and ideas for applied research and professional development; the link is supplied in a PDF in the 'Motivation letter' field and must stay accessible to the selection board through mid-April.
_rec.auditionSpec: No live audition and no on-site test. Stage I is document review only. Stage II, for shortlisted applicants only, is an ONLINE 15-minute interview (2026 cycle: 24-30 March 2026) assessing personality characteristics, way of thinking, personal life experience and character attributes. Candidates may additionally be asked to join a videoconference to verify English level. No travel is required at any point in the selection.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES — the strongest and clearest case among all six programmes. The only academic requirement published is 'A Bachelor's degree of at least 180 ECTS', with no field restriction. The application actively rewards a software background: a compulsory form asks candidates to self-assess their level in mathematics, digital signal processing and computer science, and specifically in JavaScript, Python or C, HTML, real-time graphics programming, geometry, trigonometric functions and algebra. A software-engineering graduate with a music portfolio is close to the ideal applicant profile.
_rec.applicationOpens: 2027 CYCLE, CONFIRMED ON THE OFFICIAL PAGE: 'The call for applications for the next DIGICREA cohort 2027-2029 is expected to open in November 2026. Further information regarding this procedure will be available in the autumn. Please note that some requirements will differ from those of the 2026 selection process.'
_rec.deadline: 2027-2029 deadline NOT YET PUBLISHED — expected around mid-February 2027, to be confirmed from November 2026. PRIOR CYCLE reference (confirmed on the official page): the 2026-2028 call opened 14 November 2025 and closed 16 February 2026, with Stage II online interviews 24-30 March 2026.
_rec.tuitionIntl: ZERO. Confirmed verbatim on the official financial-aid page: 'Students (scholarship holders and non-scholarship holders) are not charged any tuition fees.' Selected self-funded applicants must supply a 'Guarantee of full financial support' with a budget simulation before enrolment, and document income for the visa.
_rec.fundingLevel: Full — for EMJM scholarship holders this is a genuinely fully funded option, the only one among the six.
_rec.scholarship: CONFIRMED: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master (EMJM) scholarship — €1,400 per month for a total duration of 24 months, maximum €33,600 per student, covering travel, visa, installation and subsistence, paid to the student. A limited number are awarded per cohort. The scholarship application is included within the programme application itself, so there is no separate form. Non-scholarship holders may add Erasmus+ KA131/KA171 mobility funds. Additional support exists for students with long-term physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairments. Tunisian nationality is no barrier — EMJM scholarships are explicitly open to non-EU applicants.
_rec.stipend: €1,400/month for 24 months (€33,600 total) plus zero tuition, for scholarship holders.
_rec.facilities: Three-country mobility with a digital-creation environment at each site. At Saint-Étienne the shared CCNT/RIM teaching gives access to a music studio, video studio, multimedia prototyping studio, sensors, interfaces and sound capture/diffusion equipment. Professionals involved in the shared Saint-Étienne teaching include a sound designer at Ubisoft, a developer at Ableton (Berlin) and Cycling'74, the sound engineer running the studios at Le FIL Saint-Étienne, and researchers from INRIA and GRAME Lyon. Porto and Katowice facility inventories UNVERIFIED.
_rec.fitNotes: The standout recommendation and the only programme here that clears every one of his constraints at once: zero tuition, €1,400/month for two years, taught in English (so IELTS/TOEFL rather than a French DALF C1), a bachelor in ANY field accepted, a Sound-Music specialization, an application form that explicitly credits his programming skills, and a fully remote selection (one 15-minute online interview). The 2027-2029 call is expected to open November 2026 — precisely his window. Two concrete tasks now: build a portfolio of exactly 3-5 numbered works with public links and metadata (a composition, a sound-design project, a demo, a music cycle), and book an English test at B2 minimum, C1 preferred. Caveats: the curriculum is broad digital creativity — AI, XR, graphic design — rather than a dedicated club-music production course, and EMJM scholarships are highly competitive with only a limited number per cohort.
_rec.verificationNotes: Confirmed directly on the official DIGICREA site across three pages: /en/join-digicrea.html, /en/join-digicrea/how-to-apply.html and /en/join-digicrea/financial-aid.html. _rec.qualification: CONFIRMED: Master of Arts (HfK Bremen) or Master of Science (Universität Bremen), 120 ECTS, four semesters full-time. Real, state-recognised second-cycle degrees; the M.Sc. route carries full doctoral progression.
_rec.accreditationStatus: State programme with a published joint Aufnahmeordnung for the hochschulübergreifender Masterstudiengang Digitale Medien. Programme accreditation seal/expiry not shown — STILL UNVERIFIED; check antrag.akkreditierungsrat.de.
_rec.language: CONFIRMED ENGLISH. The official HfK page states the language of instruction is English. This remains the only fully English-taught record of the six, and the only one where he needs no German at all for admission.
_rec.languageRequirement: CONFIRMED EXACTLY AS PREVIOUSLY STATED: C1 CEFR, or TOEFL iBT 95 or higher, or IELTS Band 7, or Cambridge CAE, or US UNIcert III or similar. CONFIRMED WAIVER: the requirement is waived if the qualifying degree or the school education was taught in English, with proof. No German certificate is required for admission. IELTS 7.0 is a demanding band and he must plan a real preparation year — but the waiver is a live possibility worth chasing first.
_rec.durationEcts: CONFIRMED: 4 semesters, 120 ECTS, full-time. Semesters 1-2 introductory and project-preparation courses; semester 3 a full major project; semester 4 the thesis. Start 1 October.
_rec.focus: Digital media at the intersection of media design (HfK) and media informatics (Universität Bremen) — experimental-artistic and applied engagement with new technologies. Sound and audio is a legitimate project area within HfK digital-media practice, but this is NOT a dedicated sound degree: he would have to make sound his own project focus and defend it.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Openly structured and project-driven. The third semester is given over entirely to one major project of the student's own definition — that is where sound design or electronic-music work would live. The open structure is precisely what lets an engineer bend the degree toward audio.
_rec.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED: proof that AT LEAST 150 ECTS have been acquired in the qualifying degree programme, in a relevant field — computer science, design, media arts, fine arts, architecture, systems engineering and related. A BSc Software Engineering fits cleanly, and 150 ECTS is a notably low bar next to TH Köln's 210. This is the single most important structural advantage of this record for him.
_rec.auditionSpec: No audition. A digital interview round applies after shortlisting.
_rec.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED REQUIRED, with the spec differing by route. M.A. (HfK): the guidance states 'a standard number of 10-20 works has proven to be sufficient', spanning artistic, design, academic or professional projects, submitted as PDF, by post, or as a link to a personal website, private upload area or repository. M.Sc. (Universität Bremen): a SINGLE video of no more than 5 minutes demonstrating the breadth of his digital-media work. The 5-minute video route remains the most actionable detail across all six records — it is exactly what one focused year of building can produce. All other documents must be PDF, total upload capped at 50MB with the portfolio exempt.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES — CONFIRMED. No music degree, conservatory training or audio experience required anywhere. Software engineering sits inside the named list of acceptable backgrounds.
_rec.equipmentRequired: None stated.
_rec.facilities: HfK Bremen digital-media studios and workshops plus Universität Bremen media-informatics labs; the joint 'bremen digitalmedia' infrastructure.
_rec.intakes: CONFIRMED: winter semester (start 1 October) for all applicants; summer semester (start 1 April) for advanced entrants only.
_rec.applicationOpens: CONFIRMED: 1 April, both the HfK and the Universität Bremen portals open.
_rec.deadline: CONFIRMED: 31 May, all application portals close. The full published cycle, verified: applications 1 April – 31 May; selection committee review by 15 June; interview invitations 22 June; digital interviews 2-3 July; final results mid-July; programme start 1 October. For a September/October 2027 start he applies 1 April – 31 May 2027 and should expect the same rhythm. VISA WARNING RESTATED: a mid-July decision leaves roughly ten weeks to obtain a Tunis student visa against a German processing norm of about three months. He must book the embassy appointment the day he is offered, and should pre-open the blocked account before results.
_rec.tuitionEU: No tuition fee; semester contribution EUR 431.40. CONFIRMED.
_rec.tuitionNonEU: CONFIRMED IDENTICAL — EUR 431.40 per semester. No separate non-EU rate is published and Bremen does not charge non-EU tuition.
_rec.otherFees: The EUR 431.40 is the whole published semester cost and includes the semester ticket. Postal portfolio submission and certified translations of non-German/non-English documents are at his own cost. IELTS fee if the waiver does not apply.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: About EUR 862.80 per year in semester contributions, plus Bremen living costs (moderate by German standards), plus the blocked account required for the visa, plus the IELTS fee. No tuition, no application fee published.
_rec.scholarships: None programme-specific published. DAAD / Deutschlandstipendium only. STILL UNVERIFIED — ask the HfK International Office.
_rec.englishTest: IELTS 7.0 / TOEFL iBT 95 / CEFR C1. Waiver only if his SMU MedTech degree or his school education was taught in English AND he can prove it. Worth pursuing hard, because SMU MedTech teaches substantially in English and a medium-of-instruction letter could remove this gate outright — unlike at Ilmenau, this waiver is written into the published requirements rather than restricted to native-English countries.
_rec.visaEligible: YES. Full-time state degree at two state institutions.
_rec.recommendation: This record survived verification with ZERO corrections — every figure, date and requirement checked out exactly, which is not true of any other entry here. It is the best-documented and most accessible option of the six for him: English-taught with no German required at all, a 150-ECTS entry bar his BSc clears comfortably, software engineering explicitly named as an acceptable background, EUR 431.40 a semester and nothing more, no audition, and an M.Sc. route whose entire portfolio requirement is a 5-minute video. Three action items, in order: (1) request a medium-of-instruction letter from SMU MedTech immediately and send it to the HfK International Office asking in writing whether it waives the IELTS 7 requirement — this single email could remove his largest obstacle; (2) if it does not, book a diagnostic IELTS now, because Band 7 from 'working English' is a genuine year of work; (3) start building the 5-minute video around sound and music-technology projects so that his portfolio year, his application and his career goal all point the same direction. Apply to both the M.Sc. and M.A. routes if permitted — the M.Sc. video is easier to produce than 10-20 finished works. Second official source for application detail: https://www.hfk-bremen.de/en/application/bewerbung-im-digitale-medien-m-a/3

_rec.city: Rome (via Baccina 47 main site; also via Urbana, via Boschetto, via Cimarra; a Milan operational site exists)
_rec.institutionType: Private AFAM higher music-education institution authorised by the Italian MUR. Footer states it is "La prima Istituzione di Alta Formazione Artistica Musicale in Italia autorizzata dal Ministero dell'Università e della Ricerca al rilascio di diplomi accademici di I e II livello, equivalenti a laurea magistrale specialistica". Legal entity: Saint Louis Music Center srl.
_rec.degree: Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello (master-equivalent, MUR-recognised)
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 CFA — NOW VERIFIED from the official Piano di studi PDF (Year 1 = 60 CFA: Tecnologie e tecniche della ripresa e registrazione 1 (6) + Analisi compositiva (8) + Composizione musicale elettroacustica I (22) + Storia delle tecnologie elettroacustiche (8) + Tecniche compositive pop rock I (10) + Materie elettive (6); Year 2 = 60 CFA: Ripresa e registrazione II (6) + Forme, sistemi e linguaggi musicali (8) + Composizione musicale elettroacustica II (22) + Diritto d'autore e royalties (5) + Tecniche compositive pop rock II (10) + Tesi e prova finale (9)). Teaching is fortnightly, concentrated in two consecutive days, approx. 300 contact hours per year.
_rec.language: Course page states "Lingua: Italiano e Inglese". The official international-students page goes further: "Tutti i Corsi al Saint Louis sono offerti in lingua inglese o in lingua italiana, in base alla preferenza dello studente" — Italian is explicitly NOT a prerequisite, A2 is recommended, and a weekly Italian course is included in the ordinary fees. His French/English/Arabic profile is workable here.
_rec.focus: Music Production — the closest thing in this slice to a producer's degree. Note the formal home department is Musica Elettronica e Nuove Tecnologie, so the study plan is weighted toward electroacoustic composition alongside the production craft.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Verified against BOTH the course page and the official Piano di studi PDF, and they differ in emphasis — read the PDF, not the marketing copy. Marketing prose: managing a music-production project through every phase, from creative idea to arrangement with real and virtual instruments, recording, mixing and mastering. The actual credit-weighted plan is: COMPOSIZIONE MUSICALE ELETTROACUSTICA I and II — 22 CFA each, by far the largest component; TECNOLOGIE E TECNICHE DELLA RIPRESA E DELLA REGISTRAZIONE 1 and II (6 CFA each) — the Music Producer specialisation strand, in which "ciascuno specializzando produrra' sotto la guida del docente due brani", taking two tracks from songwriting and pre-production (key, bpm, groove, feel, style) through arrangement with real and virtual instruments, rehearsals, recording and overdubbing in both a home and a commercial studio, microphone choice and placement, monitoring, executive production, mix and mastering, for himself and for third parties; TECNICHE COMPOSITIVE POP ROCK I and II (10 CFA each); ANALISI COMPOSITIVA (8) and FORME, SISTEMI E LINGUAGGI MUSICALI (8); STORIA DELLE TECNOLOGIE ELETTROACUSTICHE (8); DIRITTO D'AUTORE E ROYALTIES (5) covering copyright, royalties, licence, publishing, production and performance contracts; 6 CFA of free electives usable across any department; 9 CFA thesis and final work. The bienni are "costruiti intorno alle inclinazioni artistiche di ciascuno studente", with original productions and third-party commissioned work running through the degree.
_rec.entryRequirements: TWO different statements exist and the international one is the one that governs his case. Course page: "Diploma accademico triennale di primo livello già conseguito o da conseguirsi entro la sessione di Febbraio (iscrizione con riserva)". Official international-students page: "Accademici di II Livello: possono richiedere l'ammissione Cittadini UE o NON-UE in possesso del Diploma di Triennio universitario o accademico (o equivalente), ottenuto in Italia o nel proprio Paese di provenienza. È inoltre necessario dimostrare di avere un minimo di 15 anni di scolarizzazione." Degree must be submitted as a scanned original plus certified translation plus DOV (Dichiarazione di Valore) from the Italian embassy/consulate, or alternatively a CIMEA Diplome certificate. Attendance minimum 80% of classes; a part-time route exists. Erasmus+ mobility up to 12 months within the biennio. Non-EU applicants must ALSO run the parallel Universitaly pre-enrolment through the Italian diplomatic mission in Tunisia, which normally closes in July with no extensions; Saint Louis advises starting it no later than January/February.
_rec.portfolioSpec: CORRECTED — the prior record's "3 pieces in a group of at least a trio" brief does NOT apply to him. That wording belongs to the performer accordions (Jazz, Composizione Jazz, Pop). The accordion that actually covers this course — "SONGWRITING + FILM TV SCORING + MUSICA APPLICATA + LIVE ELECTRONICS + MUSIC PRODUCTION + MIX E MASTERING" — omits the videoclip step entirely. And the official international-students page gives the applicable brief verbatim: "Composizione/Musica Elettronica/Musica Applicata: Prepara un link contenente il Portfolio (video, audio, spartiti) dei tuoi lavori più indicativi e recenti." So: a single link to a portfolio of his most representative and recent works (video, audio, scores). No number of works, no duration, no format prescribed.
_rec.auditionSpec: NO performance audition. The official Piano di studi publishes the exact test: "PROVA DI AMMISSIONE — 1) colloquio individuale; 2) test a risposte multiple su argomenti di tecnologia musicale: fondamenti di audio digitale, sintesi sonora, protocollo MIDI; 3) clausura di 5 ore in cui gli allievi dovranno produrre un brano in due versioni diverse senza vincoli stilistici, a partire da una traccia vocale che verrà fornita loro." That third element is a supervised FIVE-HOUR production test: build a track in two different versions, any style, from a supplied vocal. CRUCIAL for him: the international-students page states that for international candidates the admission tests "potranno essere sostenute online tra Gennaio e Giugno, in date da concordare individualmente" — online, individually scheduled, January to June; only if he chooses to sit them in person is there a single June session. Numero chiuso: maximum 20 students per academic year, from Saint Louis's own first-level courses or selected by audition among external candidates.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES — RESOLVED, and this is the biggest correction to the prior record. The official international-students page states that admission to II livello is open to EU or NON-EU citizens holding a "Diploma di Triennio universitario o accademico (o equivalente)" obtained in Italy or in their home country, with a minimum of 15 years of schooling. A university bachelor is therefore explicitly acceptable — no Italian first-level music diploma is required of an international applicant. What he must supply is the DOV or CIMEA certificate. Residual risk: "Gli studenti la cui preparazione in entrata NON sia RITENUTA IDONEA all'ingresso diretto ai Corsi di livello Accademico, potranno accedere ai Corsi di livello pre-accademico" — if the commission judges his musical preparation inadequate he can be routed to a pre-accademico year instead.
_rec.tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED — genuinely not published. The site publishes no tuition schedule for academic courses anywhere (no fee page exists in the sitemap). Confirmed and published: registration fee €240–290 depending on the month of enrolment, plus a €250 down payment deducted from the annual fee; the admission process itself is free but the registration fee is non-refundable. The commonly cited "~€2,800/year" figure is NOT on the official site — do not rely on it. Request a written preventivo from the Segreteria Didattica. Fees are ISEE-linked for scholarship purposes, which matters below.
_rec.scholarship: Saint Louis borse di studio (partial exonerations), Borse di collaborazione, LAZIODISCO regional right-to-study grants, Banca Sella student financing. NOT applicable to him: the Giorgia Mileto award, which is restricted to instrument and voice courses in the Jazz and Popular Music departments and is decided by a live audition in a Rome club.
_rec.fundingLevel: Partial — self-pay baseline with income-and-merit-based reductions and a possible regional grant. No full-ride route found.
_rec.stipend: No stipend. Saint Louis's own scholarships are partial exonerations worth €500–2,500 per year of full-time study, conditional on BOTH an ISEE below €22,000 AND, for students who did not come through Saint Louis's pre-accademici, an admission-test average of at least 26/30 (penalty of 1 point per outstanding subject). Applications run 2–31 July each year. Borse di collaborazione are worth €1,095 each for up to 150 hours of work per year. LAZIODISCO is compatible and can be held simultaneously. PRACTICAL WARNING: the ISEE threshold requires an ISEE parificato, which a Tunisian family must obtain through an Italian CAF — build time for this.
_rec.applicationOpens: 1 January for international applicants ("Le domande di ammissione ai corsi accademici, che devono essere inviate complete dei link per la pre-selezione, vengono accettate ogni anno a partire dal 1° gennaio"). The generic Italian course page instead says 3 February. Both are standing annual rules rather than a dated cycle, but confirm the 2027 edition.
_rec.deadline: 30 April (standing annual rule: "dal 3 febbraio al 30 aprile" on the course page; "a partire dal 1° gennaio, entro e non oltre il 30 APRILE" on the international page). Late applications considered only against remaining places. In-person admission tests in June and September; online tests for internationals January–June. PRIOR CYCLE — these are published standing dates, not a 2027-specific calendar; confirm the 2027/28 edition, and note the separate Universitaly pre-enrolment deadline of roughly July 2027 set by the Italian ministry.
_rec.facilities: Rome campus across four sites plus a Milan site. Resident bands and permanent ensembles gigging in Rome clubs year-round, plus a large formation doing theatre concerts and record productions with international guests — recent named guests include Aaron Parks, Gegè Telesforo, Greg Hutchinson, Roberto Gatto, Vince Mendoza, Paolo Fresu, Fabrizio Bosso, Gianluca Petrella, Javier Girotto. Note the "Synth Louis" ensemble, an experimental group dedicated to electronic music, synthesisers and electronic instruments, open to electronic musicians. Erasmus+ partner since 2012 with up to 12 months of mobility per cycle. A dedicated International Office with a named Head of International Admissions (Marzia Bagli) and a per-department tutor for Musica Elettronica e Applicata (Sergio Bachelet). UNVERIFIED: studio, console and immersive-room inventory.
_rec.fitNotes: Re-rated upward after verification. Three things the prior record got wrong in his favour: his BSc is explicitly accepted for a non-EU applicant, his portfolio is simply a link to his own audio/video works rather than a live-trio video, and the admission tests can be taken online from Tunis between January and June. Courses can be delivered in English. What remains genuinely hard: (1) tuition is not published anywhere, so this is an unpriced fee-paying route until he gets a written quote; (2) the scholarship route runs through ISEE, which is awkward from Tunisia; (3) the admission test includes a five-hour supervised production task — building a track in two versions from a supplied vocal — which he cannot pass on theory alone and must train for over the coming year; (4) the credit-weighted study plan is dominated by electroacoustic composition (44 of 120 CFA), so this is less of a pure record-production degree than the landing page implies. Still the strongest craft-and-production match in this slice.
_rec.verificationNotes: The live site is behind a SiteGround proof-of-work bot challenge; the challenge was solved programmatically and the genuine live pages were read in full (not archived copies). Confirmed directly on saintlouis.eu: course exists at II livello, Rome, 2 years, fortnightly two-day blocks, ~300 h/year, "Lingua: Italiano e Inglese", numero chiuso of 20, entry-title wording, application window 3 Feb–30 Apr, admission tests in June and September over two consecutive days, 80% attendance, part-time route, Erasmus+. Additionally verified from the official Piano di studi PDF (linked from the course page): ministerial code DCSL34 Musica Elettronica indirizzo Music Production, the full 120-CFA subject list, and the exact three-part admission test including the five-hour production clausura. Additionally verified from https://saintlouis.eu/studenti-internazionali/ : non-EU entry title (university triennio + 15 years schooling), DOV/CIMEA requirement, the Composizione/Musica Elettronica portfolio brief, online admission tests January–June for internationals, 1 January–30 April window, €240–290 registration + €250 deposit, Universitaly pre-enrolment, Italian not a prerequisite. Additionally verified from https://saintlouis.eu/borse-di-studio/ : scholarship values, ISEE and merit criteria, 2–31 July window, LAZIODISCO compatibility, collaboration grants. COULD NOT VERIFY: annual tuition (no fee page exists on the site or in its sitemap); the CFA total for the second year's thesis line was read from the PDF and is included above; 2027-cycle dates are not yet published.

_rec.university: Saint Louis College of Music
_rec.institutionType: Private AFAM higher music-education institution authorised by the Italian MUR to award first- and second-level academic diplomas equivalent to an Italian laurea magistrale specialistica
_rec.degree: Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello in Sound Design (MUR-recognised)
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years; fortnightly teaching in two consecutive days, approx. 300 contact hours per year. Year 1 = 60 CFA VERIFIED from the official Piano di studi (Storia del Sound Design e della post produzione audio I 6 + Sound Design I 20 + Audio Interattivo non Lineare Wwise I 8 + Tecnologie e tecniche del Restauro I 8 + Tecnologie e tecniche della ripresa e della registrazione audio I 12 + Materie elettive 6). Year 2 lists Restauro II 6 + Sound Design II 20 + Campionamento e post produzione Audio 8 + Wwise II 8 + Ripresa e registrazione II 12 + Materie elettive 3 = 57 CFA in the readable extract; the thesis/final-work line did not render, so the 120 CFA total is inferred rather than fully read.
_rec.language: "Lingua: Italiano e Inglese" on the course page; the international-students page confirms all Saint Louis courses are delivered in English or Italian according to student preference, Italian is not an entry prerequisite, A2 is recommended, and a weekly Italian course is included in the fees.
_rec.focus: Sound Design; Film, TV series, gaming, animation, media and advertising post-production; interactive game audio; audio restoration and forensic audio
_rec.whatYouStudy: Verified against the course page and the official Piano di studi. SOUND DESIGN I–II (20 CFA each, the largest block): creating, recording and manipulating sound effects — ambiences, specials, Foley, organic and artificial effects — plus the Pro Tools post-production workflow (session setup, AAF/OMF interchange, working to picture, video export, timecode and frame-rate sync), the aesthetics of sound design (analysing a film's sound requirements, sound design in trailers, the relationship between effects and music in modern cinematic language) and hardware technique (microphones, portable recorders). AUDIO INTERATTIVO NON LINEARE WWISE I–II (8 CFA each): non-linear game audio through Audiokinetic Wwise, covering the full 101 syllabus plus advanced material — navigating the Wwise environment, building an implementation to spec, events, spatialisation, non-linear mixing and integration into the game engine. CAMPIONAMENTO E POST PRODUZIONE AUDIO (8): sampling and building custom sound libraries — instruments, modulators, envelopes, mapping, digital sound management. TECNOLOGIE E TECNICHE DEL RESTAURO I–II (8 + 6): audio restoration and remastering, from digitising historic material to recovery and treatment in specialised labs. TECNOLOGIE E TECNICHE DELLA RIPRESA E DELLA REGISTRAZIONE AUDIO I–II (12 each). STORIA DEL SOUND DESIGN E DELLA POST PRODUZIONE AUDIO. Original projects with Saint Louis's Composizione and Musica Applicata alle Immagini departments and with RUFA (Rome University of Fine Arts) and Vigamus.
_rec.entryRequirements: Course page: "Diploma accademico triennale di primo livello già conseguito o da conseguirsi entro la sessione di Febbraio (iscrizione con riserva)". Governing rule for him, from the official international-students page: EU or NON-EU citizens holding a "Diploma di Triennio universitario o accademico (o equivalente)" plus a minimum of 15 years of schooling, evidenced by scanned original degree + certified translation + DOV from the Italian embassy, or a CIMEA Diplome certificate. 80% minimum attendance; part-time route available; Erasmus+ up to 12 months. Non-EU applicants must also complete Universitaly pre-enrolment through the Italian mission in Tunisia, normally closing in July.
_rec.portfolioSpec: NONE — RESOLVED, and this reverses the prior record's UNVERIFIED. The official international-students page states plainly: "Per il Corso di Tecnico del Suono non è prevista pre-selezione ma un colloquio attitudinale." This course IS Tecnico del Suono (DCSL61). There is no pre-selection stage and no portfolio to submit — only an aptitude interview. The ensemble-video wording elsewhere on the page belongs to the Jazz/Pop/Songwriting/Classical performer tracks and does not apply.
_rec.auditionSpec: NO audition and no practical production test. The official Piano di studi publishes the exact test: "PROVA DI AMMISSIONE — 1) Colloquio attitudinale; 2) Test scritto a risposte multiple incentrato sui seguenti argomenti: Fondamenti di audio digitale, Pro Tools, Riprese microfoniche, Protocollo MIDI." That is the whole thing: an aptitude interview plus a written multiple-choice test on digital audio fundamentals, Pro Tools, microphone technique and MIDI. For international candidates these tests can be sat ONLINE between January and June on individually agreed dates; an in-person route exists as a single June session. Numero chiuso: maximum 20 students per academic year.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES for a non-EU applicant — the international-students page accepts a university triennio (or equivalent) with 15 years of schooling, with no requirement for an Italian first-level music diploma. This is also the most natural of the two Saint Louis routes for an engineer: the feeder programmes are the first-level diplomas in Tecnico del Suono and Musica Elettronica, the entrance test is a technical multiple-choice paper rather than a musical performance, and the Wwise/game-engine strand rewards a software background directly. Residual risk unchanged: a candidate judged unprepared can be routed to a pre-accademico year.
_rec.tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED — no tuition schedule is published on saintlouis.eu for academic courses. Published and confirmed: registration fee €240–290 depending on month of enrolment, plus a €250 down payment credited against the annual fee; the admission process is otherwise free and the registration fee is non-refundable. Request a written preventivo from the Segreteria Didattica.
_rec.scholarship: Saint Louis borse di studio (partial exonerations of €500–2,500 per year), Borse di collaborazione (€1,095 for up to 150 hours per year), LAZIODISCO regional grants (compatible and holdable simultaneously), Banca Sella student financing. The Giorgia Mileto award does not apply — it is restricted to Jazz and Popular Music instrument and voice courses.

_rec.stipend: No stipend. Saint Louis exonerations require BOTH an ISEE below €22,000 AND an admission-test average of at least 26/30 for candidates not coming from its own pre-accademici; applications 2–31 July. _rec.facilities: Pro Tools-based post-production teaching, Audiokinetic Wwise for interactive game audio, dedicated audio-restoration labs handling digitisation of historic material, cross-departmental projects with Composizione and Musica Applicata alle Immagini, and partnerships with RUFA and Vigamus. Erasmus+ network since 2012 with up to 12 months of mobility. Dedicated international tutor for Tecnico del Suono (Davide Prestanicola). Rome campus across four sites plus Milan. _rec.fitNotes: After verification this is the single most ATTAINABLE programme in the slice for him: no portfolio at all, no audition, no performance requirement, an admission test that is an interview plus a multiple-choice paper on digital audio, Pro Tools, mic technique and MIDI — all sittable online from Tunis — and a non-EU entry rule that explicitly accepts his university bachelor. The Wwise and game-engine strand converts his software-engineering background into an immediate advantage. Two honest caveats. First, this is post-production for picture and games, not electronic music production — it will make him employable as a sound designer and give him a paying craft, but it will not by itself make him a producer or a DJ; the sister Music Production biennio is the better fit for the stated goal, and this one is the better fit for the bank balance. Second, tuition is unpublished and the scholarship route runs through ISEE, so treat it as an unpriced fee-paying route until the Segreteria gives him a written quote. Best used as the low-risk Italian application alongside a craft-focused first choice.

_rec.whatYouStudy: Three years covering physical acoustics, sound technologies and practices, and the aesthetics of artistic projects, training students for 'des postes de régie, d'ingénierie ou de création, seul ou en encadrement d'équipe', becoming 'l'interlocuteur privilégié dans son domaine qui guide techniquement et artistiquement la mise en scène'. _rec.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED from the official fiche concours. Age: minimum 18 at 1 September of the entry year, 'sans dérogation possible' and, per the concours page, 'sans limite d'âge maximum'. Diplomas: 'Etre titulaires du baccalauréat ou d'une équivalence' AND 'Justifier d'au moins 2 années d'études supérieures et être détenteurs de 120 crédits ECTS … délivrés dans le cadre d'une formation reconnue par l'Etat'. Foreign nationals outside the francophone list must supply their most recent diploma translated into French by a sworn translator (or a plurilingual version) plus DALF C1 or equivalent. 'Aucune demande de dérogation ne sera possible.' Connaissances souhaitées: 'Mathématiques, Physique : niveau minimum requis BAC + 1 scientifique' — published syllabus covers integral calculus, linear ODEs of 1st and 2nd order, complex numbers and De Moivre, log/exp/power functions, Taylor expansions, derivatives, binary arithmetic and 'Notion de programmation algorithmique'; physics covers electricity and electromagnetism (Ohm, Kirchhoff, superposition, Thévenin/Norton, capacitors, Laplace, Faraday, Lenz, impedance/admittance), mechanics, damped and forced oscillators, resonance, bandwidth, Q factor, and travelling/standing waves with interference. Also: writing ability; broad general, literary, contemporary-art (photo, plastic arts, cinema, music) and theatre culture; ability to work collectively; 'Toute expérience vécue en milieu professionnel, au sens large, est souhaitée'. Three recommended books: Daniel Deshays 'Pour une écriture du son'; Larrue & Mervant-Roux 'Le son du théâtre XIXe-XXIe siècle'; Yann Paranthoën 'Propos d'un tailleur de sons'. A candidature-review commission decides who is authorised to compete at all.

_rec.program: Interface Cultures — Master Programme (MA)
_rec.institution: Universität für künstlerische und industrielle Gestaltung Linz (Kunstuniversität Linz / University of Arts Linz)
_rec.institutionType: Public federal art university (Kunstuniversität) under the Austrian Universitätsgesetz 2002
_rec.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. How I know: the university's own tuition-fee page states the fee amount is set by 'the 2002 Universities Act' (Universitätsgesetz 2002), the federal statute that governs Austria's 22 state universities, and it levies the statutory federal rates (EUR 363.36 / 726.72) rather than a market price. It is federally funded via the BMBWF. Not a Privatuniversität.
_rec.accreditationStatus: Real, state-recognised second-cycle degree. Kunstuniversität Linz is a federal public university established by law; its Masterstudien are ordentliche Studien under UG 2002 and award a Master of Arts. Admission as an ordentliche/r Studierende/r in a degree programme is the basis for an Aufenthaltsbewilligung – Studierende under §64 NAG, so it supports a student residence permit for a Tunisian national.
_rec.qualification: Master of Arts (MA) — a genuine second-cycle degree, not a certificate or 'Lehrgang'. Kunstuni Linz's own Study & Admission page confirms 'Master's Programme — Duration: 4 semesters'.
_rec.focus: Media art / digital art, interactive art, interface design, participatory practice at the art–technology–research intersection. Sound is present as a medium inside interactive/installation work, but this is NOT a music-production or audio-engineering degree.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Artistic and scientific development of interactive media; human–machine, human–human and machine–machine interaction; critical data, sustainable IT and the environmental politics of digitalisation; conceptual and practical prototype development. Strong link to Ars Electronica (Linz), which is the single biggest reason this department matters for a portfolio-builder.
_rec.durationEcts: 4 semesters. Kunstuni Linz's Study & Admission page states master's duration = 4 semesters; the standard Austrian equivalent is 120 ECTS, but the exact ECTS figure is not published on the Interface Cultures pages — UNVERIFIED, ask interfacecultures@kunstuni-linz.at.
_rec.language: ENGLISH. The official programme text states: 'The master program is fully held in English language.' This is one of the few fully English-taught art-university masters in Austria.
_rec.languageRequirement: No specific IELTS/TOEFL band is published on the Interface Cultures pages — UNVERIFIED. The comparable Kunstuni Linz master (Timebased Media) publishes 'English: Level B2 proficiency required before program start if completing coursework in English' and 'German: Level B1 by third-semester enrolment'. Ask the Student Service Center (international.office@kunstuni-linz.at) whether an IELTS/TOEFL certificate is demanded for Interface Cultures or whether a self-declared B2 / interview in English suffices. This matters for him because he has not sat IELTS.
_rec.entryRequirements: 'To study at Interface Cultures you need a valid bachelor (or equivalent) degree to qualify for admission.' Application materials: copy of degree, motivation letter, CV, and a portfolio of works. Plus the departmental entrance exam — Kunstuni Linz's Study & Admission page: 'To be admitted to a Master's programme, applicants need a compatible Bachelor's certificate and have to pass the entrance exam of the department.' Note: no music degree is required and no conservatory training is required. A BSc in Software Engineering is a plausible, even attractive, base here — the department explicitly wants people who can build things.
_rec.portfolioSpec: Portfolio of own works + letter of motivation + CV, submitted online. The sister programme's procedure (same admissions machinery) is: online registration → portfolio + motivation letter upload → ~30-minute admission interview including 'a ten-minute presentation of selected work samples' → result by email/PIN. Exact Interface Cultures portfolio format/file limits are not published — UNVERIFIED, ask interfacecultures@kunstuni-linz.at.
_rec.auditionSpec: No musical audition. An admission interview with work presentation, not a performance audition. This is a significant advantage for a candidate with no conservatory background.
_rec.equipmentRequired: None stated. Department provides shared kit.
_rec.facilities: Two dedicated computer rooms, a production workshop, a rapid-prototyping lab (3D printers, soldering stations, laser cutters), and shared equipment including MIDI controllers, cameras, speakers, projectors and VR headsets. Note the MIDI controllers and speakers — usable for sound work, but there is no published professional studio/control-room or spatial-audio rig here.
_rec.intakes: Winter semester (September/October) start only, as far as published.
_rec.applicationOpens: Around mid-March. For the 2026/27 cycle the parallel Kunstuni Linz master opened online registration on 18 March 2026. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Interface-Cultures-specific opening date UNVERIFIED — ask interfacecultures@kunstuni-linz.at.
_rec.deadline: UNVERIFIED for Interface Cultures specifically. The comparable Kunstuni Linz master (Timebased Media) ran: online registration 18 March – 7 June 2026, portfolio due 7 June 2026, interviews 30 June – 1 July 2026 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. CRITICAL PLANNING POINT: this is a SPRING deadline (March–June), not the October–February window he is planning around. For a September 2027 start he must be ready to submit a portfolio by roughly June 2027, and register from about March 2027.
_rec.tuitionEU: EUR 363.36 per semester (EU/EEA nationals are exempt during the standard duration plus a two-semester grace period; Austrians exempt).
_rec.tuitionNonEU: EUR 726.72 PER SEMESTER — this is the rate he would pay as a Tunisian national. Quoted directly on the Interface Cultures page ('non-EU-citizens currently have to pay a fee of 726,72 € per semester') and on the university's tuition-fee page. That is EUR 1,453.44 per academic year, EUR 2,906.88 for the whole 4-semester degree. By European standards this is very cheap. Note: Kunstuni Linz states a reduction to the EU rate can be requested in some 'close relationship to Austria' cases — not applicable to a first-time arrival.
_rec.otherFees: Austrian National Union of Students (ÖH) fee including insurance: EUR 24.70 per semester as quoted on the Kunstuni Linz page. The ÖH fee is indexed and rises most years (other Austrian institutions already quote EUR 25.20 / 26.20) — treat 24.70 as a floor and confirm at enrolment. Payment must be made in full within the admission period or admission is refused; partial payment is not accepted.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Tuition + ÖH over 2 years: approx. EUR 2,996. Living costs in Linz are the real expense and are NOT published by the university — budget separately. For the Austrian student visa he must additionally prove sufficient means to the immigration authority (a fixed monthly figure set annually by the ASVG — UNVERIFIED here, confirm with the Austrian embassy/OeAD).
_rec.scholarships: None attached to this programme. Kunstuni Linz publishes no programme scholarship for non-EU master applicants. Realistic external routes for a Tunisian: OeAD-administered Austrian government scholarships (Ernst Mach Grant is aimed mainly at short research stays, not full masters) and the Ernst Mach Grant – worldwide. Nothing verified as covering a full Kunstuni Linz master — treat as UNVERIFIED and ask OeAD (grants.at) directly.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes. Admission to an ordentliches Masterstudium at an Austrian public university is the standard basis for the Aufenthaltsbewilligung – Studierende (§64 NAG). He must apply at the Austrian representation in Tunis before travelling.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES — explicitly. Requirement is 'a valid bachelor (or equivalent) degree', not a music or art degree. A Software Engineering BSc plus a strong interactive/sound portfolio is a coherent application here.
_rec.recommendation: ONE OF THE TWO BEST FITS FOUND IN THIS ENTIRE SLICE, but with an honest caveat. In its favour: fully English-taught (removes the German wall that kills almost every other Austrian and Swiss option for him); EUR 726.72/semester is among the cheapest real master's degrees in Western Europe; no music degree, no conservatory training and no audition required; the entry gate is a portfolio he can genuinely build in a year as a software engineer (interactive sound objects, generative audio, installations, Max/MSP or SuperCollider work, web-audio pieces); the Ars Electronica connection is a real career asset. Against it: this is media art, not music production — it will not train him as a DJ or a record producer, and there is no published pro studio. He should treat it as a route into sound art and creative technology, not into the club/label industry. ACTION: (1) email interfacecultures@kunstuni-linz.at NOW to get the 2027 registration window, the exact portfolio spec and whether an English certificate is required, because the deadline is in SPRING, several months earlier than the Oct–Feb window he has assumed; (2) build 4–6 interactive sound works over the coming year, documented on video.

Teaching is shared between the Arts plastiques and Musicologie departments — described by the university as unique in France — with contributions from many internationally recognised professionals. Max/MSP appears in module descriptions. Dedicated equipment and production spaces are provided across both years: computers, sensors, interfaces, image-capture, sound-capture and diffusion tools, plus a 'studio musical', a 'studio de prise de vue' and a 'studio de maquettage de dispositifs multimédia'. Placements in both M1 and M2. Named RIM career outcomes include work in music production centres, recording studios, theatre, dance, video games and sound design; the wider list includes designer sonore, professeur de MAO, développeur en informatique musicale, and roles at IRCAM, GRM and Centres Nationaux de Création Musicale.
_rec.entryRequirements: The official university page confirms the entry level is M1 (start of the programme) but does NOT publish the admission criteria — the livret states only 'CONDITIONS D'ADMISSION — Se référer aux portails monmaster ou ecandidat.' The older RIM-specific documentation (for the M2 route) states entry for holders of a 'Master I en musique, en arts numériques, ou équivalents', or any Master 1 with a demonstrated strong level in musical or digital-arts practice, and expects 'une culture scientifique et une expérience en informatique musicale et/ou en programmation dans le champ des arts numériques'; professionals may enter via VAE. Cohort reported at a maximum of 20 students — UNVERIFIED on the current official page. Programme directors: Laurent Pottier (RIM, laurent.pottier@univ-st-etienne.fr) and Vincent Ciciliato (Arts numériques). Faculty ALL: 04 77 42 13 05.
_rec.portfolioSpec: NOT PUBLISHED for M1 entry. For M1 via monmaster the required documents will appear in the mention's 'critères d'examen des candidatures' when the 2027 campaign opens — UNVERIFIED until then. For the M2 RIM route the documented requirement is a dossier from the secretariat or the university site submitted via eCandidat, plus an 'audio commentary' exercise for RIM candidates (an analysis of a musical work) demonstrating artistic/musical competence. He should email laurent.pottier@univ-st-etienne.fr directly to ask what an M1 applicant must submit.
_rec.auditionSpec: No instrumental audition. For the M2 RIM route: an interview with a jury of professionals assessing motivation and career project, plus the audio-commentary exercise. For M1 entry via monmaster the selection method is UNVERIFIED. The only dates ever published for the RIM exam route are from a 2018 cycle (application 31 May, admission exams 8 June) — PRIOR CYCLE, long superseded, do not rely on these.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: CHECK — leaning favourable but not proven for M1. Substantively the profile sought is scientific: the RIM documentation asks for 'une culture scientifique et une expérience en informatique musicale et/ou en programmation dans le champ des arts numériques', and accepts 'des étudiants issus d'autres formations ... pouvant justifier d'un bon niveau en pratique musicale et/ou artistique numérique'. So a computer-science background is welcome in principle. What is NOT published anywhere official is the M1 admission criterion — the university page confirms M1 is an entry point but defers entirely to monmaster. He must confirm with the programme director whether a Tunisian BSc in software engineering with a self-built music portfolio is an acceptable M1 dossier.
_rec.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. M1 applications go through monmaster.gouv.fr on the national calendar, which typically opens in late February; M2 applications go through UJM eCandidat. No 2027 dates are published. Monitor monmaster.gouv.fr from January 2027.
_rec.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. No current deadline is published for this programme. The national monmaster M1 window for the 2026-2027 cycle ran roughly late February to late March 2026; the 2027-2028 window will follow the national calendar published in winter 2026-2027. The only programme-specific dates ever found are from a 2018 cycle and must not be used.
_rec.tuitionIntl: CORRECTED — the earlier claim of a near-automatic reduction to about €255 is no longer safe. UJM publishes the non-EU differentiated master fee for 2026-2027 as €3,950/yr. UJM's conseil d'administration decided on 8 September 2025 to apply an automatic partial exemption from differentiated fees for international-mobility students enrolled in a UJM national master's diploma; however the €255 reduced figure on that page is explicitly tied to students already enrolled at UJM in 2023-2024 continuing in the same programme, not to new entrants. Crucially, décret n° 2026-385 of 19 May 2026 abolished blanket institutional exemptions and caps discretionary exemptions at 30% of affected students in 2026-2027, 25% in 2027-2028 and 20% from 2028 — so a September 2027 entrant faces a 25% cap. Plan for €3,950/yr plus CVEC (~€105) and treat any reduction as a bonus. Confirm the 2027-2028 UJM policy in spring 2027.
_rec.fundingLevel: Partial at best, and now uncertain — no programme stipend, and the fee exemption that previously looked near-automatic is capped and discretionary after décret 2026-385.
_rec.scholarship: No programme-specific scholarship found. Two realistic routes: (1) the EMJM DIGICREA at the SAME university, whose €1,400/month scholarship is the funded alternative — apply to both; (2) France Excellence Eiffel, which is nominated BY the institution, pays €1,181/month at master level and carries an age limit of 25 for master candidates. Eiffel internal institutional deadlines for the 2026-2027 cycle fell in October-December 2025 with the Campus France national deadline in early January 2026, so for a September 2027 start he must contact UJM about Eiffel nomination by roughly October 2026. Campus France Tunisie and French Embassy bourses are the other vehicles. UNVERIFIED whether UJM nominates for Eiffel in the Arts mention.
_rec.facilities: CONFIRMED on the official page: a dedicated music studio, a video/filming studio and a multimedia prototyping studio, plus computers, sensors, interfaces and capture/diffusion tools available across both years. Teaching staff reported to include Pierre Colomies (sound designer, Ubisoft Montpellier), Emmanuel Jourdan (Ableton Berlin and Cycling'74), Christophe Lebreton (LISILOG), Stéphane Letz (GRAME Lyon), Romain Michon (INRIA), Jérémy Lhuillier (head of studios at Le FIL Saint-Étienne), Michele Tadini (CNSMD Lyon) and Michel Pascal (CNRR Nice) — staff list PARTIALLY VERIFIED, drawn from programme documentation rather than the main university page. Regional partners GRAME and AADN Lyon. Opens onto doctoral study.
_rec.fitNotes: Content-wise this is the best match in the whole batch for a programmer who wants to make electronic music: Max/MSP, music computing, sound design for games and live performance, an Ableton developer on the teaching staff, a real music studio, and Ubisoft/GRAME/INRIA connections. The good news from this verification round is that M1 is confirmed as an entry point, so the earlier worry that RIM was M2-only is resolved at programme level. Three live caveats: the M1 admission criteria are simply not published, so he must email Laurent Pottier before committing; instruction is in French, so he needs a DALF/TCF C1-level certificate; and the fee position has worsened — budget €3,950/yr rather than €255. Practical strategy: apply here AND to DIGICREA at the same university in the same season, since a DIGICREA place brings zero tuition plus €33,600.
_rec.verificationNotes: Confirmed on the official UJM programme page: the programme exists at master level, the exact parcours and two options (RIM / Arts numériques), 2-year duration, Saint-Étienne, French as language of instruction, entry level M1 (this CORRECTS the earlier ambiguity that RIM might be M2-only), the three dedicated studios quoted verbatim, the RIM career outcomes, and the two programme directors with contact emails. Separately confirmed via a UJM search that the mention is offered at both M1 and M2. Fees verified on UJM's own 'Droits d'inscription différenciés' page: €3,950 for master 2026-2027, with the €255 figure applying to students already enrolled in 2023-2024. Décret n° 2026-385 of 19 May 2026 verified via Légifrance/Sénat sources: caps exemptions at 30% (2026-27), 25% (2027-28), 20% from 2028, and ends blanket institutional exemptions. NOT confirmed: total ECTS, the 20-student cohort cap, M1 admission criteria and required documents, whether a portfolio or audio commentary is required at M1, the 2027 application dates, the English-taught shared DIGICREA courses (livret only), and the detailed staff list.

_rec.whatYouStudy: From the official M2 page, semester 3 covers: cinematic culture and research methodology, intellectual property law, history of film sound, improvisation for visual media, electronic music, virtual instrument programming, advanced mixing and mastering, English, and musical composition and orchestration applied to image. Substantively no — the official page requires the applicant to already be a composer with command of music notation and orchestration. The open-discipline rule exists for self-taught composers, not for career changers with no music.
_rec.portfolioSpec: A composition portfolio is the selection instrument. The programme requires three recent personal compositions in varied styles, written to three short films: three audio files (wav or mp3) synchronised to three short films of 3–5 minutes maximum, plus three corresponding scores in PDF. _rec.equipmentRequired: Stated on the official M1 page: a powerful computer; advanced DAW software (Logic Pro X, Reaper or Cubase); quality headphones; an audio interface with a keyboard controller. This is a published, mandatory technical prerequisite — a real cost line for him.
_rec.facilities: Campus Rachais, Lyon; students work on their own DAW rigs (see equipment requirement). Studio inventory not published — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.intakes: September (annual), 16 places.
_rec.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED. Route: the official M1 page states applications are made exclusively online through Mon Master (monmaster.gouv.fr); the M2 page refers to eCandidat and notes separate procedures for EU and non-EU applicants. _rec.deadline: UNVERIFIED — no dated calendar on the pages I opened; the M2 page refers to a 'calendrier de candidature'. Confirm with lesla.m1maaav@univ-lyon2.fr and Campus France Tunisie.

_rec.tuitionNonEU: THIS IS THE RATE HE WOULD PAY: 3 950 € at master level for non-EU students, academic year 2026-2027, from Lyon 2's official droits d'inscription page. Important and recent: Lyon 2's own page states its transitional exemption regime 'prend fin dès la rentrée 2026/2027' and that being exempt today no longer carries over automatically — so a new non-EU entrant in 2027 should assume the full 3 950 €. National rules cap institutional exemptions at 30% of liable students in 2026-2027, 25% in 2027-2028 and 20% thereafter.
_rec.otherFees: CVEC payable in addition (Lyon 2 states enrolment = national fees + CVEC); amount not shown on the page I opened — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: ~3 950 €/year plus CVEC plus Lyon living costs, plus the mandatory home studio rig (computer, DAW licence, interface, controller, headphones). No official estimate — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.scholarships: None specific to this programme on the official pages — UNVERIFIED. Note the programme states international recruitment with 36 countries represented, so non-EU applicants are clearly admitted in practice; ask the scolarité what fee exemption exists.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes — public university, diplôme national de master, RNCP 39199.
_rec.recommendation: Report it so he knows it exists, but do not queue it for 2027. The unusual open-discipline rule (a licence in any field) makes it look reachable for a software engineer, and the M2 content — electronic music, virtual instrument programming, advanced mixing and mastering — reads well against his goals. The gate closes it: 16 places a year, decided on three original scored compositions written to three short films, with the official page stating the candidate must already be a composer commanding music notation and orchestration. He cannot write orchestral scores and has a year, not five. If film/game scoring genuinely attracts him, this is a 2029-2030 target reachable only after sustained composition study; the ENJMIN sound-design route and the two engineering routes are the ones that fit the profile he actually has.

_rec.program: Master Cinéma et audiovisuel — parcours Son (entered via the Master 1 Cinéma & Audiovisuel Parcours Généraliste, then Master 2 Son)
_rec.university: Université Toulouse - Jean Jaurès / École Nationale Supérieure d'AudioVisuel (ENSAV)
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years. M1 entry requires Bac+3 / 180 ECTS; M2 Son entry requires Bac+4 / 240 ECTS. Programme ECTS total not published — UNVERIFIED (French masters are 120 ECTS).
_rec.focus: Film Sound + Sound Design + Recording, practice-based and very production-heavy. This is cinema and audiovisual sound, not music production.
_rec.institutionType: Public university film school — école interne of Université Toulouse - Jean Jaurès, described as the first and only national film school located outside Paris
_rec.language: French throughout
_rec.whatYouStudy: Roughly 15 compulsory exercises across the two years — sound pieces, documentaries and fiction works, each with defined pedagogical constraints — plus a personal film at the end of M1 and of M2 with no restriction on genre or duration, each accompanied by a methodological dissertation. Taught content covers acoustic principles, analogue and digital audio technology, sound recording, editing, mixing and diffusion. CONFIRMED M2 Son exercises specifically: location sound recording (phonography), documentary sound creation, sound post-production, a written audio-technology dissertation, sound design for a visual sequence, collaborative work with the Image and Réalisation M2 students on the 'Filmer le Travail' project, and a final thesis with an accompanying audio or audiovisual product defended before a professional jury.
_rec.entryRequirements: IMPORTANT STRUCTURAL CORRECTION. ENSAV does not run a 'parcours Son' from M1. It runs a Master 1 Cinéma & Audiovisuel Parcours Généraliste (alongside M1 Production, REX and XR), and Son is one of seven M2 specialisations (Son, Image, Réalisation, Production, REX, Architecture Décor/VFX, XR). M1 Généraliste entry: 'Licence Création Audiovisuelle ou d'une formation bac+3 équivalente dans les domaines des arts, des arts du spectacle, de l'architecture, du design, des arts plastiques, DE L'INFORMATIQUE ou des beaux-arts', i.e. Bac+3 / 180 ECTS. M2 Son entry: Bac+4 / 240 ECTS, and the ENSAV page states that entrants must have 'already been previously trained in sound basics during the generalist years of Licence and Master 1' at ENSAV. Selection is on dossier, and after the file review 'un entretien peut être programmé avec le candidat'. Dossiers are emailed directly to ensav@univ-tlse2.fr — the Son route is handled by ENSAV itself, not via Mon Master (the Production parcours does use Mon Master). Extra-European applicants are also routed through Études en France. Contact: Djazaira Berkouk, ensav@univ-tlse2.fr, 05 61 50 44 46; ENSAV, 56 rue du Taur, 31000 Toulouse, 05 61 50 35 07.
_rec.portfolioSpec: Not published. The application is a downloadable ENSAV dossier form emailed back to the school. For the Production parcours the dossier requires a one-page mémoire project; the equivalent creative requirement for the generalist M1 and for M2 Son — number of works, length, format — is NOT specified on any public page. UNVERIFIED. He must request the current dossier from ensav@univ-tlse2.fr.
_rec.auditionSpec: No live audition and no written concours found. Selection is on dossier, with a possible interview after the file review ('un entretien peut être programmé'). Whether the interview is remote or on-site in Toulouse is UNVERIFIED.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES for the M1 entry point, and this remains the most explicitly CS-friendly admissions wording found in France: the accepted bachelor list names 'DE L'INFORMATIQUE' outright, so a Bac+3 in computer science is a named, accepted qualification for the Master 1 Généraliste. No music degree, no audition and no music-theory test. BUT — and this is the correction — that acceptance gets him into the GENERALIST M1, not into Son. M2 Son requires Bac+4 and presumes sound training already acquired during ENSAV's own Licence and M1 years, so reaching the Son specialisation means completing the generalist M1 first and then competing internally.

_rec.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 2026-2027 cycle, confirmed on the ENSAV site: M1 dossiers were due 10 May 2026 and M1 registrations are now closed; M2 REX dossiers due 31 August 2026; DURCA due 13 September 2026. The 2026-2027 M2 Son round is also closed. Confirm the 2027-2028 M1 deadline with ensav@univ-tlse2.fr from early 2027.
_rec.tuitionIntl: Public university fees, but the exemption position has worsened. The non-EU differentiated master rate for 2026-2027 is €3,950/yr nationally. Université Toulouse Jean Jaurès's own exemption policy was not read and is UNVERIFIED, but décret n° 2026-385 of 19 May 2026 abolished blanket institutional exemptions across the whole French public system and caps discretionary exemptions at 30% of affected students in 2026-2027 and 25% in 2027-2028. Budget €3,950/yr plus CVEC (~€105) and verify with ENSAV/UT2J directly.
_rec.fundingLevel: None to partial — discretionary and capped fee exemption only, no stipend.
_rec.scholarship: None programme-specific. External routes only: France Excellence Eiffel (institution-nominated, €1,181/month at master level, age cap 25, national Campus France deadline in early January with institutional internal deadlines in the preceding autumn), Campus France Tunisie and French Embassy bourses, and BGF which brings full fee exemption.
_rec.facilities: ENSAV is a public national film school with seven M2 specialisations co-located, so sound students work inside real crews with image, directing, production, VFX and XR students. The M2 Son year emphasises analogue and digital audio technology, acoustic principles and professional audio systems, and includes a cross-specialisation collaborative project. No itemised equipment or console inventory is published — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.fitNotes: Verification changed the verdict here. The admissions wording is still the most CS-friendly in France — 'de l'informatique' is a named accepted licence — and the route into the M1 Généraliste is genuinely open to him, dossier plus possible interview, no audition. But Son is not an M1 parcours: it is one of seven M2 specialisations, and ENSAV states that M2 Son entrants are expected to have already acquired sound basics during the school's own Licence and M1 years. So the realistic path is two-step and uncertain: get into the generalist M1, absorb the sound fundamentals there, then compete for one of the M2 Son places. Layered on top: it is cinema sound rather than music production, so it trains a boom operator or re-recording mixer, not a DJ or producer; it is French-language throughout (fine for him, though a C1 certificate will still be asked for); the dossier contents are not public so he must write to ENSAV; and the fee is now €3,950/yr rather than near-free. Good school, wrong craft for his stated goal, and a bottleneck between entry and specialisation.

Also confirmed there: M1 applications route via Mon Master or Études en France for extra-Europeans, but 'les inscriptions au Master doivent être effectuées directement sur le site de l'ENSAV'. The page does not list the dossier contents, so whether personal sound work may be attached is UNVERIFIED. He should email the programme to ask, since a demo reel would be his strongest argument for equivalence.
_rec.auditionSpec: No audition. An interview ('entretien') follows the dossier review for BOTH M1 and M2 entry — this is a mandatory part of selection, not an optional add-on. Format (remote or on-site in Brest) and language of the interview are UNVERIFIED; assume French.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: CHECK — leaning yes on subject matter, unproven on procedure. The stated requirement is an L3 in Sciences Pour l'Ingénieur with the Image & Son specialisation 'ou équivalent'. A software-engineering BSc is scientifically adjacent and the master's own spine is signal processing, electroacoustics and audio informatics, so the content fit is real. But the programme is explicitly designed as a continuation of UBO's own L3 Image & Son, and nowhere does the page publish wording accepting a general non-specialised science degree, let alone a foreign one. With only 18 places and internal candidates in the pipeline, a direct M1 entry from a Tunisian CS degree needs a case-by-case ruling. He must email the programme to test eligibility BEFORE the monmaster window opens. Note: no music degree is required — the obstacle is the missing image-and-sound specialisation, not a missing music background.

UBO's own notice states plainly that until the new decree it applied a partial exemption to ALL non-EU students it hosted, and that this is 'désormais plus possible'. Following décret n° 2026-385 of 19 May 2026, exemptions are granted only on individual circumstances and may cover a maximum of 30% of affected students in 2026-2027, falling to 25% in 2027-2028 — his intake year. Budget €3,950/yr plus CVEC (~€105). Contact for eligibility: mobilite.internationale@univ-brest.fr.

External routes only: France Excellence Eiffel (institution-nominated, €1,181/month, master age cap 25, institutional internal deadlines around October-December preceding the Campus France national deadline in early January), Campus France Tunisie and French Embassy bourses, and a French government scholarship (BGF) which also brings full exemption from differentiated fees.

Console and room inventory UNVERIFIED — no equipment list is published.
_rec.fitNotes: Technically the closest French public master here to a real sound-engineer training, and verification improved the picture on content: the S8-S9 split confirms an explicit Sound/Music track whose practical project can be musical recordings with mixing and mastering, not just film sound. With 18 students per year, studio time should be genuinely available. Three frictions, one of them new. First, entry: the programme is built as a continuation of its own L3 Image & Son, so a direct M1 entry from a Tunisian CS degree needs a case-by-case ruling — send an eligibility email well before February 2027. Second, money: the blanket partial exemption is gone, so this is now a €3,950/yr proposition rather than the near-free option previously assumed. Third, place: Brest is a long way from any electronic-music scene, which matters for someone whose goal is to become a working DJ. If they accept him, the curriculum-to-goal alignment is among the best in this batch; the risk is that they simply do not.
_rec.verificationNotes: Confirmed on the official UBO formations page: the programme exists at master level; Brest; French; 2 years, 4 semesters, 120 ECTS at 60 per year; the 18-student-per-cohort cap quoted verbatim; M1 entry from L3 SPI parcours Image & Son 'ou équivalent' via monmaster with dossier plus interview; M2 entry via UBO eCandidat with dossier plus interview; the full sound module list (electroacoustics and room acoustics, microphones and loudspeakers, audio signal processing, sonic perception, studio recording/mixing/mastering, spatialized sound in stereo/object-based/binaural); the S8-S9 choice between a Sound/Music and a Cinema track; the practical project alternative of musical recordings with mixing and mastering; internship minimums of 4 weeks in M1 and 4 months in M2; and the ABSENCE of any portfolio requirement.
