_rec.scholarships: No scholarship information on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED. Ask about Centrale Lyon / Université de Lyon international scholarships and pair with Eiffel (already in the database; note Eiffel is nominated by the institution, so he would need Centrale Lyon to put him forward, which means contacting them by autumn 2026).
_rec.visaEligible: Yes — public establishments, national master, and the programme explicitly instructs international applicants to run Études en France in parallel.
_rec.recommendation: Realistically his most admissible option in France: no portfolio, no audition, no music degree, no French-language gate, and an entry rule written for science graduates. It is also the one where his software background is an asset rather than an oddity, and 'sound perception' plus signal processing is a legitimate on-ramp to audio DSP and immersive-audio work. Three honest caveats. (1) It is acoustics engineering — it will not train him as a producer or DJ; that ambition has to be pursued in parallel. (2) His curriculum is software, not mechanics/physics; he should email the programme office with his transcript in autumn 2026 before investing in an application. Cost is the standard non-EU rate with no exemption published, so plan on paying, or get nominated for Eiffel early.

Applicants must bring working knowledge of studio audio technology, microphones and DAW operation. B2 German per the academy's general standard.

The programme-overview table requires only 'entsprechende Vorqualifikation, etwa mindestens ein Vordiplom oder Bachelor' with NO subject restriction, and no music degree is anywhere demanded — a BSc Software Engineering satisfies that on its face. However, the general application page summarises Diplomaufbaustudium entry as requiring a 'completed degree in a related field', which introduces a relatedness test that is not defined for Filmton. A software-engineering degree is plausibly 'related' to audio technology, but he must get this confirmed in writing before applying. The decisive filter in practice is the Pro Tools practical exam, not the bachelor subject.
_rec.portfolioSpec: PARTIAL. Own projects/work samples are uploaded via the online portal, and applicants must clearly identify their individual contribution to each. Published technical limits (example spec, varies by department): video up to 1 GB, MP4 container, H.264 codec, data rate 15 MB/s, typically 5–7 minutes maximum. The exact number and duration of AUDIO samples required for Filmton/Sounddesign is not published — UNVERIFIED. Also submit certified copies of the Hochschulreife and of any Vordiplom/Diplom/Bachelor/Master.
_rec.auditionSpec: YES — pre-selection on the file, then an on-site Aufnahmeprüfung conducted IN PRO TOOLS. Confirmed: 'Die Aufnahmeprüfung für Filmton/Sounddesign wird mit dem Programm Pro Tools durchgeführt. Bewerber*innen sollten daher Grundkenntnisse in den Disziplinen Aufnahme, Sounddesign, Mischung und Bouncing mitbringen.' There is NO instrumental audition and no music-theory paper — the gate is a DAW competence test. This is by far the most learnable audition of the six programmes here.

_rec.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: 15 February, annually and without a year published on the programme page. For a 2027 start plan on 15 February 2027 and confirm when posted.

The academy's fee schedule is €0/semester for a first degree, €650/semester for a second degree or Projektstudium, and €1,500/semester for non-EU citizens, plus a €131.50 semester contribution for everyone. As a Tunisian national over 5 semesters that is roughly €7,500 in fees plus ~€658 in contributions — about €8,150 total, before living costs. The Diplomaufbaustudiengänge are exempt from the second-degree fee, but NOT from the non-EU fee.

Note that DAAD art/film scholarships generally target accredited degree programmes, so the non-master status of this Diplom should be checked against DAAD's eligibility rules before counting on it.
_rec.facilities: PARTIALLY VERIFIED via the curriculum: cinema film mixing and Dolby Atmos, Foley collaboration, film-music recording and mixing, on-set production-sound equipment, and DAW-based post-production suites are all taught, which confirms the corresponding facilities exist. Detailed room and console specifications UNVERIFIED. The academy is one of Europe's most production-active film schools with heavy German TV/film placement.
_rec.fitNotes: The most realistically ENTERABLE film-sound route in Germany for someone without a music degree — the gate is a Pro Tools practical test he can genuinely train for, not a conservatory audition or a theory paper, and no music bachelor is demanded. But verification worsened two things: the fee is €1,500 PER SEMESTER (~€8,150 total, no funding found), and the award is an institutional Diplom rather than an accredited master's. And it makes film and game sound designers, not DJs or producers. Only worth an application if he decides he genuinely wants a screen-audio career alongside producing, and only after confirming both the degree recognition and whether his SE bachelor counts as 'related'.
_rec.verificationNotes: Confirmed on official Filmakademie pages: the programme exists as a Diplomaufbaustudium in Filmton/Sounddesign awarding the Diplom der Filmakademie; 4 semesters + 1 diploma semester; German with English in Projektstudium; the curriculum including Dolby Atmos, Foley, dialogue editing and optional games-sound specialisation; the 15 February deadline (no year); the Pro Tools-based Aufnahmeprüfung with the required prior knowledge of recording, sound design, mixing and bouncing; the video work-sample technical spec (1 GB, MP4, H.264, 15 MB/s); the Hochschulreife requirement with the Begabtenpassus talent clause; B2 German as the academy standard; and the fee schedule. KEY CORRECTIONS: the non-EU fee is €1,500 PER SEMESTER plus €131.50 semester contribution (previously ambiguous), and the Diplom is officially described only as 'comparable to professional qualifying degrees' of state art universities rather than as an accredited master. NOT confirmed: ECTS, the audio work-sample count and duration, the 2027 portal opening date, whether a software-engineering BSc satisfies the 'related field' phrasing, and DAAD eligibility for a non-accredited Diplom.

Stated aim: specialisation in the interdisciplinary area emerging from the intersection of electronic sound technology, sound art and music production, covering recording, processing and reproduction of sound in art and production. Structure: two semesters of taught modules combined with supervised practical/research work, then a third semester devoted entirely to the master's thesis. The official document list places artistic portfolio, publications, documented technological projects and work experience under optional supporting materials. No number of works, duration or format is prescribed. However the selection scoring makes it decisive in practice: the 100-point scale is academic qualifications 30, research/artistic achievements 30, written examinations if required 15, and interview 25 — so 30 points hang directly on demonstrable artistic or research output.
_rec.auditionSpec: No live audition. Candidates whose files are complete and meet the criteria proceed to an INTERVIEW before an evaluation committee, held either in person in Corfu OR ONLINE — remote-friendly. IT, Electronics and Engineering graduates are on the named list of eligible fields, so a BSc in Software Engineering is squarely eligible without any special pleading. Semester A, both specialisations: Ήχος και Τέχνη / Sound and Art (6 ECTS) and Μουσική Πληροφορική / Music Informatics (6) — the latter teaching code-based representation of musical structures, Music Information Retrieval, SuperCollider, ChucK, Python, TensorFlow and LilyPond, plus hands-on additive, subtractive, FM, non-linear waveshaping, spectral, convolution, physical-modelling, granular and stochastic synthesis. Specialisation A adds Σύνθεση Ηλεκτροακουστικής Μουσικής (6) and Ηχητικός Σχεδιασμός / Sound Design (6); Specialisation B adds Τεχνική και Τεχνολογία της Ηχογράφησης / Recording Technique and Technology (6) and Ακουστική – Ψηφιακός Ήχος (6). Semester B: a compulsory 12-ECTS individual research project producing a complete creative work, plus Ραδιοφωνική Ηχητική Τέχνη, Διαδραστικά Ηχητικά Περιβάλλοντα, Σχεδιασμός Λογισμικού Ηχητικής Επεξεργασίας (audio-software design), ΜΟΥΣΙΚΗ ΠΑΡΑΓΩΓΗ / Music Production (6), Ηχητική Επένδυση and Ακουστικός Σχεδιασμός Χώρων. Article 7 and the curriculum page both guarantee that applied creative work "αντιστοιχούν κατ' ελάχιστον στο 50% του συνολικού διδακτικού έργου" — at least half of all teaching work is practical creation, not theory. _rec.entryRequirements: Holders of a first-cycle degree from a Greek HEI or an equivalent foreign institution under Article 34 of Law 4485/2017, in a field related to (a) sound and music art and science, (b) SOUND TECHNOLOGY — explicitly including Μουσικής Τεχνολογίας & Ακουστικής, Φυσικής, ΠΛΗΡΟΦΟΡΙΚΗΣ (Informatics), Ηλεκτρονικής, Ηλεκτρολογίας, Τεχνολογίας Ήχου and engineering diploma-holders from Polytechnic or Architecture schools, or (c) applied fields such as cultural management, cultural technology and communication, cinema and mass media. Graduates of other fields may enter only if they can demonstrate substantial research and/or artistic activity in the field. Required documents: application form stating the chosen specialisation; ID copy; two photographs; degree certificates — and for foreign degrees, "συνοδευόμενους από βεβαίωση αναγνώρισης ισοτιμίας από τον Δ.Ο.Α.Τ.Α.Π.", i.e. a formal DOATAP equivalence recognition, which is a slow and non-trivial process for a Tunisian degree; a certificate of at least good knowledge of English; full CV; statement of purpose; and AT LEAST TWO recommendation letters. Submission in the last published cycle was BY POST to the secretariat in Corfu.
_rec.portfolioSpec: Recommended but not mandatory. The official document list places "φάκελος καλλιτεχνικών έργων" (artistic portfolio) alongside work experience, scientific publications and documented technological development work under the optional heading "Λοιπά στοιχεία (εφόσον υπάρχουν) που να τεκμηριώνουν την υποψηφιότητα". No number of works, duration or format is prescribed. But it is decisive in practice: Article 11 of the regulation sets a 100-point scale of formal qualifications 30, scientific/artistic qualifications 30, written examinations where held 15, and statement of purpose plus interview 25 — so 30 of 100 points hang on demonstrable artistic or research output, and a further sub-rule gives up to 10 points for certified professional experience at 2 points per year, which he does not have.
_rec.auditionSpec: No audition. Candidates whose files are complete and meet the criteria are called for interview before the evaluation committees, held "είτε με φυσική παρουσία στην έδρα του ΔΠΜΣ (Κέρκυρα), είτε διαδικτυακά" — in person in Corfu OR online. The interview is worth 25 of 100 points. A written examination may be set (15 points) but is conditional, not automatic.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Yes, explicitly. Πληροφορικής (Informatics), Ηλεκτρονικής, Ηλεκτρολογίας, Φυσικής and Polytechnic-school engineering diplomas are all on the named eligible list, so a software-engineering BSc is squarely eligible without invoking the escape clause. The practical gate is not the discipline but DOATAP equivalence recognition of the Tunisian degree.
_rec.tuitionIntl: €2,700 total for the whole programme — VERIFIED from both the official call and Article 18 of the regulation. Payable in one sum or in five instalments: €500 on enrolment, €400 before the first-semester exam period, €400 within two weeks of the second semester starting, €500 before the second-semester exam period, €900 within two weeks of the third semester starting. Non-refundable if studies are interrupted. This figure is from the 2022-23 edition — Greek postgraduate fee law has changed since, so confirm for 2027.
_rec.scholarship: Article 18 fee waivers: "Ποσοστό έως 30% κατά μέγιστο των εισακτέων μεταπτυχιακών φοιτητών απαλλάσσονται από την καταβολή του συνόλου των τελών φοίτησης" — up to 30% of admitted students are fully exempt from all tuition under Article 35 of Law 4485/2017. _rec.fundingLevel: Partial to Full on tuition — a full fee waiver is genuinely available to up to 30% of the intake; no living stipend exists.
_rec.stipend: None. Fee waiver only, and it carries a service obligation: waiver holders and scholarship recipients "έχουν την υποχρέωση να προσφέρουν υπηρεσίες υποστήριξης προς τα δύο Τμήματα" — laboratory, tutorial or other support work for the two departments. He would self-fund living costs in Corfu.
_rec.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. The most recent call published on the official site opened 1 July 2022 for the 2022-23 year. No newer call is posted and the announcements page is empty.
_rec.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: 18 September 2022 for the 2022-23 intake, by postal submission, date-stamped by the programme secretariat. For a September 2027 start a summer 2027 call would be expected — but see the continuation warning below before planning around it.

Annual festival and artistic summer school immediately after the spring semester, at which student creative work is formally presented. Places strictly capped at 15 per specialisation. _rec.fitNotes: On paper still the best-designed curriculum in the slice for his profile — an Informatics/engineering bachelor is named as eligible, there is no audition, the portfolio is formally optional, the interview can be done online from Tunis, tuition is only €2,700 with a real 30% chance of a full waiver, at least half of all teaching is guaranteed to be applied creative work, and Specialisation B literally contains a Music Production module. But three verified facts push it down. FIRST AND DECISIVE: the language of instruction is stated as Greek, with only some parts in English and no English track — he does not have Greek and cannot realistically reach delivery-level Greek by September 2027. SECOND: foreign degrees require formal DOATAP equivalence recognition, a slow bureaucratic step he must start well over a year out. THIRD, and the one to check before spending any effort: the most recent call on the official site is 2022-23, the site was last updated 31 May 2022, the announcements page is empty, and Article 1 of the regulation states the programme was established to run for eight academic years from its 2018-19 start — which expires with 2025-26. It may well have been renewed, but nothing published confirms it. Email the secretariat (kaiti@ionio.gr) to ask whether the programme is still running for 2027-28 and how much of Specialisation B is deliverable in English before treating this as a live option.

_rec.institutionType: Public conservatory / national academy of music
_rec.focus: Electroacoustic Composition; Electronic Music/Live Electronics; Sonic Arts
_rec.language: English — the Stipendium Hungaricum course record confirms "Study language: English". But the Academy's own page carries a conditional: "in case of non-instrumental majors, tuition is only offered in English if there are a minimum of 3 international students admitted in a given year to the same major." This remains the key structural risk for an English-track applicant.
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years — CONFIRMED as "4 semesters (120 ECTS)" on the Stipendium Hungaricum course record. (Prior record listed ECTS as unverified; now verified.)
_rec.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED programme description: one-to-one lessons with a composition teacher developing one's own compositions and analysing 20th- and 21st-century pieces; performance of orchestral and vocal final diploma pieces; composition-related special courses freely chosen by interest; master courses from visiting professors and artists; and explicitly "Possibility to deepen studies in the field of electronic music." Applicants admitted to Classical Composition who have not studied electronic music before may have to complete two semesters of 'The basics of electronic composition'. Note: no specialisation named "Elektronikus zenei médiaművészet" or "EZMM" appears on the official MA admission page — the three published tracks are Classical, Electroacoustic and Applied Composition.
_rec.entryRequirements: Bachelor diploma or higher. CONFIRMED verbatim: "Applicants must submit a preliminary credit recognition request directly to the Liszt Academy to determine whether the applicant's BA diploma can be accepted to apply for the programme, unless they have finished their BA studies at the Liszt Academy in the same field. Deadline: 31 March." Acceptable BA diplomas are defined in Annex 8 of the Academic Regulations for Students. An official Hungarian translation of the BA diploma is required by 31 March, made from the original document (not a copy); English translations are accepted during the application window only. Language certificate: TOEFL iBT min. 60, IELTS Academic min. 5.0, or Cambridge min. 154 — no other certificates accepted. A motivation letter is required. Applications route through the Stipendium Hungaricum portal or, for self-financed study, separately by 31 March.
_rec.portfolioSpec: MAJOR CORRECTION — this is far less classical than previously recorded. For the ELECTROACOUSTIC COMPOSITION specialisation, verbatim: "Presentation of a fixed electroacoustic music piece and another piece applying live electronics with an acoustic instrument", and "The pieces submitted together must not exceed 25-30 minutes." Style exercises for electroacoustic are: "1 short etude in the style of any significant 20th-century musique concrète composer" and "1 short etude in the style of significant 20th-century synthesis technique composer". THERE IS NO BACH FUGUE AND NO CLASSICAL SONATA REQUIREMENT for this specialisation — the fugue, the Viennese Classical sonata movement and the 20th-century etude apply ONLY to Classical and Applied Composition. Separately, the Stipendium Hungaricum course record states generically that applicants "are to upload sheet music of three of their own compositions (and recordings if possible)" and are first pre-screened on that portfolio — reconcile this generic wording with the specialisation-specific spec directly with the Academy.
_rec.auditionSpec: In person in Budapest, per the Academy's Stipendium Hungaricum page, verbatim: "All applicants are required to appear at the entrance examinations in person in Budapest, Hungary. The live entrance examinations cannot be substituted in any way", and on the SH course record: "Live streaming, video streaming, DVDs, CDs, or any other recordings are not accepted as a substitute." Exams take place late June / early July; candidates who clear the portfolio pre-screening are told their date during May. Components FOR ELECTROACOUSTIC specifically: formal analysis, written and oral, of a 20th-century instrumental work and an electroacoustic work; orchestration assessed as "MIDI sequencer orchestrating a chamber music piece for MIDI instruments or sampler" (not symphony-orchestra orchestration, which is the Classical track); score reading replaced by "Analysis of a contemporary graphic music notation"; a mandatory written test on the basics of electronic music (history from Varèse through Stockhausen, Xenakis, Chowning; sound parameters; waveform/spectrum/sonogram; sound types; tunings; sampling rate, Nyquist, bit depth; additive, subtractive, FM and granular synthesis); an oral practical computer task — mounting in ProTools or another DAW, algorithmic music in MAX/MSP or Pd, or sound synthesis in MAX/MSP, CSound, Pd or SuperCollider; and a personal interview on artistic beliefs, goals and general musical literacy. NOTE A CONTRADICTION: the admission-requirements page carries the heading "For applicants for the online entrance examination:", implying an online route exists, while the SH pages insist on in-person only. Resolve with international.office@lisztacademy.hu.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Check — no longer a flat 'no', but genuinely uncertain and gated. Nothing formally bars a non-music BA, and the electroacoustic exam does NOT test classical composition craft. The binding gate is the mandatory preliminary credit recognition request, which decides "whether the applicant's BA diploma can be accepted to apply for the programme" against Annex 8 of the Academic Regulations — a software-engineering BSc may simply fail that check, and it is decided before the exam. The exam itself still assumes he can produce two credible electroacoustic works including one with live electronics and an acoustic instrument, write two style etudes, analyse 20th-century scores and graphic notation, and pass an electronic-music theory test. This is buildable in a year of hard work in a way a Bach fugue is not. Submit the credit recognition request early and treat its outcome as the go/no-go.

This is the only fully-funded, English-taught, Tunisia-eligible route in the slice, and the electroacoustic entrance exam turns out to be about electroacoustic craft, not classical conservatory training — no fugue, no sonata, no orchestral score reading, and the orchestration test is MIDI sequencing. Two hard gates remain: the preliminary credit recognition decision on a software-engineering BSc, and a mandatory in-person exam in Budapest. IELTS 5.0 is a low bar he can clear easily. Named modules: LABORATORIO DI PRODUZIONE — developing original projects with a music-producer's approach to the whole production chain; TECNICHE DI RIPRESA E REGISTRAZIONE — each specialising student produces TWO TRACKS end-to-end, from pre-production and arrangement through rehearsals, recording and overdubbing, microphone choice and placement, editing, mixing and mastering; ORCHESTRAZIONE — professional virtual orchestration, arrangement, real and virtual instruments, sound construction within the production; ANALISI DELLA PRODUZIONE MUSICALE — evolution of the producer's role, the approaches of the most influential producers in history, and the compositional/structural/expressive techniques of the main contemporary popular-music languages, completed with sound design applied to the timbral character of a track; DIRITTO D'AUTORE, ROYALTIES E CONTRATTUALISTICA — copyright, royalties, licence, publishing, production and performance contracts. Institution: ProDJ Academy
Programme / scheme: Curso Master Producer (Producer I + Producer II) — SHORT COURSE, NOT A MASTER'S DEGREE DESPITE THE NAME
Why that chance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's; portfolio required, so build it

_rec.program: Curso Master Producer (Producer I + Producer II) — SHORT COURSE, NOT A MASTER'S DEGREE DESPITE THE NAME
_rec.institution: ProDJ Academy
_rec.qualification: NOT A DEGREE AND NOT A MASTER'S. The word 'Master' in 'Master Producer' is a marketing label for an advanced course, NOT an academic master's degree. It is a DGERT-certified vocational diploma with no ECTS and no academic grau. This is exactly the naming trap to watch for.
_rec.institutionType: Specialist private DJ and electronic-music-production academy (DGERT-certified training entity, not higher education). Describes itself as the only DGERT-certified DJ and music production academy in Portugal.
_rec.focus: Electronic music production and DJing in Ableton Live — by far the closest institutional match in Portugal to his stated goal of becoming an international DJ/producer.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Producer I: DAW introduction, MIDI manipulation, beat construction, musical composition (scales, chords, progressions), analogue and digital synthesis, audio engineering fundamentals (compression, EQ, mixing), introduction to mastering. Producer II: advanced production processes, mixing techniques, sound design, vocal treatment, compression variations, sidechain effects, professional mastering. Plus 40 hours of professional studio access bookable online and usable up to 3 months after the course ends, 20 hours of 'LAB' Q&A sessions with instructors, four video tutorials with instructor corrections, and access to online classes from other timetables.
_rec.durationEcts: 200 hours over approximately 10 months. No ECTS. Multiple weekly timetable options in both cities.
_rec.language: Portuguese — UNVERIFIED whether any English-medium delivery exists.
_rec.entryRequirements: Extraordinarily low: minimum age 14; basic computer literacy; any special health conditions to be documented at registration. No portfolio, no interview, no prior music knowledge.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES — completely. Minimum age 14 and basic computer skills are the only stated requirements. There is no academic prerequisite at all. Be clear-eyed about what that means: this is an open-enrolment commercial course, and the absence of any selection is itself information about what the certificate is worth.
_rec.portfolioSpec: None required.
_rec.auditionSpec: None. No interview, no test.
_rec.englishTest: None.
_rec.tuitionPerYear: €2,490 upfront for the full 200-hour Master Producer course (Lisbon and Porto, same price). Alternatives: 4 monthly instalments of €622.50, or from €320/month over 10 months.
_rec.tuitionTotal: €2,490 total tuition (upfront price). The 10-month plan 'from €320/month' implies up to €3,200 if taken over ten payments — a materially higher total, so the instalment route costs more. No non-EU differential published.
_rec.otherFees: Enrolment/registration fee €420 (stated to vary by payment method). Diploma issuance fee €45 — charged SEPARATELY, i.e. the certificate itself is an extra. Total realistic outlay: €2,955 upfront (€2,490 + €420 + €45) or up to roughly €3,665 on the 10-month plan. No insurance or materials fee published — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.equipmentRequired: Not published as mandatory — UNVERIFIED. In practice an Ableton Live licence and a laptop are needed; the course includes 40 hours of studio access, which partly offsets this. Confirm whether an Ableton licence is included or must be purchased.
_rec.paymentPlans: Three published options: upfront €2,490; 4 × €622.50; from €320/month over 10 months. No early-bird, alumni or referral discount published — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.scholarships: NONE published — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.intakes: MULTIPLE intakes per year — several 2026-2027 start dates published for Lisbon (weekend and weekday options) with more limited availability in Porto. This rolling-intake pattern is typical of commercial academies.
_rec.applicationOpens: Rolling — enrol at any time for the next available cohort.
_rec.deadline: No deadline; rolling enrolment by cohort start date.
_rec.facilities: In-studio learning with professional equipment in both Lisbon and Porto; 40 hours of bookable professional studio time included, usable up to 3 months post-course; 20 hours of LAB mentoring. Detailed equipment inventory not published — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.visaEligible: NO. Although the 10-month duration is longer than most courses in this slice, it is still under the 12-month threshold for a D4 study residence visa, and vocational OFP training at a non-higher-education academy is not a recognised visa-sponsoring category. ProDJ publishes nothing about visa support for non-EU students. He CANNOT move to Portugal on this.
_rec.reputationSignals: Positive and genuinely relevant: DGERT certification (it claims to be the only DGERT-certified DJ/production academy in Portugal), instructors holding CCP pedagogical credentials, two campuses, included studio hours, and a syllabus squarely aimed at electronic music and DJing — which is what he actually wants. Negative: age-14 minimum and no selection whatsoever; the 'Master Producer' name invites exactly the confusion this report exists to prevent; a separate €45 charge to issue the diploma; an enrolment fee (€420–€520) that varies by payment method, which is an odd and slightly opaque practice; and instalment plans that increase the total cost without this being flagged. No independent graduate-outcome data or notable alumni published.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: €2,955 all-in paying upfront (tuition €2,490 + enrolment €420 + diploma €45). Up to roughly €3,665 on the 10-month instalment plan. Plus living costs if attending in person in Lisbon or Porto (~€900–€1,300/month for 10 months = €9,000–€13,000) — which dwarfs the tuition and is unfunded and visa-less.
_rec.recommendation: CLOSEST TO WHAT HE WANTS TO DO, FURTHEST FROM WHAT HE NEEDS INSTITUTIONALLY. Be direct with him: if the only goal were 'learn to produce electronic music and DJ', this is the most on-target training in Portugal, and €2,955 is not unreasonable for 200 hours plus 40 studio hours. But it is not a master's despite its name, it confers no academic credit, and critically it CANNOT get him a residence permit — so he would be paying €12,000+ including living costs to sit in Lisbon on a tourist footing with no legal study status. The rational play is the inverse: use an accredited master's (UCP Porto, Lusófona, or funded ReSound) to obtain the visa and the residence permit, and then, once legally resident, add a ProDJ or ETIC specialisation as a cheap evening top-up. Never the other way round.

Mandatory documents: ID/passport; graduation certificate; transcript listing all courses with ECTS; CV; motivation letter (PDF, max 1 page); dissertation/research-topic proposal (max 5 pages); portfolio. Application fee €55 (PayPal accepted for applicants without a Portuguese bank account). No language certificate appears on the published documentation list.

It is run out of the engineering faculty's informatics department and its sibling specialisation is Interactive Technologies and Digital Games. A BSc Software Engineering is a natural feeder. The competitive risk is not the degree subject — it is the mandatory portfolio and the 50%-weighted project proposal.

CORRECTED place counts: 60 places in total for the Master in Multimedia across all four specialisations, split 10 (1st phase) / 30 (2nd) / 20 (3rd) — not 20 per phase. FEUP explicitly warns visa-needing international students to check each phase's result-posting and enrolment dates; for a Tunisian applicant phase 1 or 2 is effectively mandatory.

It is where a programmer becomes a technical sound designer, not where you learn to mix a club track.

_rec.whatYouStudy: IAD's sound training covers the full sound-engineer profession: studio and live recording, mixing, editing, mastering, event sound reinforcement (sonorisation) and sound design, training 'sound engineers who master sound recording tools and techniques in radio, television and multimedia, as well as editors and sound mixers who master editing and sound mixing tools'. Students collaborate with IAD's multimedia, theatre and directing programmes on real productions. The three orientations split the field: Son Studio is closest to music recording and mixing, Son Sono covers live sound, Cinéma Son covers film sound.

Application is by email to admissions-masters@iad-arts.be with: identity photo, CV, motivation letter, secondary-education diploma, the relevant degree, ID copy, birth certificate, prior academic records, and the portfolio. Candidates selected on file and works are then auditioned by a jury.

The real gate is the portfolio, which must prove technical and artistic ability in the chosen orientation, and the assumed technical baseline is that of IAD's own 180-ECTS sound bachelor.

CRITICAL: IAD does NOT appear on the official list of MASTER IN – WBI grant host institutions (which does include ARTS², La Cambre, INSAS and other arts schools), so the main WBI master's scholarship is not available here. No IAD-internal scholarship for non-EU students was found.

Master students undertake an advanced internship and defend a final work before a professional jury, and work across the school's multimedia, theatre and directing programmes. Software engineering is neither performing nor composing music nor an artistic discipline, so a bridging (schakel) programme is the probable path, not direct master entry. _rec.focus: Music technology / electronic and computer music composition, in a classical-conservatoire setting. Not a commercial dance-music or DJ school.

_rec.entryRequirements: THIS IS THE PROBLEM FOR HIM. The official MA-Admission page states: 'The prerequisite for admission to Master's degree programmes is a Bachelor's academic degree, higher academic musical education.' Read literally, that demands a music bachelor - which he does not have. However, the Music Technology entrance is assessed purely on artistic project + portfolio + English interview, with no instrumental or theory exam, which is the kind of programme that in practice admits technologists. HE MUST WRITE TO enrollment@tsc.edu.ge AND ASK, IN WRITING, WHETHER A BSc IN SOFTWARE ENGINEERING SATISFIES THE ENTRY REQUIREMENT FOR MUSIC TECHNOLOGY. Do this in autumn 2026, before investing in the portfolio. Additional documents required from a foreign applicant not taking the Unified Master's Exam: bachelor's diploma from an HEI recognised in his country (electronic version of the original), transcript of grades and credits, passport copy, one 3x4 digital photograph, payment receipt.

The official 'Master's Degree Educational Programme of Music Technology - Requirements for the Admission/Exam/Audition Round' document specifies: assessment on a 100-point system, passing range 71-100. The round consists of (A) a written description of the applicant's artistic project (electronic file/folder) plus submission of a portfolio of past artistic activities (electronic file/folder), and (B) an English-language interview on project-related issues, in which the applicant presents the project and answers questions. Crucially, that document states the General Master's Exam applies to the GEORGIAN-language programme; the English-language programme requires only the specialty exam/audition round. Document: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1dfV5yDgkkFwWVWQTrHFew3a78tD8fjCi/view

(2) A portfolio of completed creative activities. Both are submitted as an electronic file or folder to enrollment@tsc.edu.ge with the registration pack. Changes to the Artistic Project and Portfolio are permitted up to 25 June of the admission year. No format, length, duration or track-count specification is published - UNVERIFIED; ask the Music Technology department for a spec before he builds it. For him the Artistic Project is the lever: it is a proposal, not a track record, and a software engineer can write a strong one.

_rec.facilities: Officially documented: a Music Technology Department (within the Composition and Musicology Faculty), a Grand Hall and a Recital Hall, a library and a museum. TSC's Music Technology department has hosted electroacoustic-music teaching including recording techniques. NO official inventory of studios, control rooms, consoles or immersive/spatial rigs is published - UNVERIFIED. Ask ir.office@tsc.edu.ge for a studio list with photographs before committing; this is the single biggest unknown about the programme.

_rec.englishTest: B2 CEFR minimum. IELTS, Cambridge English PET, Pitman ESOL International, TOEIC or TOEFL are named as acceptable, BUT the rule also accepts 'any other official document issued by an accredited educational institution confirming at least B2-level proficiency in English'. He has not taken IELTS - this alternative clause may spare him the test entirely. Confirm in writing with enrollment@tsc.edu.ge.
_rec.scholarships: NONE HE CAN WIN. TSC's own fee PDF carries the explicit sentence: '*Scholarships and institutional funding are not available for international students.' There are 5 state-funded places in the English-language Music Technology MA, but those sit in the quota table for applicants applying WITH the Georgian Unified Master's Exam - the domestic route. The separate quota table for applicants WITHOUT the Unified Master's Exam (his route) carries no funding column and simply caps foreign admission at 5% of maximum enrollment capacity. External options he could pursue independently are not offered by TSC and are UNVERIFIED here.
_rec.visaEligible: He would need a Georgian immigration (study) visa and then a study residence permit. WHETHER A TUNISIAN NATIONAL NEEDS A VISA BEFORE ARRIVAL IN GEORGIA IS UNVERIFIED - TSC publishes nothing on this and I did not open the Georgian MFA register. Check the visa navigator at the Georgian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (mfa.gov.ge) and the Public Service Development Agency (sda.gov.ge) for the study residence permit. IMPORTANT AND OFTEN MISSED: Georgia is NOT in the EU or Schengen. Studying here gives him no EU residence rights, no Schengen mobility, and no route to an EU post-study work permit. The degree itself is EHEA/Bologna and recognisable in the EU via ENIC-NARIC, but he would be starting his EU access from zero after graduating.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: UNCERTAIN AND DECISIVE - MUST BE ASKED. The stated prerequisite is 'a Bachelor's academic degree, higher academic musical education', which on its face excludes him. Against that: the Music Technology entrance has no musical audition at all, only a project, a portfolio and an English interview - a structure designed for people who make things with computers. This is the single question that determines whether Georgia is on his list. Email enrollment@tsc.edu.ge and ir.office@tsc.edu.ge in October 2026.
_rec.recommendation: THE BEST FIND IN THIS ENTIRE FOUR-COUNTRY SLICE, and the only one taught in English. Fit with him is genuinely good: no instrumental audition, no music-theory exam, entry on a written artistic project plus portfolio, an English-language interview, a B2 English rule with a non-test escape clause, MusiQuE international accreditation, and 3,423 EUR/year - cheap enough that self-paying is realistic. Two hard warnings. FIRST: zero funding. TSC states in writing that international students get no scholarships or institutional funding, so this is a pure self-pay decision of about 6,900 EUR tuition plus living. SECOND: the entry rule says 'higher academic musical education' and he has a software engineering BSc - resolve this by email before spending a year building a portfolio for it. Two smaller cautions: the studio inventory is not published, which for a technology programme is a real gap he should close with photographs before accepting; and Georgia is outside the EU and Schengen, so this degree advances his craft and his credential but not his European residence position. Practical sequencing: because TSC registration opens in late May, it does not compete with the Oct 2026 - Feb 2027 European deadlines. He can apply to funded European programmes first and hold Tbilisi as a paid fallback decided in summer 2027. Action list: (1) Oct 2026 - email enrollment@tsc.edu.ge and ir.office@tsc.edu.ge with three questions: does a non-music BSc qualify for Music Technology; what exactly does the portfolio need to contain; what studios and equipment does the Music Technology department have. (2) Ask whether a letter from SMU MedTech confirming English-medium study satisfies the B2 rule. (3) Spend the year building the portfolio and, more importantly, drafting the Master's Artistic Project - that document, not his back catalogue, is what he is admitted on.

_rec.program: Creative Production (Music) MA
_rec.university: Catalyst – Institute for Creative Arts and Technology, Berlin (degree validated by Plymouth Marjon University, UK)
_rec.institutionType: Private specialist creative-arts institute, not a German state Hochschule. Its own FAQ describes it as a registered training centre regulated under German law whose degrees are 'validated by our accrediting partner Plymouth Marjon University in the United Kingdom', with MA graduates receiving 'British degrees and certificates with an equivalent status recognised in Germany and the EU'. The earlier description 'state-accredited HEI' overstates this — correct it.
_rec.degree: MA (Master of Arts), awarded by Plymouth Marjon University (UK)
_rec.durationEcts: 1 year full-time or 2 years part-time. Credit total (UK credits or ECTS) is NOT published on the course page or fees page — it sits in the downloadable course guide/syllabus. UNVERIFIED.
_rec.language: English throughout — 'taught entirely in English'. No German required.
_rec.focus: Sonic Arts / practice-led artistic research, spanning music production, electronic and electroacoustic music, spatial and immersive audio, creative coding, sound art
_rec.whatYouStudy: Five modules forming one arc: Imagine (detailed research proposal, research contract and work plan agreed with a supervisor), Contextualise (critical review of existing concepts, literature, practices and methods in the field), Investigate (survey then depth), Present (creation, public presentation and documentation of outward-facing work), Synthesise (a substantial original work or body of works). Three concurrent year-long workshops: Creative Sound Practices — weekly sessions moving 'between modular synthesis, spatial sound, creative coding, field recording, improvisation and sound installation', with the explicit aim being 'not technical mastery but the development of a personal methodology'; Contexts of Listening (musicology, sound studies, philosophy, critical theory — Oliveros, Schaeffer, Attali, Fisher, Butler, Derrida and others); and Supervision (one-to-one plus group critique). Guest artists have included Nicolas Collins, Bob Ostertag and Kaffe Matthews. The page is emphatic and repeats the warning twice: 'This is not a studio engineering degree, a vocational production course or a genre-based music programme. It is postgraduate artistic research' and 'This programme is not suited to those seeking vocational production training, DAW certification or a genre-based music course.' Encouragingly for him, past students have come 'from various backgrounds, including songwriting, house, techno, folk, jazz ... experimental and electroacoustic music'.
_rec.entryRequirements: 'Bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline, with an Honours grade (e.g. 2:1 in the UK university system) or be in the final year of studies for one.' Non-standard entry exists: applicants lacking the minimum education requirement 'may be assessed on the strength of a professional CV and portfolio, which must demonstrate a solid background in artistic practice and research'. English at 'IELTS 6 (referred to as B2 in Germany and other EU countries)', evidenced either by an official certificate or by taking Catalyst's own online assessment — which is a real advantage given he has not sat IELTS. Submission is via an online portal: transcripts, portfolio with work samples, professional references, and a project proposal.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Check — likely yes, but not stated as such. The requirement is a bachelor's 'in a relevant discipline' at Honours level, and students are said to come 'from a wide range of backgrounds'. Software engineering is arguably relevant to creative coding and spatial audio, and the non-standard route offers a fallback, but the page does not name computer science and selection turns on the project proposal and portfolio. Ask Admissions directly whether an SE BSc satisfies 'relevant discipline'; the FAQ invites exactly that conversation.
_rec.portfolioSpec: Not quantified anywhere public — UNVERIFIED as to number and duration. Confirmed components: a portfolio with work samples; a detailed project proposal framed as practice-led artistic research (the school runs free online prep workshops on artistic and practice-based research specifically to help applicants shape it, and offers to send a recent graduate's final project portfolio as a reference on request); a sample of research/academic writing; academic transcripts; professional references; and personal/educational documentation. The proposal, not the music, is the decisive artefact.
_rec.auditionSpec: None — confirmed: there is no interview or audition requirement; the assessment is a digital submission reviewed by admissions. A voluntary call with the Admissions team is offered and, given the 'relevant discipline' question, he should take it.
_rec.applicationOpens: Rolling, with a priority deadline that carries a €1,000 tuition discount for early enrolment.
_rec.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Published for the 2026 intake (start September 2026): priority deadline 28 February 2026 (early-enrolment bonus); visa-required applicants 30 April 2026; EU/visa-exempt 5 June 2026; late applications until 28 August 2026 'subject to availability'. For a September 2027 start expect the same pattern — priority around late February 2027 and a visa-required deadline around 30 April 2027 — but the 2027 dates are not yet published. As a Tunisian national he is bound by the EARLIER visa-required deadline, not the general one.
_rec.tuitionIntl: SELF-PAY FALLBACK, confirmed, and the same for everyone: 'Our fees are the same for all students, no matter where you come from, and stay consistent for every year of your studies.' Full-time €6,028 per semester (two instalments per year) or €11,693 per year paid annually (3% discount). Part-time €3,678 per semester or €7,134 per year. Plus a non-refundable enrolment fee of €895 per study year, which includes visa support. So roughly €12,588 for the full-time year, or about €16,000 over two years part-time. Monthly and extended payment plans exist.
_rec.fundingLevel: None (self-pay). BAföG and German/EU national schemes are referenced on the site but are not open to a first-time non-EU international student, and because the degree is awarded by a UK university rather than a German Hochschule, DAAD study scholarships for study in Germany would not apply either.
_rec.scholarship: No means- or merit-based scholarship for a non-EU applicant was found. Only price reductions: €1,000 early-application/priority tuition discount, 3% discount for annual payment, a further discount for paying in full, and €500 off total tuition for combining a summer short course with a degree within two years.
_rec.facilities: Located in the Funkhaus, the former GDR broadcasting complex. Confirmed from the site: multiple studios, extensive modular-synthesis equipment, spatial-sound tools, creative-coding resources and a bookable gear library; past MA projects have used 'the internationally unique Monom system based at the Funkhaus' for 4D multichannel composition. The programme is embedded in Berlin's experimental scene, engaging each year with Atonal, CTM, Floating University and MANIFEST:IO, running a public two-day MA Symposium and the student-run Etikett Radio (with partnerships including Refuge Worldwide). The 'Ableton Certified Training centre' claim was not seen on the pages checked — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.fitNotes: The best environment on this list for a would-be electronic producer and the only one with no language barrier: Berlin, the Funkhaus, English-taught, no audition, one year, and an English test he can sit through the school itself rather than booking IELTS. Two hard caveats. It costs about €12,588 for the full-time year with no funding he can access — label it the self-pay fallback and nothing else. And the school states twice, unprompted, that this is postgraduate artistic research and explicitly not vocational production training or a genre-based course; the admissions decision hinges on a practice-led research proposal, which is a genuinely unfamiliar genre of writing for a software-engineering graduate and the thing he would need months of preparation for (their free prep workshops exist for exactly this reason). Judged purely as a career move, the Berlin network, the Funkhaus studios, the symposium and the radio station may be worth more to a DJ career than any credential in this batch — but he would be buying access, not being funded into it.

Lusófona: general-purpose recording studio, 5.1 Dolby Surround post room, 7.1.4 Dolby Atmos post auditorium, Sonic Arts Lab (audio+video+microcontrollers), Apple/MIDI-equipped labs, large equipment loan warehouse. Other fields considered with relevant prior experience. Also required: passport copy, headshot, stamped degree documents + transcripts (certified English translation if needed), CV of professional qualifications and experience, TWO letters of recommendation (at least one academic, addressed to 'board members of ReSound'), letter of motivation (max 1000 characters, explicitly 'do not use AI / Large Language Models'), a 500-character description of a proposed final thesis project, portfolio, English proof. English: IELTS 6.0 with no component below 6.0, or TOEFL iBT 79 / Duolingo 110 / Cambridge B2 / LanguageCert ESOL, taken within the last two years; OR a full EQF Level 4+ qualification of at least one academic year taught through English. FAQ adds: works can be "audio recordings or audio related outputs... video related outputs and there could be songs, music, soundtracks, arts and Electro acoustic music performance"; "Focus on contrast rather than have three of the same sort of style"; and explicitly "If I do not already have a suitable portfolio of work can I create one specifically for this programme? _rec.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL and the highest-quality signal available in this slice. Critically, the published wording states: 'Applicants with degrees in other fields may also be considered if they possess relevant prior experience' in areas such as sound, music, film or media. Application pack: academic transcripts, portfolio, TWO recommendation letters, proof of English proficiency. Maximum 24 places per year.

A Software Engineering BSc is a 'degree in another field', so admission turns entirely on evidencing 'relevant prior experience' in sound/music/film/media. He currently has NONE — no music degree, no conservatory training, no professional audio work. Between now and a January-2027 deadline he must manufacture that evidence: released tracks, credited sound work on short films or games, live sets, an audio software project. Without it, this is a rejection.
_rec.portfolioSpec: Exactly specified, unusually clearly: maximum 3 examples of sound or media-related work; a single hyperlink to a portfolio site or a compiled file is acceptable; each piece needs a short reflective paragraph stating his role; total realistic listening/viewing time 10–15 minutes. Note the discipline this demands — three strong pieces, not a dump.
_rec.auditionSpec: No audition or performance test published. Selection is on documents, portfolio and references; an interview stage is UNVERIFIED.
_rec.englishTest: YES — and this is his action item. IELTS 6.0 minimum with ALL components at 6.0 or above. Equivalents accepted: TOEFL iBT 79, Duolingo 110, Cambridge B2, LanguageCert ESOL. Tests must be within 2 years of application. Alternative: completion of an EQF Level 4+ qualification with at least one year taught in English — worth checking whether his SMU MedTech BSc, if English-taught, qualifies him for this waiver, as that would save both the fee and the sitting. He has NOT taken IELTS; on a January 2027 deadline he must book it by roughly October 2027... i.e. autumn 2026, immediately.

CONFLICT FLAG: Universidade Lusófona's own ReSound page instead quotes an average of about €2,250 per month for 30-ECTS semestral units (roughly €9,000 per semester), which does not reconcile with the consortium's €15,000 total. Treat the consortium figure (resound-ma.eu) as authoritative and get the discrepancy resolved in writing before applying.

Because of the three-country mobility, he should also budget for THREE residence-permit processes (Ireland, Portugal, Lithuania) and inter-country relocation — a real, unpublished cost that could easily add €1,500–€3,000 across the two years. Erasmus Mundus scholarships cover FULL tuition (he pays €0) plus a stipend of €1,400 PER MONTH, which is explicitly described as contributing to travel, visa and living allowance. Over 24 months that is roughly €33,600 in stipend plus €15,000 in waived tuition — around €48,600 of value. Awarded on merit. Number of scholarships is a limited share of the maximum 24 annual places — so it is genuinely competitive, but EMJM calls typically reserve a substantial quota for Partner Country (non-EU) applicants, which is his category. This is the single item in this whole Portuguese slice that could make his plan free instead of self-funded.

_rec.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. The 2026 intake round opened in autumn 2025. Expect the round for a September 2027 start to open around October–November 2026 — i.e. within months of now. He should be monitoring resound-ma.eu from October 2026.

_rec.facilities: Lisbon semester: Lusófona's professional multitrack studios, acoustic laboratories, cinema post-production and 3D Atmos room. Dublin: IADT's media production facilities. Vilnius: LMTA. Plus the FilmEU alliance network of artists, producers and researchers across Europe.
_rec.visaEligible: YES, and better than a single-country route in one respect: Erasmus Mundus students receive structured institutional support for visas at each partner, and the €1,400/month stipend comfortably satisfies proof-of-means tests. Counterpoint: three separate immigration processes in two years is administratively heavy for a Tunisian passport holder, and Ireland is outside Schengen — factor in Irish immigration (IRP) separately from the Schengen leg.
_rec.reputationSignals: European Commission selection and funding; FilmEU European University alliance membership; three national accreditations; capped at 24 students a year (so genuinely small cohorts); explicit English-medium delivery. This is the most prestigious sound qualification reachable through a private Portuguese institution. No red flags found. The only structural caveat is that only ONE of four semesters is actually in Portugal, so if his goal is to establish himself in Lisbon specifically, this scatters him across three countries.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: With an Erasmus Mundus scholarship: effectively €0 tuition and a net-positive €1,400/month. Without a scholarship: €15,000 tuition + roughly €14,400–€24,000 living over 24 months + relocation/permits, i.e. a realistic all-in €31,000–€42,000 over two years.
_rec.recommendation: APPLY. THIS IS HIS SINGLE HIGHEST-VALUE SHOT IN THE PORTUGUESE SLICE — and the only one that is taught in English and can be fully funded. The maths is decisive: an Erasmus Mundus scholarship converts a €30k+ plan into a funded one with a €1,400/month stipend, which for a budget-sensitive Tunisian self-payer is transformative. But be blunt with him about the odds and the work: 24 places, worldwide competition, and an admission clause that requires 'relevant prior experience' he does not yet have. His concrete twelve-month plan should be (1) book IELTS now and clear 6.0 in every band — or verify his BSc's English-medium waiver; (2) build the three portfolio pieces the spec asks for, at 10–15 minutes total, ideally one released track, one piece of sound-to-picture, and one audio-software/interactive piece that leverages his engineering background as a differentiator rather than a liability; (3) secure two recommenders now; (4) watch for the call opening around October 2026. If he only does one thing from this entire Portugal report, it should be this application — with UCP Porto and Lusófona's own mestrado as the paid fallbacks.

_rec.program: Medialogy (Copenhagen) — MSc, with specialisation in Sound and Music Computing (CORRECTION: NOT closed — it survives as a specialisation, not a standalone degree)
_rec.university: Aalborg University (AAU), Copenhagen campus
_rec.degree: MSc (cand.scient. in Medialogy). Sound and Music Computing is an officially published specialisation chosen after the 1st semester — the diploma is Medialogy, the specialisation is the track.
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS (4 semesters). Confirmed on the official page: "Specialiseringen i Sound and Music Computing på Aalborg Universitet består af fire semestre (120 ECTS-point)".
_rec.focus: Sound Design + Immersive Audio + Electronic/interactive audio (sonic interaction design, spatial audio for VR/AR, machine learning for sound). This is the CS-to-audio bridge — engineering and interaction-design framing, not music-conservatory craft.
_rec.institutionType: Public university (problem-based learning / group project model)
_rec.language: English. Confirmed: the Medialogy Copenhagen page lists "Engelsk" as Sprog, and the specialisation page states "2-årig specialisering / Engelsk". (The AAU website itself is Danish; teaching is English.)
_rec.tuitionIntl: 57,850 DKK / EUR 7,745 PER SEMESTER for non-EU/EEA students, listed explicitly as "Medialogy (Copenhagen)" in the official 2026 tuition table. That is roughly EUR 30,980 / 231,400 DKK for the full 2-year degree. Plus a non-refundable application fee of EUR 150 (1,150 DKK) for non-EU/EEA applicants, which covers up to 3 AAU applications and is refunded if he enrols.
_rec.fundingLevel: Full (competitive, scarce) or None. There is no partial tier.
_rec.scholarship: Danish Government Scholarships administered by AAU. Official wording: "Each September intake, Aalborg University grants a limited number of scholarships to individually selected applicants from non-EU/EEA countries based on strategic considerations and academic qualifications... All non-EU applicants are automatically considered when applying to a master's programme. Therefore, it is not possible to apply for a scholarship separately." A Tunisian national is eligible. BUT: "approximately 15 each year" for the ENTIRE university, and AAU explicitly warns "We do not advise you to rely solely on receiving a scholarship".
_rec.stipend: A scholarship = full tuition-fee waiver PLUS a monthly living stipend. 2026 rate: 11,225 DKK / EUR 1,503 per month, paid for four semesters. Possibly taxable. Decision communicated by early July at the latest; if he has already paid tuition it is refunded.
_rec.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree. Three bachelors are pre-approved as directly qualifying: BSc Medialogy (Aalborg or Copenhagen) and BSc Engineering (Electronic Engineering / Electronic Systems Engineering) at AAU. Everyone else is individually assessed against explicit ECTS thresholds: "Minimum 10 ECTS i Programming", "Minimum 10 ECTS i technical knowledge behind media technologies", "Minimum 10 ECTS i methods within Interaction Design/User Experience Design". CRITICAL WARNING, quoted: "Bemærk, at det ikke er muligt at supplere fag for at opfylde adgangskravene" — it is NOT possible to take top-up courses to meet the entry requirements. Also: no pre-assessment is offered ("Der foretages ikke forhåndsvurderinger"). English at Danish B-level required, evidenced by upper-secondary certificate or an accepted English test. The programme is capacity-capped (adgangsbegrænset): Medialogy Copenhagen offered 33 places in 2025, and qualified applicants are ranked by (1) bachelor grades, (2) a max 1-page English statement of relevance/motivation and knowledge of the programme — where he may indicate he wants the Sound and Music Computing specialisation, and (3) documented relevant activity such as work experience in IT, media production, programming, sound or film.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — emphatically. This is an engineering/media-technology master and no music qualification is asked for anywhere. The risk runs the other way: his BSc Software Engineering will clear the 10 ECTS Programming bar easily, but he must be able to point to 10 ECTS of media-technology content AND 10 ECTS of Interaction Design / UX methods in his SMU MedTech transcript, and he cannot make up a shortfall afterwards. He should map his transcript against those three lines before anything else.
_rec.portfolioSpec: No creative portfolio required. The only written submission is the ranking-criterion statement: an English text of maximum 1 page covering relevance to his future career goals, his reasons for applying, and his knowledge of the programme — plus documentation of relevant activities/work experience. Uploads: bachelor diploma and full transcript (or transcript to date if not yet graduated), and English B-level documentation.
_rec.auditionSpec: None. No audition, no interview, no on-site test. Selection is entirely on documents and grade ranking.
_rec.applicationOpens: The application portal (Ansøgningsportalen) opens "medio december" — mid-December — for the following September intake. For a September 2027 start that means roughly mid-December 2026. This is a published standing rule, not a one-off date.
_rec.deadline: 1 March at 23:59 for a September start — published as a standing annual rule on AAU's official 'Ansøgning og frister' page ("Du skal søge senest den 1. marts kl. 23.59, hvis du vil optages til september"), with decisions by 10 June at the latest and any leftover places advertised mid-June on a first-come-first-served basis. So for September 2027: apply by 1 March 2027. Re-confirm in late 2026, but this is a stable rule rather than a lapsed cycle date. He may apply to a maximum of 3 AAU masters per intake.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Semester 1: project 'Adaptive Media Systems' plus 'Machine Learning for Media Experiences', choosing two electives from Sound and Music Perception and Cognition (recommended for this specialisation), Real-Time Computer Graphics, Mobile and Wearable Computing, Narratives in Interactive Systems. Semester 2: project 'Immersive Sonic Experiences' plus the course 'Sonic Interaction Design', with two electives from Multi-Sensory Interaction and Media Cognition, Signal Processing for Interactive Systems, Embodied Interaction, Spatial User Interfaces, Game Research and Development. Semester 3: a company internship, DADIU Game Production (the Danish national game-production programme), a regular project, or a semester abroad. Semester 4: thesis only. Everything is problem-based group project work. Honest framing for him: this is audio ENGINEERING and interaction design — spatial audio, VR/AR sound, AI for sound, new interfaces for musical expression — not beat-making, mixing records or DJ craft.
_rec.facilities: The Multi-sensory Experience Lab is attached to the programme and is named on the official page in a student testimonial as offering "ekstraordinære faciliteter" for spatial audio in VR. Named employer/industry pipeline on the official page: Bang & Olufsen, T-Rex Engineering, IO Interactive, Carl Martin, Dicentia. Semester 3 can be spent inside DADIU, the Danish national game-production consortium.
_rec.fitNotes: The previous entry's claim that this programme is dead is WRONG and must be corrected before he sees it. The old standalone smc.aau.dk / 'Sound and Music Computing' master URL does redirect into AAU's 'programmes without admission' area, which is what caused the false negative — but the content has moved: it is now a live 2-year, 120-ECTS, English-taught specialisation inside the MSc Medialogy at the Copenhagen campus, and it is open for application. This remains the single most natural destination in this whole slice for a computer-science graduate who wants to work in sound. Two real obstacles: (1) the hard ECTS gate — 10 ECTS each of programming, media technology and interaction design/UX, with no possibility of topping up, and no pre-assessment, so he is guessing until he submits; (2) money — EUR 7,745 per semester, about EUR 31,000 all in, with the only escape being one of roughly 15 government scholarships awarded across the whole university, which do at least pay tuition in full plus about EUR 1,500 a month. It will not, on its own, make him a DJ or a record producer; it will make him someone who can build audio technology and design interactive sound.
_rec.verificationNotes: sourceUrl CORRECTED. Verified directly on the live official AAU pages: the specialisation page (curriculum, 120 ECTS, English, entry ECTS thresholds, ranking criteria, 33 places), the parent Medialogy Copenhagen page (Copenhagen, English, 2 years, September start), AAU's official master admission-and-deadlines page (1 March deadline, portal opens mid-December, decision by 10 June), and AAU's official English 'Finance and fees' page (Medialogy Copenhagen listed at 57,850 DKK / EUR 7,745 per semester for 2026; EUR 150 application fee; Danish Government Scholarship terms and the 11,225 DKK monthly stipend rate). _rec.university: BIMM University
_rec.city: Berlin, Dublin, London, Brighton, Bristol, Birmingham, Manchester — all seven confirmed on the course page
_rec.degree: MA Popular Music Practice — CONFIRMED verbatim 'Awarding institution: BIMM University'. BIMM holds its own UK degree-awarding powers, so this is a genuine university master's rather than a validated diploma, including at the Berlin and Dublin campuses.

_rec.tuitionIntl: MAJOR CORRECTION — the Berlin and Dublin figures are now VERIFIED, resolving the biggest open question. UK CAMPUSES: UK/Irish £9,950 full-time (£4,975/yr part-time); EU/EEA/Swiss and non-EU both list at £15,950/yr, with an automatic £6,000/yr discount for EU/EEA/Swiss passport holders (not him) and a £2,000 Early Acceptance Discount for non-EU students who accept and pay the deposit by the published date — so c. £13,950 net for him. BERLIN (bimm-institute.de): German/EU/EEA/Swiss/UK €11,950/yr, International/Non-EU €16,950/yr with a €4,000 deposit, less the €2,000 Early Acceptance Discount = c. €14,950 net. DUBLIN (bimm.ie): EU/IE €8,450/yr, International €16,950/yr. So Berlin is cheaper than the UK campus but NOT dramatically so — the earlier assumption that the German operation would be materially lower is only partly right. Deposits: UK £4,000 self-funded / £1,000 if government-funded; Berlin €4,000 non-EU / €1,000 EU. Berlin remaining balance due 8 weeks before start; a payment plan spreads the balance over 8 monthly instalments Sept-April.
_rec.scholarship: MAJOR CORRECTION — BIMM's current scholarships page lists only THREE awards, not the long portfolio previously reported. (1) Launchpad Bursary — a tuition reduction for the duration of study, but only 10 students per year and explicitly 'across BIMM Music Institute's UK campuses', so it does NOT apply to Berlin or Dublin. (2) Open Day, Audition & Interview Travel Bursary — UK travel only. (3) Fair Access Fund — UNDERGRADUATE students only. The IDLES, Joan Armatrading, Fatboy Slim/Martlets, Jim Aiken, MusicMaker, Black Music Coalition x Wretch 32, Universal Music UK Sound Foundation and Creative Futures Bursary awards are NOT on the current page — treat them as lapsed. The International Hardship Bursary is confirmed CLOSED. BIMM Berlin states outright: 'BIMM University Berlin does not offer scholarships directly.' BUT Berlin signposts an external option he can genuinely use: the SBW Berlin Scholarship for International Students, which may cover shared student housing, a monthly living allowance, tuition fee support and travel assistance, for applicants aged 18-30 who show academic capability, financial need and social/community engagement; applications accepted year-round with no fees. The Creative Futures Discount (£1,000/€1,000) is BIMM-alumni-only and does not apply to him.
_rec.fundingLevel: Partial at best. No BIMM award is open to him at Berlin or Dublin; the only BIMM lever is the £2,000/€2,000 Early Acceptance Discount, which is a discount not a scholarship. The external SBW Berlin Scholarship for International Students is the one genuine funding avenue and is worth pursuing early.
_rec.stipend: No BIMM stipend or housing. The external SBW Berlin scholarship may include housing and a monthly living allowance — UNVERIFIED as to amounts and success rates.
_rec.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED verbatim: 'A good degree (normally 2.2 or above) or significant experience in a relevant field.' And: 'Overseas students for whom English is not their native language may be required to meet a minimum English language requirement of an Academic IELTS 6.5. We require a minimum of 6.0 to be achieved in each band.' And: 'All applicants will be subject to interview and a portfolio may also be requested for Recognition of Prior Certified or Experiential Learning (RPCEL).' Contextual offers with reduced entry requirements exist for applicants meeting certain criteria. Tunisia does NOT appear in BIMM's international entry-requirements country table — he must email admissions for an equivalency ruling on the SMU MedTech BSc.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — the most permissive degree-subject wording of any real master's in this slice. The requirement is 'a good degree (normally 2.2 or above)' with NO subject restriction stated anywhere on the page; the alternative is 'significant experience in a relevant field'. A software-engineering BSc satisfies the letter of the requirement. The real filter is the compulsory interview, not the degree subject.
_rec.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED verbatim and CONDITIONAL, not automatic: 'All applicants will be subject to interview and a portfolio may also be requested for Recognition of Prior Certified or Experiential Learning (RPCEL).' A portfolio is therefore requested when prior learning needs accrediting, not as standard. No number of works, duration or format is published — UNVERIFIED. In practice, for a Production-specialism applicant with no music degree, expect to be asked for a demo, so build one regardless.
_rec.auditionSpec: INTERVIEW IS MANDATORY for every applicant — verbatim: 'All applicants will be subject to interview.' No instrumental audition for the MA. Whether the interview runs online from Tunisia is not stated on the page — UNVERIFIED, but BIMM operates an international agent network and offers a UK travel bursary specifically for people attending auditions and interviews in person, implying both modes exist. Confirm remote interviewing with admissions.
_rec.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED. Postgraduate entry is Apply Direct, not UCAS. BIMM Berlin's site currently shows a 'Final Application Deadline – 12 August' banner for the in-progress cycle, indicating a late-summer close in Berlin.
_rec.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. No MA application deadline is published for the UK campuses; admissions appear rolling. Two dated anchors in the current cycle: the Early Acceptance Discount cut-off of 06 August 2026 for non-EU students (worth £2,000 / €2,000, applies at UK, Berlin and Dublin), and BIMM Berlin's advertised final application deadline of 12 August. Expect equivalent early- to mid-August 2027 dates. Note Berlin also requires the balance of fees 8 weeks before the course starts.
_rec.facilities: 'Fantastic studio facilities and industry-leading lecturers' for the Production specialism — named consoles, Atmos or immersive rooms are NOT published, UNVERIFIED. Geography is the real asset: BIMM Berlin sits in the world's densest electronic-music scene with no UK visa needed; BIMM Dublin is inside the EU. Confirmed subject areas across the institute include Music Production alongside performance disciplines.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Five modules across three trimesters, CONFIRMED: Popular Music Practice and Research (theory applied to your practice, research training, one-to-one mentoring); You and the Popular Music Industry (refine direction, audit skills, audience/market research, liaise with industry stakeholders); Popular Music & Technology (technology's role in creative practice and entrepreneurship, mentoring and workshops); Exploring Collaborative Practice (negotiation, leadership, teamwork; curate a symposium or run group project work); Major Project (the extended culminating piece). The Production specialism is described verbatim as: 'specialising in production will stretch your skills in recording, mixing, mastering and more. Get involved in extraordinary recording projects and build your portfolio for a sustainable career.'
_rec.fitNotes: Still the best combination of accessibility and geography in this slice, and the Berlin fee question is now answered: c. €14,950/yr net after the Early Acceptance Discount, versus c. £13,950 in the UK — Berlin is cheaper and avoids the UK visa entirely, but it is not the bargain that was hoped. Strengths: any bachelor subject at 2:2 is acceptable, IELTS 6.5 is attainable with preparation, English-taught in Berlin, 90 ECTS, portfolio only conditional, and the same BIMM University award in Berlin, Dublin or the UK. Weaknesses: no BIMM scholarship reaches a non-EU student at Berlin or Dublin (Launchpad is UK-only, Fair Access is undergraduate-only), the interview is mandatory and is the real gate, and this is a project-supervision MA culminating in a Major Project rather than a taught mixing curriculum — he must arrive already able to produce. Chase the external SBW Berlin Scholarship for International Students; it is the only route to meaningful funding here.

CONFIRMED: all seven campuses, 180 FHEQ / 90 ECTS, BIMM University as awarding institution, English language of study, verbatim entry and interview wording, IELTS 6.5 with 6.0 per band, conditional RPCEL portfolio, the full five-module structure, the Production specialism wording, UK PG fees (£9,950 home / £15,950 international), Berlin PG fees (€11,950 EU / €16,950 non-EU, €4,000 deposit), Dublin PG fees (€8,450 EU / €16,950 international), the £2,000/€2,000 Early Acceptance Discount with a 06 August 2026 cut-off, and the reduced current scholarship list.
