_rec.program: Music Composition MA/M.Mus
_rec.university: Iceland University of the Arts / Iceland Academy of the Arts (Listaháskóli Íslands, LHÍ), Department of Music
_rec.institutionType: Art school / self-owned university of the arts
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS — NOW CONFIRMED on the official programme page (previously logged as UNVERIFIED)
_rec.language: English — NOW CONFIRMED: "Program information is provided in English, as the language of MA program in composition is English" and "The Master Program of Composition is an international program conducted in English."
_rec.focus: Art-music composition (contemporary classical), with an electronic-composition and sound-art application stream and a sound-technology course in the core
_rec.whatYouStudy: "The international MA program in composition enables the student to develop his/her artistic and theoretical activity in a stimulating creative and critical environment, with access to the staff's wide professional experience and theoretical knowledge and supported by an inspiring learning community." Structure, per the official page: one-to-one private lessons with a composition tutor plus collective composition classes; "the subject of composition is by far the largest item in the syllabus, generating almost half the credits in the first three terms"; first two terms also carry "a course in sound technology, either electronic or instrumental, a course on artistic research, a course on music analysis and an introduction to some recent issues [in] music composition", plus electives. Weekly seminars analyse notable compositions and discuss students' research. The school "collaborates with professional musicians who give workshops where students' works are heard and discussed". Master's project options: (a) 20-credit composition + 10-credit paper, (b) 10-credit composition + 20-credit paper, or (c) a 26-credit practical project + a 4-credit reflection. CONFIRMED on the official page (previously flagged as aggregator-sourced): "Students are offered the opportunity to have their final project performed by the Caput Ensemble at a graduation concert." No PhD in music yet, though one is in development.
_rec.entryRequirements: NOW PUBLISHED AND CONFIRMED (previously logged as UNVERIFIED). General: "a bachelor's degree or equivalent university education that supports the applicant's ability to meet the [demands] of the MA Program", with certified academic transcripts. Programme-specific: "Applicants will have completed a BA degree in composition or the related fields of music theory or the arts. Non musical academic degrees are not excluded, especially on graduate and doctoral levels. Applicants who do not have a BA degree in composition can be recommended to the program provided they demonstrate a comparable knowledge, experience and technical ability in the field of musical composition." Language: "Students must be proficient in spoken and written English in the academic context. In case the admission committee has doubts regarding the applicant's competence, he/she may be required to submit evidence of English proficiency" — so no blanket IELTS/TOEFL requirement, but a test can be demanded. Documents: certified degree certificate(s) and transcript(s) (PDF); ONE reference, max one page, submitted directly by the referee via an emailed link (waived for former LHÍ students); letter of motivation in English (PDF); CV in English (PDF); portfolio. Non-refundable application fee ISK 5,000, payable per application; the application is not valid until both submitted and paid.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: TECHNICALLY YES, PRACTICALLY DEMANDING. Quoted: "Non musical academic degrees are not excluded, especially on graduate and doctoral levels." But the same paragraph sets the real bar: an applicant without a BA in composition must "demonstrate a comparable knowledge, experience and technical ability in the field of musical composition" — i.e. the door is open only if the portfolio performs at conservatory-graduate level. With no music degree, no conservatory training and no professional audio experience, he would be asked to evidence exactly what he does not yet have. The sibling MMus in New Audiences and Innovative Practice (NAIP), described on the department page as suitable for musicians from diverse backgrounds with "innovative and interdisciplinary approaches to creating and communicating music", is the more permissive door — but it carries the identical Department of Music tuition, which is the real blocker.
_rec.portfolioSpec: NOW PUBLISHED AND CONFIRMED (previously UNVERIFIED). Item 5, "Portfolio of works (PDF/URL)", compulsory: "Portfolio of 5 scores with or without audio files are required for applications in instrumental composition. Applicants in electronic composition and sound art must submit 5 works. Applicants for interdisciplinary studies (composing for film, theater etc.) must submit 5 original works." So his route would be the electronic-composition/sound-art stream: FIVE works, no notation obligation on that stream. No per-work duration, no audio format and no total runtime cap are specified. Submitted as PDF or URL.
_rec.auditionSpec: NO live audition and no on-site entrance test published. "An admission committee assesses applications on the grounds of assessment of the subject material, the applicant's motivation and aim with the study at the Iceland University of the Arts and the interview(s) with the applicant." Interview(s) form part of selection; the mode is not stated, so confirm whether they are held remotely. Additional risk on the official page: "If the number of applicants meeting the admission requirements for the study program falls below the minimum threshold, the program will not be offered for the upcoming academic year."
_rec.tuitionIntl: BLOCKING FINDING — the amount is now published and it is very large. From LHÍ's tuition-fee page, for the academic year 2026-2027, non-EEA students pay per academic year: Department of Music ISK 5,500,000 (also Performing Arts and Film ISK 5,500,000; Architecture, Fine Art, Design and Arts Education ISK 4,500,000). ISK 5,500,000 is roughly EUR 37,000-38,000 per year at mid-2026 rates, i.e. on the order of EUR 75,000 for the two-year MA — indicative conversion, verify at the time. LHÍ states the fees "reflect the actual cost of the studies and the amount may change between academic years", are charged in ISK by bank transfer, are non-refundable, and "must be paid in full before enrolment or continuation of studies can be confirmed. Failure to pay on time or in full may result in the loss of the study place." The ISK 100,000 annual registration fee does NOT rescue him: it applies to "students with citizenship within the EEA, the Faroe Islands, Greenland and Switzerland as well as all students regardless of nationality who started studying at LHÍ in the fall of 2025 or earlier." Only two exemptions exist, neither of which he meets: holding an Icelandic permanent residence permit (or one that can lead to it), or studying at LHÍ via an international university cooperation project, cooperation programme or university network. Separate application fee ISK 5,000, non-refundable, per application, not deducted from any other fee.
_rec.scholarship: None — and this is now an explicit institutional statement, not an absence of evidence. LHÍ's tuition-fee page: "IUA does not provide any scholarships for [tuition] fees or living expenses."
_rec.stipend: None. Beyond tuition, LHÍ tells non-EEA students to budget for "study materials, equipment, and supplies", insurance, and living expenses in Iceland — one of the most expensive countries in Europe.
_rec.applicationOpens: 14 January 2026 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date (expect approximately mid-January 2027 for a September 2027 start, but this must be reconfirmed; nothing for the 2027 intake is published as of July 2026)
_rec.deadline: 2 March 2026, with results announced April 2026 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Only the 2026-intake cycle is published (open 14 Jan 2026, deadline 2 Mar 2026, answered Apr 2026). For a September 2027 start expect roughly mid-January to early March 2027, unconfirmed. The upside relative to Aalto is a much later and longer window; the downside is that it is irrelevant unless the funding problem is solved.
_rec.verificationNotes: SOURCE URL CORRECTED — the previous URL (the department landing page, https://www.lhi.is/en/music-department/) carries almost no decision-relevant detail; the actual programme page is https://www.lhi.is/en/namsleid/tonsmidar-ma/ and it is comprehensive. Fees confirmed at https://www.lhi.is/en/about-lhi/free/tuition-fee/ and https://www.lhi.is/en/about-lhi/free/ (note: the previously circulating URLs https://www.lhi.is/en/tuition-fees and https://www.lhi.is/en/um-lhi/skrasetningargjald/ now both return HTTP 404 — the site has been restructured). Nearly every field previously marked UNVERIFIED is now resolved: 120 ECTS over 4 semesters, English-language, full admission requirements, the exact five-work portfolio spec, interview-based (no audition) selection, the full application cycle, and — decisively — the non-EEA tuition figure. Caveat on wording: LHÍ's English pages are machine-translated and contain obvious artefacts ("tuition feels", "competition fee", "enforcement" for enrolment); the substance is unambiguous but exact phrasing should be reconfirmed against the Icelandic pages or with registration@lhi.is. STILL UNVERIFIED: whether the interview can be conducted remotely; whether non-EEA students also owe the ISK 100,000 registration fee on top of tuition; whether the ISK 5,500,000 figure will be revised for 2027-2028 (LHÍ warns it "may change between academic years"); and the full admission detail for the sibling NAIP MMus.
_rec.fitNotes: DOWNGRADED TO C — this is now a confirmed financial dead end, not merely an unverified one. LHÍ has published the number the earlier record could not find: from autumn 2026 a non-EEA student in the Department of Music pays ISK 5,500,000 per academic year, roughly EUR 37,000-38,000, about EUR 75,000 across the MA, with tuition due in full before enrolment can be confirmed, no refunds, and the institution stating flat out that it offers no scholarships for tuition or living costs — in Iceland, one of Europe's most expensive countries. The only two exemptions are Icelandic residency and inbound exchange/network mobility; neither is available to him as a direct-entry Tunisian applicant. Set the money aside and the fit is still weak: it is a contemporary art-music composition MA built around private composition tutorials, score-based work and a Caput Ensemble graduation concert, with electronics as one course and one application stream. The published entry rule is honest about the bar — a non-composition bachelor is "not excluded" but must "demonstrate a comparable knowledge, experience and technical ability in the field of musical composition", which is precisely the evidence he cannot produce this cycle. There is one genuine positive to bank: the electronic-composition and sound-art portfolio route asks for five works with no notation requirement, which is a spec he could realistically meet in a year — the same five-work package would serve the Aalto portfolio. Recommendation: do not apply. If Iceland matters for non-academic reasons, email lhi@lhi.is and registration@lhi.is to check whether the NAIP MMus route or any Erasmus/network mobility arrangement could bring him in under the cooperation-programme exemption, since that is the only published mechanism that removes the fee.

If he is set on SAE-style training, the honest comparison is that the Conservatorium van Amsterdam's AEMA associate degree (public, English-taught, electronic-music focused, and CAN sponsor a visa) does the same job for a fraction of the price. Cross this off.

Semester 1: Digital Audio Processing 7.5, Audio Application Programming 7.5, General Acoustics 7.5, Sound Synthesis 7.5 = 30 ECTS. Semester 2: Special Topics in Acoustics 7.5, Applied Machine Learning for Sound and Music 7.5, Sound and Movement 7.5, Optoacoustics 7.5 = 30 ECTS. Semester 3: thesis 30 ECTS. _rec.focus: Recording and audio engineering, sound synthesis and sound design, digital audio processing, machine learning for sound and music, acoustics and optoacoustics, motion-based interaction
_rec.whatYouStudy: Verified from the official call and the department pages. The programme "explores sound in its multiple dimensions: as a wave, as a signal, and as a carrier of information", combining applied knowledge with current research in digital audio processing, sound synthesis, acoustics and audiovisual technologies, artificial intelligence, and motion tracking for musical applications. The eight compulsory courses: DIGITAL AUDIO PROCESSING — PCM, sampling-rate conversion, spectral analysis, digital filters, noise minimisation, audio coding and decoding; AUDIO APPLICATION PROGRAMMING — building audio and music applications for capture, recording, spectral analysis and signal extraction in Python or C with specialised APIs; GENERAL ACOUSTICS; SOUND SYNTHESIS — advanced synthesis and modulation techniques, computer implementation and their application to contemporary music creation; SPECIAL TOPICS IN ACOUSTICS — musical, structural and psycho-acoustics, electroacoustics, computational acoustics; APPLIED MACHINE LEARNING FOR SOUND AND MUSIC — inferring music content information and sound-scene and event detection for intelligent applications; SOUND AND MOVEMENT — embodied music cognition, multimodality in audio interaction, correlating audio and motion data, and building interactive sound systems in which motion drives sound; OPTOACOUSTICS — optical detection of sound, light-generated sound sources, micro- and nano-acoustics. The thesis may be carried out in one of the collaborating laboratories in Greece or abroad. Weekly timetable for the current year runs Monday and Wednesday afternoons and evenings, 14:15–22:00.
_rec.entryRequirements: NOW VERIFIED from the 2026-27 call, and better for him than previously recorded. Admitted, after selection, are graduates of: Faculties of Natural Sciences; POLYTECHNIC (ENGINEERING) SCHOOLS; TEI Engineering; Sound Technology and Musical Instruments T.E. and Traditional and Folk Music T.E.; Music Studies (and Ethnomusicology), Audio and Visual Arts, Journalism and Media; and Cultural Technology and Communication. "Επιπλέον στο ΠΜΣ γίνονται δεκτοί απόφοιτοι τμημάτων που είναι αντίστοιχα των παραπάνω και ανήκουν σε ομοταγή ιδρύματα της αλλοδαπής" — graduates of corresponding departments at equivalent foreign institutions are also admitted, and "Για άλλες περιπτώσεις υποψηφίων και για τη συνάφεια των ειδικοτήτων θα αποφασίζει κατά περίπτωση η Συνέλευση του Τμήματος". Required documents: two-sided copy of ID or PASSPORT; CV; degree copy and other qualifications, or a completion certificate; full undergraduate transcript; an English language certificate at level B2 or above; copies of publications and/or evidence of professional experience if any; TWO recommendation letters (or a statement of the reasons if they cannot be supplied, e.g. time constraints); and a short report of no more than one typed page on his scientific and professional interests with a clear statement of why he wants to take the programme.
_rec.portfolioSpec: None. No portfolio is required or mentioned anywhere in the official call. The only creative/professional evidence sought is optional: copies of scientific publications and/or proof of professional experience "εφόσον υπάρχουν" — if they exist.
_rec.auditionSpec: No audition and no written entrance examination. "Η διαδικασία επιλογής υποψηφίων περιλαμβάνει, μεταξύ άλλων, και προσωπική συνέντευξη, η οποία μπορεί, αν συντρέχουν λόγοι, να γίνει εξ' αποστάσεως" — the selection process includes a personal interview which may, where warranted, be held remotely. Evaluation takes place after the application deadline on a date depending on the number of candidates. Maximum intake 15 students per year.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Yes, and this is now confirmed rather than inferred. Graduates of Polytechnic (engineering) schools and Faculties of Natural Sciences head the eligible list, and corresponding foreign departments are expressly included. A Tunisian BSc in Software Engineering from an engineering school is a natural fit for that category, with the Department Assembly ruling case by case on the relatedness of the specialisation. No special pleading and no music background needed.

_rec.scholarship: Not applicable to tuition, which is already zero and where every student holds nominal scholar status. No living-cost scholarship is published. _rec.stipend: None. The programme charges nothing but pays nothing. He would self-fund living costs in Rethymno, which are among the lowest in this slice, with the free-meals card and subsidised halls materially reducing them if he qualifies.

For his SEPTEMBER 2027 target: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date, but the pattern is a late-April opening with an early-September close, so expect roughly late April to 7 September 2027.
_rec.facilities: Department of Music Technology and Acoustics, operating since September 1999, within the School of Music and Optoacoustic Technologies established in Rethymno in 2019 — described as the only academic programme in Greece dedicated to sound and music technologies combined with the science of acoustics. Named teaching staff include Assoc. Prof. Chrysoula Alexandraki (programme director, Digital Audio Processing), Assoc. Prof. Maximos Kaliakatsos-Papakostas (Audio Application Programming, also department chair), Asst. Prof. Nikos Stefanakis (General Acoustics), Nikolas Valsamakis (Sound Synthesis) and Asst. Prof. Panagiota-Styliani Paschalidou. The thesis may be done in a collaborating laboratory in Greece or abroad. A doctoral programme covers the same fields. HMU student welfare provides a free-meals card and a student residence. UNVERIFIED: studio and console inventory.
_rec.fitNotes: The strongest pure-funding case in the slice, and verification improved it on several fronts the prior record had marked as unknown: engineering graduates head the eligible-degree list, there is no portfolio and no audition, the interview can be held remotely, two recommendation letters and a one-page statement are the only written work required, and the sole language certificate demanded is ENGLISH at B2 — Greek is never mentioned as a requirement. Tuition is zero, Rethymno is cheap, and subsidised meals and housing exist. His software background maps directly onto Audio Application Programming, Applied Machine Learning for Sound and Music, and Sound and Movement. Three real obstacles. FIRST, the language of instruction is not published and the courses are timetabled in Greek — he must email the department (chrisoula@hmu.gr, maximoskp@hmu.gr, or the secretariat at ngoniota@hmu.gr) and get a straight answer before committing. SECOND, applications are submitted through morpheus.hmu.gr using TaxisNet credentials, which are Greek tax-authority login codes a Tunisian applicant does not have — he must ask the secretariat for the alternative route for foreign applicants, and should do so early. THIRD, only 15 places, attendance is compulsory and in person with a maximum of three absences per course, and the content is DSP, acoustics and machine learning rather than production or DJing — this would make him an audio engineer or audio-software specialist, not a producer. Worth pursuing as the free, funded, engineering-friendly option, but the language and TaxisNet questions must be settled first.

_rec.institution: Netherlands private higher-education sector (systematic check across NVAO/CROHO-registered private institutions and all named specialist audio providers)
_rec.qualification: NONE EXISTS. After searching in both English and Dutch ('master muziekproductie', 'opleiding sound design particulier', 'niet-bekostigde opleiding', 'master sound design Nederland particuliere hogeschool NVAO'), I found NO privately-run, NVAO-accredited master's degree in sound design, music production, audio engineering, music technology, immersive audio or electronic music performance anywhere in the Netherlands.
_rec.accreditationStatus: DEFINITIVE STRUCTURAL FINDING. In the Netherlands the audio/music education market splits cleanly in two, with nothing in between. (1) ACCREDITED = PUBLIC. Every NVAO-accredited master in this field belongs to a government-funded ('bekostigd') public institution: HKU Utrecht (Master of Music pathway Music Design; Sound Design and Audio Design at bachelor level), Conservatorium van Amsterdam / AHK (Master Immersive Audio — NVAO-assessed; plus the AEMA associate degree for electronic musicians, English-taught), Codarts Rotterdam, and the Institute of Sonology at the Royal Conservatoire in The Hague. These are all excluded from this brief as public. (2) PRIVATE = UNACCREDITED. Every private audio provider in the country (SAE, Abbey Road Institute, Sound Education, Pro Audio Education, DDMA, Master The Mix, AV Sound Education, DJ School Amsterdam, Music Production Academy) holds at most CRKBO and/or NRTO registration. CRKBO is a short-vocational-education register that governs VAT exemption; NRTO is a private-training trade association quality mark. NEITHER IS AN ACCREDITATION AND NEITHER CONFERS DEGREE STATUS. The sole exception — SAE's MA/MSc — is a UK University of Hertfordshire award delivered fully online, with no Dutch status and no campus component. Meanwhile private institutions that DO hold NVAO accreditation (Tio, Wittenborg, Nyenrode) operate exclusively in business and hospitality.

_rec.scholarships: SECTOR-WIDE FINDING: NOT ONE private Dutch audio provider publishes any scholarship, bursary, fee waiver or discount available to a non-EU or Tunisian applicant. The only financial mechanisms found were (a) upfront-payment savings of €1,300–€5,670 versus instalment plans, (b) alumni/staff discounts of 25% at SAE UK, (c) 35–50% student software discounts at Sound Education and AV Sound Education, and (d) a Dutch study-cost INCOME TAX deduction promoted by Abbey Road Institute and Pro Audio Education, which requires Dutch taxable income and by Abbey Road's own admission 'doesn't apply to those receiving governmental benefits or who aren't yet employed'. That last one is effectively worthless to an incoming international student and should be discounted entirely when comparing prices. Dutch DUO student finance is unavailable at every private provider without exception.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: For orientation: private Dutch audio tuition ranges from €699 (SAE one-month DJ Certificate) to €37,580 (SAE BA Audio Production Standard, monthly plan). The mid-market one-year full-time option is Abbey Road Institute at €18,860–€20,160. Amsterdam living costs add roughly €14,000–€18,000 per year on top.
_rec.visaEligible: THE DECISIVE FINDING FOR THIS CANDIDATE — NO. Only an IND recognised sponsor can apply for a Dutch student residence permit on a student's behalf, and the IND study register covers higher professional/university education, senior secondary vocational education (ROCs) and IB schools. NOT ONE private specialist audio provider in the Netherlands is a recognised sponsor. Both of the two credible English-language schools say so themselves, in writing: SAE Institute Netherlands states 'SAE is a private Institute, its students are not eligible for a Visa, nor a student loan via DUO' and 'The registration at SAE Institute cannot grant you a Student Visa in the Netherlands'; Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam states 'Currently, we are not able to assist non-EU residents with their visa application to study in the Netherlands' and 'Since Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam is a private Institute, students are not eligible for a VISA or a student loan', adding that applicants may only attend if they already have 'a personal means of obtaining a VISA, for example, a family connection or registration at a university'. CONCLUSION: a Tunisian national CANNOT legally relocate to the Netherlands to study at any private audio school. Verify current status yourself at https://ind.nl/en/public-register-recognised-sponsors/public-register-study (updated monthly).
_rec.reputationSignals: The Dutch private audio market is small, expensive and structurally unable to serve non-EU students. The two brands worth respecting on teaching quality — SAE Institute Amsterdam and Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam — both disclose their inability to sponsor visas only in fine print (an entry-requirements sub-page and an FAQ respectively) while running international-facing marketing. That is the sector's central red flag. A second recurring red flag is nomenclature: Pro Audio Education titles its diploma 'Master Geluidstechniek' for what it concedes is MBO+/HBO- level work, and 'Master The Mix Academy' will surface in any search for a music-production master. Neither is a master's degree. A third is opacity: three providers (Master The Mix, AV Sound Education, Music Production Academy) publish no prices at all.
_rec.recommendation: BOTTOM LINE FOR THE NETHERLANDS: DO NOT BUILD THE SEPTEMBER 2027 PLAN AROUND A DUTCH PRIVATE SCHOOL. There is no private NVAO-accredited master in this field in the country, and no private audio provider can sponsor his residence permit — so the two things he needs (an accredited master + a visa) are simply not purchasable from the Dutch private sector at any price. He should concentrate his accredited-master applications on the Spain/Portugal/Italy slices, or reconsider Dutch PUBLIC institutions, which are outside this brief but are the only Dutch route that actually works: the Conservatorium van Amsterdam's Master Immersive Audio (NVAO-assessed) and its English-taught AEMA associate degree for electronic musicians — where, notably, 'when you enroll in an Associate Degree course, you can apply for a visa' — and HKU's Master of Music pathway Music Design. TWO THINGS HE CAN USEFULLY DO IN THE NETHERLANDS ANYWAY, both on an ordinary Schengen tourist visa and neither requiring accreditation: (1) DJ School Amsterdam's Producer Professional Course, ~€2,499 for 20 one-to-one English-language sessions plus 10 studio hours, compressible into two weeks — a direct, efficient way to build the portfolio he lacks; (2) SAE Amsterdam's one-month DJ Certificate at €699–€1,099 (confirm whether the €500 registration fee applies), ideally timed around Amsterdam Dance Event in October for scene contacts. Both are training, not qualifications — but a 4–8 track portfolio built to Abbey Road's published standard is precisely what every accredited master he applies to will ask for, and he does not have one yet. That is the highest-value use of the Netherlands for him.

My concrete advice: treat this as portfolio-building in summer 2027 BEFORE or ALONGSIDE a master's application, not instead of one. _rec.program: Звукорежисура (Sound Engineering) - Master's degree, specialty B5 Musical Art
_rec.institution: Національна академія керівних кадрів культури і мистецтв / National Academy of Culture and Arts Management (NAKKKiM)
_rec.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. Definitive: the rector's order approving 2026-2027 tuition for foreign citizens is headed 'МІНІСТЕРСТВО КУЛЬТУРИ УКРАЇНИ / НАЦІОНАЛЬНА АКАДЕМІЯ КЕРІВНИХ КАДРІВ КУЛЬТУРИ І МИСТЕЦТВ' - i.e. the Academy is a national institution subordinate to the Ministry of Culture of Ukraine, with a rector (Valerii Marchenko) and an academic council (вчена рада) whose 27 April 2026 decision, protocol No 9, sets the fees. State-run, not private.
_rec.language: ACTUAL TEACHING LANGUAGE: the official 2026 programme document (OPP) states 'Мова(и) викладання: Українська, англійська' - Ukrainian and English. TREAT THE ENGLISH CLAIM WITH CAUTION. This is a standard formula in Ukrainian OPP documents and usually means individual modules or supervision can be delivered in English, not that a foreigner can complete the whole degree without Ukrainian. Ukrainian admission rules for foreigners generally require an entrance exam in the language of instruction. He must get written confirmation of how much of this 90-ECTS programme is actually deliverable in English before treating it as an English-taught option.
_rec.languageRequirement: UNVERIFIED for this specific institution - NAKKKiM's foreign-applicant language rule is not published in readable form on the pages I opened. The Ukrainian norm is either proof of Ukrainian at the required level or completion of a preparatory language faculty (підготовче відділення), typically one year. Ask the admissions office directly. Do not assume the 'англійська' line in the OPP removes a Ukrainian requirement.
_rec.qualification: Магістр музичного мистецтва (Master of Musical Art). A real second-cycle degree: the OPP states the level as 'Другий (магістерський)', 'НКР України - 7 рівень, FQ-EHEA - другий цикл, EQF-LLL - 7 рівень', diploma type 'диплом магістра, одиничний, 90 кредитів ЄКТС'. Ukraine is an EHEA member and a Lisbon Recognition Convention party, so this is EU-recognisable in principle via ENIC-NARIC.
_rec.accreditationStatus: REAL BUT FLAGGED - READ THIS CAREFULLY. The OPP states verbatim: the programme (EDEBO identifier 35623) 'акредитована умовно (відкладена акредитація)' - CONDITIONALLY ACCREDITED, DEFERRED ACCREDITATION - by decision of the National Agency for Higher Education Quality Assurance (NAZYAVO) of 13 January 2026, protocol No 1 (92), accreditation case No 1769/АС-25. Conditional accreditation in the Ukrainian system means the Agency found shortcomings and gave the programme a period to fix them, with re-assessment to follow. It is a valid accreditation and the degree is a state degree, but this is exactly the kind of status that can complicate later recognition abroad. He should check the current status on NAZYAVO's register before applying, and ask what the identified shortcomings were.
_rec.institutionType: National academy under the Ministry of Culture; postgraduate/arts-management profile with a Performative Arts institute. Programme sits in the Кафедра музичного мистецтва (Department of Musical Art) within the Навчально-науковий інститут перформативних мистецтв.
_rec.focus: Music recording and sound engineering, with an explicit AI-for-audio strand. This is the closest thing in the four countries to a music-production master's.
_rec.whatYouStudy: From the official 2026 OPP, quoted in substance: theoretical content covers musicology, theory and history of music; the professional-technological component covers computer musicology, sound engineering, and digital, computer and multimedia technologies in music/audio production; exact sciences cover foundations of electrical engineering, musical acoustics and modern sound-technical systems; the innovation strand covers 'технології штучного інтелекту для аналізу, синтезу та обробки аудіо контенту' - AI technologies for the analysis, synthesis and processing of audio content. Students carry out 'звукозапис, редагування, мікшування та мастеринг музичного матеріалу' - recording, editing, mixing and mastering - through studio, concert and pedagogical practice, and write a master's thesis. Named modules visible in the department's document library include Mastering, Sound Engineering in MIDI, Sound-technical Apparatus, Multimedia Technologies, Music-Information Technologies, Creative Mixing Techniques, Digital Sound Recording, Electronic Music, Audiovisual Producing, Fundamentals of Sound Design, and Postproduction. Graduate occupational codes listed: 2455.2 Sound Engineer, 3131 Sound Recording Operator, 1229 Chief Sound Engineer, 1229 Studio Head.
_rec.durationEcts: 90 ECTS, 1 year 4 months. Both очна (денна) full-time and заочна (distance/part-time) forms are offered, both 1 year 4 months. Stated verbatim in the official OPP.
_rec.tuitionEU: Not applicable - Ukraine has no EU/non-EU fee split. There is a domestic rate and a separate foreign-citizen rate, published as two different PDFs.
_rec.tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED - AND THIS IS A REAL GAP, NOT AN OVERSIGHT. _rec.scholarships: UNVERIFIED, and realistically unlikely. Ukrainian state-funded (державне замовлення) places at arts institutions are generally reserved for Ukrainian citizens and specific protected categories; other foreign nationals are admitted on a paying basis within quotas. There is no published international scholarship scheme at NAKKKiM that I could open.
_rec.visaEligible: Legally yes - Ukraine issues student visas (type D) and temporary residence permits to enrolled foreign nationals, and the state maintains an electronic invitation system for foreign students. BUT SEE THE RECOMMENDATION FIELD: legal eligibility is not the operative question for Ukraine right now.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES ON THE PUBLISHED RULE - the OPP requires only 'a bachelor's, specialist's or master's degree' with no subject named. This is the most open entry rule of any programme found in these four countries. Confirm the content of the professional entrance examination before relying on it.
_rec.recommendation: ACADEMICALLY THE BEST-MATCHED PROGRAMME IN THIS SLICE, AND PRACTICALLY THE ONE I WOULD ADVISE HIM NOT TO PURSUE. Take the match seriously first: 90 ECTS in 1 year 4 months, entry open to any bachelor's degree, a curriculum that runs from electrical engineering and musical acoustics through MIDI, mixing, mastering, sound design and postproduction to AI audio synthesis, a working recording studio, and placements at the National Philharmonic and the National Opera. For a software engineer who wants to become a producer, the syllabus is close to ideal. Now the reasons to stop. FIRST AND DECISIVE: Ukraine is at war. Kyiv is under regular missile and drone attack, martial law is in force, and no responsible adviser tells a 22-year-old to move there for a discretionary arts master's starting September 2027. Whatever the situation is by then, he cannot plan around it from 2026, and an application cycle he must commit to in late 2026 offers no way to hedge. SECOND: the language. The OPP's 'Ukrainian, English' formula almost certainly does not mean a foreigner can complete the degree in English; assume he would need Ukrainian, probably via a year of preparatory study, and that is two years of his life spent on a language that serves no part of his stated career. THIRD: the programme is only CONDITIONALLY accredited (deferred accreditation, NAZYAVO decision of 13 January 2026) - a status that adds friction to any later recognition in the EU, on top of the friction a Ukrainian wartime degree would already carry. FOURTH: nobody will tell him the price - the official foreign-citizen tuition PDF exists but is an unreadable scan. VERDICT: record it, do not apply to it. If he wants a Ukrainian sound-engineering education, the sane version is to keep this on file and revisit only if the war ends and the programme's accreditation is upgraded to full. His Sept 2027 effort belongs in the EU and in Tbilisi.

The programme is a nested suite (PGCert / PGDip / MMus): PGCert and PGDip take two semesters full-time, while the full MMus requires three semesters including the 60-credit Final Project, which is explicitly non-exemptible ('the Final Project module is not exempted for those wishing to complete the MMus award'). The other two pathways are Performance Studies and Music and Communities.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Across the first two semesters: two complementary Specialism modules (20 credits each) covering recent developments in the chosen pathway plus technical, research and communication skills; a Practice module devoted entirely to developing individual creative practice with one-to-one tuition; a Seminar module for contextual, aesthetic and theoretical study via group tutorials and practice-based workshops. Additional modules in Music Technology and Society and a Research Project (which may include a work placement). Third semester: Final Project (60 credits), a sustained period of self-directed practice-based work. Assessment is 100% coursework on every module — no exams — and can take the form of practical/design work, portfolio submission, performance, workshop activity, lecture recital, presentation or essay. Staff research spans composition, performance, broadcasting, contemporary music, sound design studies, film music, creative technologies and disability arts practice; Music at Ulster placed joint 2nd in the UK for Research Impact in REF2014.

_rec.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED on the official page: works using "multiple, meaningfully and irreplaceably complementary media within a single work" — performance, interactive installation, video art, opera, experimental documentary, computer games. Contemporary composition, electronic music, multimedia design and collaborative creative work, using electroacoustic studios, multichannel audio, modular synthesis and field-recording gear. Teaching shared across JAMU's Music and Theatre faculties, BUT's Faculty of Fine Arts and Masaryk University. Final state exam (official): public presentation and defence of the final artistic work plus written documentation, a diploma thesis of at least 40 pages, and exams in Multimedia Composition and Contemporary Trends and Theory of Composition.
_rec.entryRequirements: CORRECTED AND NOW VERIFIED — this is stricter than previously recorded. Official master's admission page states verbatim: "Podmínkou přijetí je ukončené vysokoškolské vzdělání, dosažené alespoň v bakalářském stupni studia oboru Multimediální tvorba nebo příbuzného uměleckého oboru" (admission conditional on a completed bachelor's in Multimedia Creation OR A RELATED ARTISTIC FIELD). Plus, from the 2026/27 decree, a HARD Czech-language barrier: "cizí státní příslušníci (s výjimkou uchazečů ze Slovenské republiky), musí předložit vysvědčení o vykonání požadované zkoušky z českého jazyka dle stanovených podmínek (B1 SERR)" — foreign nationals must produce a Czech B1 CEFR certificate (in the 2026/27 cycle by 14 June 2026), plus officially translated bachelor documents and, for a foreign diploma, a nostrification decision. JAMU runs its own Czech verification exam (3,000 CZK) focused on music/culture vocabulary; accredited B1 CEFR certificates are also accepted. Mandatory attachments: proof of bachelor completion, structured CV.
_rec.portfolioSpec: PARTIALLY CORRECTED. At MASTER level the official page requires only "portfolio dosavadních uměleckých a jiných odborných aktivit" (portfolio of previous artistic and other professional activities) with NO published number, duration or format. IMPORTANT: the widely-quoted "minimum 20 / maximum 40 items" spec is the BACHELOR-level requirement (bachelor page: "Předložení portfolia domácích prací v celkovém počtu minimálně 20 nebo maximálně 40 položek", worth 10%) — do not apply it to the MgA. The master's application must ALSO include, in writing: a concept for the master's project, and a proposed diploma-thesis topic with basic theses.
_rec.auditionSpec: On-site, single-round, in Brno. Talent exam = 90% of the score, conducted as an oral interview (ústní pohovor) assessing prior study results and the bachelor graduation project, the portfolio, the written master's project concept, the written thesis-topic proposal, knowledge of current developments in the field, and language readiness. Foreign-language written test = 10%, a lexico-grammatical test at B2+ CEFR including specialist music terminology. CRUCIAL EXTRA: "V případě uchazeče, který absolvoval bakalářské studium v jiném (byť příbuzném) oboru, se úroveň jeho znalostí prověří praktickou zkouškou" — an applicant from a different field sits an additional practical exam in three parts: (a) a thematic task, a multimedia-work project on a set theme; (b) a practical task on the visual component; (c) a free task in any media with a compulsory musical component. 2026/27 exam date was 16 June 2026 (KKMT). Only 2 places.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Check, leaning NO. The published condition is a bachelor "in Multimedia Creation or a related ARTISTIC field" — a software-engineering BSc is not an artistic field, so acceptance is at the committee's discretion. There IS an explicit route: applicants from another field are tested by the three-part practical exam above. Combined with the Czech B1 certificate requirement, this is a genuine barrier, not a formality. The department's talent advisory service (booking address for Multimediální tvorba is fajnor@jamu.cz; department head doc. Dan Dlouhý, dlouhy@jamu.cz) is the correct first contact.

_rec.stipend: None. Tuition waiver by default only. Admission does not create any entitlement to a place in a JAMU hall of residence (stated in the decree).
_rec.facilities: VERIFIED on the department/programme pages: two electroacoustic music studios, a professional recording studio, a fully equipped theatre and chamber hall, interactive technologies, multichannel audio systems, a large stock of professional software and hardware, a MODULAR SYNTHESISER, and an equipped loan pool of microphones, field recorders, video cameras and sensors. Jaroslav Šťastný, MgA. Jiří Suchánek.

Also note the direction is installation and sound art, not club releases.
_rec.verificationNotes: Programme confirmed to exist at MgA level in Brno, Czech-taught, 2 years. Verified against four official sources: the programme database page; the master's admission-requirements page (https://hf.jamu.cz/studijni-obor/multimedialni-tvorba-3-prijimaci-rizeni/) for entry conditions and exam weights; the bachelor page (https://hf.jamu.cz/studijni-obor/multimedialni-tvorba-2-prijimaci-rizeni/) which is where the 20–40 item portfolio spec actually lives; and the official decree PDF "Vyhláška – magisterské navazující studium pro akademický rok 2026-2027" (https://is.jamu.cz/do/jamu/doc/5451/smer_pr_hf/Vyhlaska_nav.MgA.26-27_JVS.pdf) for the deadline, exam date, 990 CZK fee, 2 places and the Czech B1 requirement. UTB confirms fees arise only 'pokud student studuje program, který je veden v jiném jazyce než v češtině' (if the programme is delivered in a language other than Czech). This is the single most important funding fact in this slice.

_rec.totalCostEstimate: Tuition 0. Realistic total ~300,000-430,000 CZK (~12,000-17,500 EUR) for two years, essentially all living costs. Plus a Czech-language preparatory year if needed (paid, typically 100,000-160,000 CZK).

_rec.fundingLevel: Full (tuition), None (living costs) — the degree itself costs nothing, but he must self-fund living.
_rec.intakes: One annual intake, September/October start.
_rec.applicationOpens: 1 January (e-application at www.eprihlaska.utb.cz).
_rec.deadline: Master's applications 1 January - 30 April 2026, entrance examination 10 June 2026. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. For a SEPTEMBER 2027 start expect applications 1 Jan - 30 Apr 2027 with the exam in June 2027. NOTE: this is well AFTER his assumed Oct 2026-Feb 2027 window, so he has more runway than he thinks — but also note the bachelor deadline for 2027/2028 is 30 November 2026, so the faculty's calendars differ sharply by level.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes — accredited public university, full-time MgA. programme, supports a Czech long-term residence permit for study purposes.
_rec.recommendation: THE BEST-VALUE ARTISTIC OPTION FOUND IN THIS SLICE, AND THE HARDEST TO ENTER. Zero tuition for a Tunisian national, a real film-school studio environment, and no music-conservatory gatekeeping. The two obstacles are Czech language (needed to sit the talent exam) and a portfolio strong enough to win one of only a handful of Sound Design places out of ~25 across all specializations. Concrete next step: e-mail studium@fmk.utb.cz now asking (a) for the Zvuková skladba section of the current admissions směrnice, and (b) whether the master's talent exam can be sat in English for an international applicant — some Czech art faculties permit this and it would change the whole calculus. If Czech is immovable, this is a 2028/2029 target, not 2027.

Stage 2: an aptitude CONVERSATION in which the candidate presents the prepared project sketch and discusses artistic background and motivation. CORRECTION: the published length is 30 to 45 minutes, with a minimum of 20 minutes per applicant — the previous record's '20-45 minutes' was slightly off. No instrument, no performance, no conservatory technique is tested. For a candidate with no conservatory training this is a far more winnable format than a classical audition, and the 6-12 week preparation window means the decisive work happens at home, not on the spot.

The application must contain: a CV; a written justification of the choice of programme; studiengangsbezogene Arbeitsproben (work samples relevant to the field); and a description of planned artistic projects plus a project sketch in sound-art composition. His portfolio year should be built to produce exactly these four items and nothing else.

_rec.recommendation: The re-check upgraded this record rather than downgrading it, and it now has a published deadline where it previously had a blank. Everything remarkable about it verified: an applicant from an unrelated degree is EXPLICITLY admissible on artistic aptitude, only A1 German is demanded on paper and can even be evidenced through the interview itself, the aptitude test is a project conversation rather than an instrumental audition, the candidate gets 6-12 weeks at home to prepare the decisive project sketch, and the whole cost is a semester contribution. Two corrections he must act on: the deadline IS published — registration for the Eignungsprüfung runs 1 February to 1 April for the following winter semester, so his date is 1 April 2027, not a mid-summer university deadline; and the aptitude conversation is 30-45 minutes (minimum 20), not 20-45. That said, of the three artistic options it is the only one whose curriculum names ELECTRONIC COMPOSITION outright, and it is the only programme in this entire set where a non-music engineering graduate is admissible by written rule rather than by committee discretion. _rec.recommendation: Verification confirmed everything material and improved the accreditation picture — accredited 1 October 2023 to 30 September 2031, 120 ECTS, German with no language certificate demanded, 31 May deadline, semester fee only. It is a real, properly accredited, essentially free state degree and nothing about it is a rip-off. But for HIM it stays a C, for two reasons that verification did not soften. First, it is portfolio-gated at the front door: entry runs through an artistic project proposal and an Eignungsprüfung, and he has neither a proposal nor a body of sound work, so this is an aspiration for a later cycle rather than a September 2027 plan. Second, be blunt about direction — this is installation, sonification and research sound art, explicitly framed around acoustic ecology and sound as political act. It does not serve the international-DJ-and-producer goal, and pretending otherwise would waste his portfolio year. Two zero-cost steps if he is drawn to it anyway: download the 'Anforderungen im Eignungsverfahren' document from the programme page so he sees the actual bar rather than a summary, and attend one of the free online information sessions to ask Prof. Bovermann directly whether a software-engineering applicant with a year of self-built sound work has a route. A software-engineering BSc qualifies on paper, and his coding ability is directly relevant to the algorithmic strand (the programme is co-led by Prof. Julian Rohrhuber, known for live-coding/SuperCollider work).

_rec.program: Masterstudium Elektrotechnik-Toningenieur (Electrical Engineering and Audio Engineering) — inter-university with TU Graz
_rec.university: Kunstuniversität Graz (KUG) jointly with Technische Universität Graz

_rec.focus: Recording/Engineering (audio engineering fused with musical training)
_rec.language: German. Proof of C1/CEFR required; alternatively, applicants who present proof of A2 at application may sit a supplementary German examination (Ergänzungsprüfung aus Deutsch) before beginning regular studies.
_rec.durationEcts: 4 semesters / 120 ECTS (Studienkennzahl UV 066 413)
_rec.whatYouStudy: Official text: an interdisciplinary synthesis of technology and music, science and art. 'Based on a well-founded scientific and music-theoretical foundation, followed by specialisation with a choice among electrical/information-technology, music-practical and audio-technical areas.' Courses are held at Institute 17 — Electronic Music and Acoustics (IEM). Chairs: Robert Höldrich (recording and reproduction technology, electronic music), Alois Sontacchi (acoustics and audio engineering), Franz Zotter (acoustics and audio engineering). Graduates are aimed at the audio industry, acoustics and multimedia.
_rec.entryRequirements: KUG/TU Graz BSc Elektrotechnik-Toningenieur graduates qualify automatically. External applicants must hold 'ein gleichwertiges und zur Zulassung berechtigendes Studium' (an equivalent degree conferring admission eligibility); equivalence is assessed by the Dean of Studies, and 'je nach Vorbildung und zur Erlangung der vollen Gleichwertigkeit' up to 30 ECTS of courses and exams from the bachelor programme may be prescribed. All externals must pass the admission examination. German C1, or A2 at application plus the supplementary German exam. Documents: bachelor diploma and final certificate, transcript of records, all with official German or English translations and possibly diplomatic legalisation, via KUGonline.
_rec.portfolioSpec: NONE — there is no artistic portfolio and no recording dossier. Submission is purely academic (diploma, degree certificate, transcript, certified translations). A pre-check Infoblatt and Excel worksheet are offered so applicants can self-assess equivalence before applying.
_rec.auditionSpec: No artistic audition. A written admission examination at IEM in three parts: (1) Seashore hearing test over headphones, approx. 40 minutes — paired-comparison thresholds for frequency, intensity and tone duration, timbre discrimination, tone and rhythm memory (sample tests with solutions are published on Moodle); (2) second written aural test, approx. 20 minutes — melodic and rhythmic dictation, recognition of modes, time signatures, triads and instruments, plus spotting errors in a printed score; (3) written music-theory test, approx. 15 minutes — interval and scale construction, rhythm. Confirmed on the page: 'Die Zulassungsprüfung für das Wintersemester 2027/28 findet online statt' — the WS 2027/28 admission exam is ONLINE. Results normally 2 days later via KUGonline.
_rec.applicationOpens: Registration via KUGonline; opening date not published on the page. Overview of KUG admission-exam dates for the winter semester is linked from the page.
_rec.deadline: 3 June, with the next admission test given as 'xx. Juni 2027'. This is already the WS 2027/28 cycle, but the exact test DAY is an unfilled placeholder on the official page — treat 3 June 2027 as the working application deadline and confirm the exam day once KUG fills it in.
_rec.tuitionIntl: EUR 752.92 per semester total for third-country nationals: Studienbeitrag EUR 726.72 plus ÖH-Beitrag EUR 26.20 (confirmed on the KUG fee-waiver page).
_rec.scholarship: None applicable. KUG's Studienbeitrag waiver under the Ost-/Südosteuropaschwerpunkt applies only to Albania, Armenia, Belarus, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Georgia, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, Türkiye and Ukraine — Tunisia is NOT on the list, so he pays the full EUR 752.92 per semester.
_rec.fundingLevel: Partial — low public fee only (approx. EUR 3,012 tuition across four semesters). No scholarship identified.
_rec.stipend: UNVERIFIED — no stipend found for this profile. Austrian OeAD scholarships were not checked against this programme.
_rec.facilities: Institute 17 IEM (Electronic Music and Acoustics) at KUG hosts the teaching, with chairs in recording/reproduction technology and in acoustics and audio engineering; TU Graz supplies the electrical-engineering side. IEM's specific studio and Ambisonics inventory is not itemised on this page — UNVERIFIED at that level of detail.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES, by design — the clearest technical-entry route in Austria. Official wording: 'Externe Studienwerber*innen, die kein Bachelorstudium der Studienrichtung Elektrotechnik-Toningenieur an der KUG/TU Graz absolviert haben, müssen über ein gleichwertiges und zur Zulassung berechtigendes Studium verfügen', with 'bis zu 30 ECTS aus dem Bachelorstudium Elektrotechnik–Toningenieur' potentially prescribed. A software-engineering BSc is a plausible base, but the Dean of Studies rules on equivalence and an SE degree is not an electrical-engineering degree — the 30-ECTS top-up is likely.
_rec.fitNotes: The only affordable, portfolio-free route in this slice, and the online WS 2027/28 admission exam removes the travel barrier entirely. Two hard obstacles: German at C1 (or A2 plus a supplementary German exam that must be passed before regular studies begin), and the musical-aptitude battery — Seashore test, melodic/rhythmic dictation and music theory — which needs roughly a year of deliberate ear training. Also be honest about the content: this is an engineering degree in audio, not a DJ/producer degree, and the equivalence ruling on a software-engineering BSc is a genuine unknown.

It aims to educate creative and professional practitioners who acquire sound knowledge and skills through artistic, theoretical and professional subjects, for film and television as well as for other performing, broadcast and stage arts. Courses dealing with film sound are tied to practical work, individual and team-based: sound-design students realise film, television, radio and stage works produced by ADU's other departments and collaborate with other University of Zagreb faculties. Teaching staff are working sound recordists, sound editors, music editors, re-recording mixers and sound designers. Stage (A) submission, all eliminatory: (1) životopis (CV); (2) motivacijsko pismo — motivation letter, up to 2 'kartice' of text (~3,600 characters); (3) an audiovisual work for which the candidate conceived the sound picture or participated in creating it; (4) a written analysis of that submitted audiovisual work explaining the sound-picture concept AND listing the origin of the noises, music, sound effects and computer programs used in sound post-production. Positive evaluation of BOTH the audiovisual work and the written analysis is a precondition for reaching stage (B). The commission assesses knowledge of film history, film-music history and music history, and recognition of musical forms, styles and genres. _rec.program: Müzik Teknolojileri Tezli Yüksek Lisans Programı (Music Technologies, thesis master) — Müzik Teknolojileri Ana Bilim Dalı, Müzik ve Güzel Sanatlar Enstitüsü
_rec.institution: Ankara Müzik ve Güzel Sanatlar Üniversitesi (Ankara Music and Fine Arts University, MGÜ)
_rec.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. State university, founded by Turkish law as a devlet üniversitesi and run under YÖK/Ministry of National Education funding; it is one of only three universities named by the Turkish government's own Türkiye Bursları Art Scholarship as a state art institution (turkiyeburslari.gov.tr/fulltimeprograms lists it alongside Ankara Hacı Bayram Veli and İTÜ). Not a foundation (vakıf) university.
_rec.institutionType: Specialist state university of music and fine arts (conservatoire-type), with its own Müzik ve Güzel Sanatlar Enstitüsü (graduate institute)
_rec.qualification: Tezli Yüksek Lisans diploması — a real second-cycle degree. The Turkish Qualifications Framework register (TYÇ) classifies Turkish thesis master's diplomas at TYÇ level 7 / QF-EHEA level 2 / EQF-LLL level 7. Supports a Turkish student residence permit (öğrenci ikamet izni) for a non-EU national.
_rec.accreditationStatus: State-recognised. YÖK-authorised programme at a state university; graduate degree at TYÇ/EQF level 7. A YÖK 'denklik belgesi' (recognition certificate) for the foreign bachelor's degree is REQUIRED of foreign applicants before admission — this is a real administrative hurdle and takes months, so a Tunisian SMU MedTech BSc must be sent to YÖK well in advance.
_rec.language: Turkish. All teaching, all admission documents and the entrance examination are in Turkish. There is no English-taught track.
_rec.languageRequirement: Turkish C1 certificate from a YÖK-recognised Turkish-teaching centre (e.g. TÖMER) is compulsory for foreign nationals who studied abroad. If the candidate is admitted without it, he is registered and put on one (1) year of leave to study Turkish; if he cannot present a C1 certificate at the end of that year, his registration is cancelled. No English certificate is required at all.
_rec.englishTest: None. No IELTS/TOEFL is demanded — the foreign-language score requirement is explicitly waived for master's applicants ('Yabancı Dil Taban Puanı: Aranmaz'). The barrier is Turkish, not English.
_rec.durationEcts: Standard Turkish tezli yüksek lisans: 4 semesters nominal (minimum 7 courses + seminar + thesis). Exact ECTS total not stated in the admission guide — UNVERIFIED; ask enstitu@mgu.edu.tr or the Ana Bilim Dalı (deren.karacan@mgu.edu.tr).
_rec.focus: Music technology with a strong audio-engineering and acoustics bias — the guide states graduates should carry 'ileri düzeyde ses mühendisliği bilgisi' (advanced sound-engineering knowledge) and be able to conduct scientific work in music technology.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Courses combining technical field knowledge with academic literature study in music technologies; the assessed competence areas signal the content: sound recording, sound programming, instrument making, sound electronics and acoustics. It is an academic/research master (thesis required), not a commercial music-production diploma — do not expect a DJ/producer curriculum.
_rec.entryRequirements: Graduation from ANY bachelor's programme ('Herhangi bir lisans programından mezun olmak') — this is unusually open and is the single most important fact for this candidate. Minimum bachelor GPA 2.50/4.00 (or 65/100, or 3.1/5.00). No ALES required (and explicitly not required of foreign nationals). No foreign-language score required. Foreign nationals need a YÖK denklik belgesi and a Turkish C1 certificate (or the one-year Turkish grace period).
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES — explicitly. The 2025-26 exam guide states any bachelor's degree is accepted. A BSc in Software Engineering is formally eligible. HOWEVER the entrance exam tests trained musical hearing (see auditionSpec), so formal eligibility and realistic competitiveness are two different things.
_rec.portfolioSpec: Required at pre-evaluation (10% of the entrance score). Candidate must upload and also hand the jury three (3) printed copies of: (a) ONE self-produced work in sound recording, sound programming, instrument making, sound electronics or acoustics, as a digital copy (CD/DVD/USB) plus a written explanatory text; (b) a digital copy of other personal works in the field with audio files, software and/or written documents plus an index of them; (c) a CV. Scored on form, language and content: CV 11/11/11, field-specific CV 11/11/11, work report 11/11/12.
_rec.auditionSpec: Two-stage entrance exam, in Turkish. Stage I (60% of entrance score) tests six areas: Müziksel İşitme / musical ear-training (27 pts), Mesleki İşitme / technical listening and classification of played sounds (27 pts), Mesleki Bilgi / professional knowledge (9), Problem Çözme (9), Analitik Düşünme (19), Akademik Araştırmaya Yatkınlık (9) — for the last, candidates must read in advance a named Turkish journal article on determining the acoustic properties of small-scale popular-music production spaces (dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/203754) and answer on it in writing, then defend the answer orally. Stage II (30%) is an oral examination on the submitted portfolio (main work mastery 57, written-exam review 28, general assessment 15). Pass mark 60/100. Final ranking = 70% entrance-exam score + 30% bachelor GPA.
_rec.equipmentRequired: Not stated in the guide, but the portfolio effectively requires the candidate to have produced original recorded/programmed audio work beforehand — i.e. he needs a working DAW setup and a body of finished work by the time he applies. UNVERIFIED whether the university supplies anything; ask the Ana Bilim Dalı.
_rec.facilities: Not detailed on the pages opened — UNVERIFIED. Ask deren.karacan@mgu.edu.tr / ugur.baloglu@mgu.edu.tr about studios, control rooms and acoustics labs before committing.
_rec.intakes: One intake per year, Güz (autumn/September) semester.
_rec.applicationOpens: 2026-2027 Güz: online applications 10 August 2026 09:00 – 24 August 2026 17:00 (official MGÜ announcement). For a SEPTEMBER 2027 start expect an equivalent window in roughly late July–August 2027 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Separately, the Türkiye Bursları scholarship route opens 10 January and closes 20 February every year, so the funded route for Sept 2027 is 10 Jan – 20 Feb 2027.
_rec.deadline: 24 August 2026 for the 2026-27 intake (official). 2025-26 cycle ran 29 July – 8 August 2025, exam 25 August 2025, results 3 September 2025 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Türkiye Bursları deadline 20 February each year.
_rec.tuitionEU: Not applicable in the EU sense. Turkish nationals pay no tuition for a state thesis master's (only nominal contributions).
_rec.tuitionNonEU: 15,000 TL for the academic year for foreign nationals in a Tezli Yüksek Lisans at the Müzik ve Güzel Sanatlar Enstitüsü, payable as 7,500 TL + 7,500 TL in two instalments (MGÜ announcement '2024-2025 Eğitim-Öğretim Yılında Yabancı Uyruklu Öğrencilerden Alınacak Öğrenim Ücretleri'). PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date/amount; Turkish state fees are re-set annually by presidential decree and the lira figure will rise. This is the rate HE would pay as a Tunisian national. Waived entirely if he wins Türkiye Bursları.
_rec.otherFees: YÖK denklik application costs, sworn translation and apostille of the Tunisian degree and transcript, Turkish C1 course fees if not covered (TÖMER courses typically run several thousand TL), residence-permit fee and health insurance. Exact amounts UNVERIFIED — ask enstitu@mgu.edu.tr and the İl Göç İdaresi.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Self-funded: roughly 15,000 TL/yr tuition plus Ankara living costs plus one year of Turkish language study before or during the degree. Under Türkiye Bursları: zero — the scholarship pays tuition, a monthly stipend, accommodation, health insurance, one return flight and a full year of Turkish language course. Precise living-cost figures UNVERIFIED.
_rec.scholarships: Türkiye Bursları 'Art Scholarship Programme' (Sanat Burs Programı) explicitly lists Ankara Music and Fine Arts University and names 'Music Technologies' among the master's fields it funds (turkiyeburslari.gov.tr/fulltimeprograms). It is open to non-Turkish nationals, so a Tunisian applicant is eligible. Coverage: university and department placement, monthly stipend, tuition fee, one-year Turkish language course, accommodation, health insurance and a once-off flight ticket. Applications 10 January – 20 February annually via TBBS, free of charge, submittable in 8 languages. Master's applicants must generally be under 30.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes. Full-time, on-campus, state-recognised second-cycle degree at a YÖK university — supports a Turkish student residence permit. Türkiye Bursları holders receive placement and support through YTB.
_rec.recommendation: THE STRONGEST FIND OF THIS SWEEP FOR HIM, and the only fully-funded, formally-open door found in the four countries. It is the rare music-technology master that accepts ANY bachelor's degree, demands no ALES, no IELTS and no TOEFL, and is named by Türkiye Bursları as a funded art field. Realistic assessment: (1) the killer constraint is Turkish, not English — teaching, exam and admission are all in Turkish and a C1 certificate is required within a year; the Türkiye Bursları package includes exactly that year of Turkish, which makes the scholarship route far more viable than self-payment; (2) the entrance exam is 54/100 weighted on trained musical and technical ear (müziksel işitme + mesleki işitme) — with no conservatory background he must spend the coming year on ear training and critical listening, not only on beat-making; (3) the portfolio must be his OWN produced work in recording, sound programming, sound electronics or acoustics, with a written technical report — his software-engineering background is a genuine asset here if he builds audio-DSP or plug-in projects rather than only DJ sets; (4) only 2 foreign-national places were advertised in the 2025-26 guide, so it is competitive. Concrete plan: apply to Türkiye Bursları 10 Jan – 20 Feb 2027 naming this programme; start YÖK denklik and Turkish study in autumn 2026; build a portfolio of self-recorded/self-coded audio work with written technical documentation across 2026. Note also that the same programme is an academic/research master with a thesis — it will not by itself make him an international DJ; it will make him a credentialed audio technologist.

_rec.program: Elektronika a komunikace, navazující magisterský program — specializace Audiovizuální technika a zpracování signálů (Audiovisual Technology and Signal Processing)
_rec.institution: České vysoké učení technické v Praze (ČVUT) / Czech Technical University in Prague, Fakulta elektrotechnická (FEL / FEE)
_rec.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. ČVUT is a veřejná vysoká škola established under Act No. 111/1998 Sb.; its admission conditions are issued as a dean's decree (příkaz děkana FEL_PD_2025_05_V01) explicitly governed by that Act and the CTU Statute.
_rec.language: TWO PARALLEL TRACKS — this is the key finding. The specialization exists in a CZECH-TAUGHT version (free of charge) and the Electronics and Communications master's is ALSO delivered in ENGLISH (fee-paying), with the faculty's English programme page confirming the audiovisual technology and signal processing content among its seven specializations. Confirm before applying which track carries the Audiovisual Technology specialization in the target year.
_rec.languageRequirement: For the English track: proof of English knowledge, assessed by the admissions committee, with a certificate required if the applicant is not a native speaker — NO named IELTS/TOEFL band is set in the dean's decree, the committee judges it. That is unusually flexible and matters for an applicant who has not yet sat a test. For the Czech track: Czech, entrance examination in Czech.
_rec.qualification: Ing. (inženýr) — a real, state-recognised second-cycle engineering degree.
_rec.accreditationStatus: Nationally accredited public university programme (NAÚ). Supports a Czech long-term residence permit for study.
_rec.durationEcts: 120 credits (ECTS) minimum to complete; standard 2 years / 4 semesters, full-time. The study plan is 'Elektronika a komunikace — Audiovizuální technika a zpracování signálů'.
_rec.focus: Engineering of audiovisual signals — acoustics, sound and image technology, signal processing — with the human perceiver as the organising principle. NOT a creative sound-design or music-production degree.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Sensing, processing and reproduction of audiovisual signals; practical acoustic design and measurement; image and sound technology; modern methods of processing, compression and reconstruction of image, sound and other signals; explicit orientation toward 'the human as recipient of audiovisual information'. Graduates go into television and radio operations, audiovisual and acoustics design, automotive, and biomedical applications. Specialization guarantor: prof. Petr Páta (pata@fel.cvut.cz).
_rec.entryRequirements: A completed bachelor's degree, evidenced before enrolment. Entrance examination consists of an ONLINE INTERVIEW plus an optional test if the admissions committee decides to set one — for the English track. Documents required: transcript of results, English certificate (if not a native speaker), and a MOTIVATION LETTER. Documents not in Czech, Slovak or English need a certified translation. Nostrification (recognition) of the foreign higher-education qualification must be completed by the end of October of the first semester — the application itself does not require it up front, which materially lowers the barrier at application time.
_rec.portfolioSpec: NONE. No portfolio, no creative dossier, no artistic assessment. Applicants are merely 'recommended' to submit evidence of significant personal achievements or professional/academic excellence in electrical engineering, informatics, mathematics or physics — which a software-engineering graduate can supply directly from his degree and projects.
_rec.auditionSpec: None. There is no audition and no musical assessment of any kind.
_rec.equipmentRequired: None.
_rec.facilities: FEL acoustics and audiovisual-technology laboratories at ČVUT Prague; measurement and signal-processing infrastructure rather than creative studios.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES — EMPHATICALLY. This is an electrical-engineering faculty programme that actively prefers applicants from electronics, informatics, mathematics or physics. A BSc in Software Engineering is a normal, expected feeder profile. Of every programme in this slice, this is the one where his existing degree is an asset rather than a liability.
_rec.englishTest: No fixed band. The dean's decree requires 'a certificate of English proficiency if the applicant is not a native speaker', with the admissions committee assessing the level — no IELTS/TOEFL minimum is published. He should still sit IELTS Academic (target 6.5) to be safe, but the absence of a hard threshold means a modest score is unlikely to be an automatic bar. UNVERIFIED which certificates the committee accepts — ask the FEL admissions office.
_rec.tuitionEU: 0 CZK for the Czech-taught track (all nationalities). For the English-taught track, EU citizens pay the same fee as everyone else.
_rec.tuitionNonEU: CZECH-TAUGHT TRACK: 0 CZK for a Tunisian national — CTU FEE states plainly that students in Czech-language programmes 'do not incur these costs, regardless of citizenship'. ENGLISH-TAUGHT TRACK: fee-paying — 'All students enrolled in programs taught in English are supposed to pay tuition fees', with the amount depending on the level of study and the faculty reserving the right to adjust it each semester. THE EXACT AMOUNT IS NOT PUBLISHED on the faculty's tuition-fees page and I will not guess it: e-mail the FEL admissions office or the programme guarantor prof. Páta (pata@fel.cvut.cz) and ask for the per-semester fee for the English-taught Electronics and Communications master's for 2027/2028. A secondary source quoted 66,000 CZK/semester for CTU English-taught programmes generally — TREAT AS UNCONFIRMED until the faculty states it.
_rec.otherFees: Application fee 950 CZK per programme AND per specialization — applying to two specializations costs 1,900 CZK. Payment must be made the same day the application is filed; the application is only entered into the procedure once the fee is paid. Prague living costs ~20,000-28,000 CZK/month, the highest in this slice.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Czech track: ~500,000-670,000 CZK (~20,000-27,000 EUR) for two years, all of it living costs. English track: add the unpublished tuition — if the unconfirmed 66,000 CZK/semester figure is right, that would add ~264,000 CZK (~10,700 EUR) over the degree.
_rec.scholarships: The faculty states that high-performing international students may be eligible for scholarships to offset expenses, with details on its scholarship pages — no amounts or eligibility rules published there. UNVERIFIED - ask the FEL international office whether any entry scholarship is open to a first-year non-EU master's student.
_rec.intakes: Main intake for the following academic year, plus an EXTRAORDINARY SECOND ROUND (mimořádný termín, 2. kolo) that FEL has run in consecutive years — a genuine second chance, but it requires a brand-new application even if one was already filed that year.
_rec.applicationOpens: Autumn preceding the academic year; the dean's decree for 2026/2027 was issued 19 November 2025.
_rec.deadline: English-taught programmes: application completed AND fee paid by 31 March 2026. Czech-taught: application by 31 March 2026 with the entrance examination on 5 June 2026; a late window running to 13 August 2026 is referenced for the extraordinary round. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. For a SEPTEMBER 2027 start expect a 31 March 2027 deadline — this sits just outside his assumed Oct 2026-Feb 2027 window and is the single most important date to diarise.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes — accredited public university, full-time Ing. programme, supports a Czech long-term residence permit for study purposes. Note the nostrification requirement lands AFTER arrival (by end of October of semester one), so he must gather diploma, transcripts and legalisations before leaving Tunisia — the faculty explicitly warns applicants to obtain all documents before travelling to the Czech Republic.
_rec.recommendation: TOP PICK OF THIS ENTIRE SLICE FOR THIS CANDIDATE. It is the only programme found where every one of his weaknesses is irrelevant: no portfolio, no audition, no music degree, no conservatory training, no fixed IELTS band, and an admissions process that is an online interview plus a motivation letter. His BSc Software Engineering is the preferred feeder. The Czech-taught version costs a Tunisian national nothing; the English-taught version removes the language barrier at an unpublished but probably manageable cost. It is emphatically NOT a DJ or music-production degree — it is audiovisual signal engineering — but it is a credible, fundable, visa-supporting European master's that puts him inside a Prague audio-engineering ecosystem where he can build the production career on the side. Three actions now: (1) e-mail pata@fel.cvut.cz asking whether Audiovizuální technika a zpracování signálů is available in the English track for 2027/2028; (2) ask FEL admissions for the exact English-track fee; (3) start Czech from zero anyway, because the Czech track is free.

But it is delivered entirely at a distance in Greek, with remote exams, no studio, no cohort and no student visa. For a man whose whole plan depends on getting a European residence permit and building an international network, that makes it close to useless as a migration instrument, though not worthless as a credential if he could read Greek, which he cannot. Recorded here so the database contains the finding and no later sweep wastes time on it.
