_rec.program: Sound Design — szakirányú továbbképzés (postgraduate specialist training). WARNING: THIS IS NOT A MASTER'S DEGREE.
_rec.institution: Moholy-Nagy Művészeti Egyetem (MOME) / Moholy-Nagy University of Art and Design
_rec.publicPrivate: PUBLIC-FOUNDATION ("közfeladatot ellátó közérdekű vagyonkezelő alapítvány" model). MOME is a state-recognised Hungarian university of art and design, formerly directly state-run, now maintained by a public-interest asset management foundation under the 2021 Hungarian model — this is the ambiguity flagged in the brief. It is NOT a private company or church institution, it is state-recognised and appears in the Hungarian higher-education register, and it hosts Stipendium Hungaricum places on its degree programmes. But it is no longer a directly state-maintained institution either, and its fees are set commercially.
_rec.institutionType: University of art and design
_rec.qualification: NOT A MASTER'S DEGREE. The award is explicitly "Specialist training" (szakirányú továbbképzés) — a Hungarian post-bachelor specialist qualification that requires a prior degree to enter but does NOT confer a mesterfokozat (second-cycle master's degree) and does not carry 120 ECTS. It is a legitimate, accredited Hungarian qualification, not a fake, but it is NOT a second-cycle degree and will not be treated as a master's for further study or for most immigration purposes.
_rec.accreditationStatus: A genuine accredited Hungarian szakirányú továbbképzés at a state-recognised university — so not a diploma mill. But it sits outside the Bologna second cycle. Anyone reading the English page, which markets it under "Programmes" alongside MA courses, could easily mistake it for a master's. It is not one.
_rec.focus: Sound design for film, games and spatial audio
_rec.whatYouStudy: Sound design and sound art with a complex, cross-disciplinary view; collaboration with film and video game work. Students must complete three practical projects — a film sound project, a game sound project, and a spatial sound composition project — which together form a sound-design portfolio. Broad grounding in sound-design theory and technology and creative handling of the relevant software. Led by sound artist Ádám Krasz (director of MOME TechPark) and Csaba Hajnóczy DLA.
_rec.durationEcts: 1 year / 2 semesters. Delivered as a NIGHT COURSE ("Night course" on MOME's own English page; designed to be completed alongside employment). ECTS not published — UNVERIFIED. Being part-time evening study is itself disqualifying for a study residence permit in most cases.
_rec.language: HUNGARIAN. MOME's own English-language programme page states "Language: Hungarian". There is no English track. All teaching, the application documents and the interview are in Hungarian.
_rec.languageRequirement: Hungarian. No formal certificate level is published — UNVERIFIED — but the motivation letter, CV and interview are conducted in Hungarian, so functional Hungarian is required in practice. IELTS/TOEFL are irrelevant and will not help him.
_rec.entryRequirements: A completed bachelor's, master's, or university/college-level degree ("Alap- vagy mesterfokozat, illetve egyetemi vagy főiskolai szintű végzettség") — so his BSc would satisfy the degree condition. BUT he must also already have: knowledge of sound design and music-theory fundamentals, and working knowledge of Pro Tools and Ableton at basic level. Plus a professional portfolio.
_rec.auditionSpec: Three stages: (1) online application form; (2) upload of documents; (3) admission interview. For the 2026 intake the interviews were held 3–4 September 2026, and only the strongest applicants on the strength of motivation letters and portfolios were invited. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates.
_rec.portfolioSpec: MANDATORY. Required uploads: a motivation letter (max 1 A4 page), a CV, a PROFESSIONAL PORTFOLIO of existing work — explicitly a showreel or previous musical works, maximum 100 MB — and a scanned copy of the degree certificate. He currently has no portfolio, so he could not apply today.
_rec.equipmentRequired: Basic working knowledge of Pro Tools and Ableton Live is an explicit entry requirement, so access to and competence in both is assumed on day one.
_rec.facilities: MOME operates the MOME Sonic Studio and a Spatial Experimentation Studio, and the programme is run out of MOME TechPark — genuinely strong spatial-audio facilities by regional standards. No published equipment inventory. Partly UNVERIFIED.
_rec.tuitionEU: 790,000 HUF per semester, self-funded (önköltséges) — so 1,580,000 HUF for the full 2-semester course. Roughly €4,000 at prevailing rates, but do not rely on that conversion; the published figure is in forint.
_rec.tuitionNonEU: The SAME 790,000 HUF/semester — MOME publishes a single self-funded rate with no separate international tier for this course. So the rate he would pay as a Tunisian national is 790,000 HUF × 2 semesters = 1,580,000 HUF. Note this does not make it accessible: the barrier is language and immigration status, not price tiering.
_rec.otherFees: A non-refundable special procedure fee of 5,000 HUF per application; failure to pay excludes the applicant from the admission procedure entirely.
_rec.scholarships: NONE. Critically, Stipendium Hungaricum does NOT fund this. Tunisia IS an eligible Stipendium Hungaricum sending partner (the Tunisian Republic is named in the official 2026/27 Call for Applications, with the Ministère de l'Enseignement Supérieur as sending partner, deadline 15 January, stipend HUF 43,700/month plus HUF 40,000/month accommodation contribution plus tuition waiver and medical insurance) — but the Call restricts postgraduate specialist training courses and partial study to particular frameworks, and applicants may only apply for the study fields fixed in the bilateral educational cooperation programme between Hungary and Tunisia. A Hungarian-taught, part-time, non-degree evening course is not a realistic Stipendium Hungaricum target. Check the Tunisia entry at stipendiumhungaricum.hu/partners/ for the exact fields agreed with Tunisia.
_rec.intakes: September (course started 14 September 2026 for the 2026 cohort). PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
_rec.applicationOpens: Application form deadline 24 August 2026; document upload deadline 27 August 2026; interviews 3–4 September 2026. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates.
_rec.deadline: 24 August 2026 for the 2026 intake. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
_rec.visaEligible: ALMOST CERTAINLY NOT. Two independent problems: (1) it is a szakirányú továbbképzés, not a degree programme; (2) it is delivered as a part-time night course, and Hungarian study residence permits generally require full-time enrolment in a degree programme. Do not apply for this expecting it to produce a student residence permit. If he wants certainty, ask MOME's international office in writing whether the course issues the enrolment certificate accepted by the National Directorate-General for Aliens Policing — but expect the answer to be no.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Degree-wise yes — any bachelor's satisfies the formal entry condition, and no music degree is named. But the SUBSTANTIVE prerequisites exclude him today: he must already know sound design and music-theory fundamentals, already work in Pro Tools and Ableton, and already have a professional showreel or body of musical work. This is a course for people who are already practising, designed to specialise them further.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: 1,580,000 HUF tuition plus 5,000 HUF application fee, plus Budapest living costs, plus whatever it costs to reach functional Hungarian. In practice not a viable expenditure for him.
_rec.recommendation: DO NOT PURSUE — INCLUDED SPECIFICALLY AS A TRAP TO RULE OUT. This will surface prominently in any search he runs: it is marketed in English, on a well-known university's site, under a menu called "Programmes", was launched with press coverage as "Hungary's first accredited degree-granting sound design programme", and covers exactly his interests (film sound, game audio, spatial composition) with genuinely good facilities. It is nonetheless wrong for him on four independent grounds, any one of which is fatal: (1) it is NOT a master's degree — the award is 'Specialist training', outside the Bologna second cycle; (2) it is taught entirely in HUNGARIAN, with a Hungarian-language interview; (3) it is a part-time NIGHT COURSE and so will almost certainly not support a student residence permit for a Tunisian national; (4) it requires an existing professional showreel plus working Pro Tools and Ableton skills he does not yet have. There is also no funding: Stipendium Hungaricum, for which Tunisia IS eligible, will not cover a Hungarian-taught non-degree evening course. He should look at MOME only for its full MA programmes, and note that MOME's Média design MA is likewise not offered in English, and that Budapest Metropolitan University's Media Design MA states plainly "We do not offer this course in English".

_rec.program: DCSL60 — Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello in Musica Applicata, indirizzo Sound Design (Biennio)
_rec.institution: Conservatorio di Musica "Francesco Venezze" di Rovigo
_rec.institutionType: State conservatoire within the AFAM system, under the Ministero dell'Università e della Ricerca
_rec.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. A Conservatorio Statale di Musica; its right-to-study tax is administered by ESU Padova (the Veneto regional agency), and foreign students without a codice fiscale are directed to dirittoallostudio@esu.pd.it — both markers of a state AFAM institution.
_rec.qualification: Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello in Musica Applicata — explicitly stated on the official page as EHEA second cycle, EQF level 7. A real state-recognised second-cycle degree, equated to a Laurea Magistrale.
_rec.accreditationStatus: State-accredited under ministerial course code DCSL60 in the MUR AFAM register. The official page itself states the EHEA 2° ciclo / EQF 7 mapping, which is unusually explicit and useful for credential recognition abroad.
_rec.language: Italian. The requirement of B2 Italian for non-native speakers confirms the teaching language.
_rec.languageRequirement: B2-level Italian proficiency is explicitly required of non-native Italian speakers as an admission condition. This is a stated, formal requirement.
_rec.englishTest: None.
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years, 120 ECTS/CFA: 55 CFA in year one, 56 CFA in year two, plus 10 CFA for the final thesis/project.
_rec.focus: Applied music with a Sound Design orientation — DCSL60 'Musica Applicata' is a distinct ministerial course family from DCSL34 'Musica Elettronica', and is oriented toward music and sound applied to media rather than toward concert electroacoustic composition. For a candidate aiming at commercial and media work rather than academic art music, this framing is a better match.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Composizione per la musica applicata alle immagini (15 CFA — composition for music applied to images, the largest single block); Composizione musicale elettroacustica – Sound Design; Informatica musicale; Storia della musica elettroacustica; audio post-production and mixing technologies.
_rec.entryRequirements: Applicants must hold a 'diploma accademico di primo livello, o di diploma di laurea triennale, o di diploma di conservatorio', PLUS demonstrate B2 Italian for non-native speakers. THE KEY POINT: 'diploma di laurea triennale' — any three-year university degree — is listed as a qualifying route in its own right, alongside conservatoire diplomas. The candidate's BSc in Software Engineering satisfies this on its face. This is the most explicitly open entry wording of any Italian programme found in this sweep.
_rec.auditionSpec: An oral assessment. The candidate must submit a portfolio containing video/audio works, electronic compositions, or scores, which the admissions committee evaluates for mastery of electronic production across multiple instrumentation contexts. Notably there is NO written theory paper, NO solfège/ear-training test and NO instrumental performance requirement published — the assessment is portfolio-plus-oral. For a self-taught candidate this is the lowest published barrier in the Italian state sector.
_rec.portfolioSpec: Portfolio of video and/or audio works, electronic compositions, or scores, demonstrating command of electronic production across varied instrumentation contexts. Because scores are only ONE of the accepted alternatives, a purely audio/DAW-based portfolio is admissible — which is precisely what a year of self-directed work can produce. Build toward: music-to-picture cues (matching the 15-CFA composition-to-images core), original electronic pieces, and evidence of mixing and post-production competence.
_rec.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED — not published. A personal laptop with a DAW should be assumed.
_rec.facilities: UNVERIFIED — not published on the course page. The syllabus implies audio post-production and mixing facilities. Ask the conservatoire, and note that Rovigo is a small institution so studio access per student may be better than at a large conservatoire.
_rec.tuitionEU: UNVERIFIED as to exact amounts. The mechanism is documented: the annual contributo is paid via PagoPA, is organised in ISEE-based income bands, and requires the ISEE certificate to be attached at enrolment to obtain reduction or exemption; the system verifies the ISEE against the INPS database and computes the amount due. Multi-sibling reductions apply (first child full, second 60%, third 40%). Total exemption applies for students with certified disability of 66% or more. For calibration only, comparable Veneto and Emilia-Romagna state conservatoires cap the biennio contributo between roughly €1,800 and €2,300 — but do NOT rely on that for Rovigo. Ask the segreteria for the current Regolamento contributi.
_rec.tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED as to amount, but the mechanism is documented and favourable. Rovigo applies the standard Italian ISEE-band system rather than a flat non-EU surcharge: foreign students must present an ISEE (parificato/ISEEE), and if ISEE data is entered the system computes the amount due against the INPS database. Two documented facts help him directly: foreign candidates are EXEMPT from the admission examination fee ('i candidati stranieri sono esonerati dal versamento della tassa di esame di ammissione'), and foreign students without an Italian codice fiscale are told to contact ESU Padova at dirittoallostudio@esu.pd.it to sort out their position. Expect that with a low ISEEE reflecting Tunisian family income he lands in the lowest band or is exonerated. Confirm the exact band table by requesting the current Regolamento tasse e contributi from the segreteria.
_rec.otherFees: Tassa regionale per il diritto allo studio universitario (ESU Veneto) — payable annually, amount UNVERIFIED; the conservatoire publishes an annual notice for this. Marca da bollo. Admission examination fee — WAIVED for foreign candidates.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Cannot be stated precisely without the contributi table. On the Italian pattern, with an ISEEE filed, expect anywhere from near-zero to roughly €2,000/year. Rovigo is a small provincial Veneto city with materially lower living costs than Bologna, Turin or Milan — roughly €600–850/month, and housing is far easier to find. This combination of a low barrier to entry and low cost of living is the reason this programme deserves serious attention.
_rec.scholarships: ESU Padova (the Veneto regional right-to-study agency covering Rovigo) runs income-based borse di studio open to non-EU students, covering maintenance, fee exemption and subsidised housing. The conservatoire directs foreign students to ESU directly, which suggests a working pathway. MAECI government scholarships are the alternative national route. UNVERIFIED whether the conservatoire itself offers any internal award.
_rec.intakes: Autumn — Italian academic year.
_rec.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — not published on the course page. Italian conservatoire ammissioni bandi are typically issued in spring. Watch conservatoriorovigo.it from about March 2027, and complete Universitaly pre-enrolment on the Ministry calendar in parallel.
_rec.deadline: UNVERIFIED — obtain the annual Bando di ammissione.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes. A Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello from a state conservatoire supports an Italian student visa and permesso di soggiorno per studio. Non-EU applicants resident abroad must pre-enrol via Universitaly and compete for places within the annually published non-EU contingent.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES — the clearest 'yes' in this sweep. The published entry list names 'diploma di laurea triennale' (any three-year university degree) as a qualifying title in its own right, and the assessment is a portfolio plus an oral, with no published theory paper, ear-training test or instrumental requirement. A Software Engineering BSc plus a genuine audio/audiovisual portfolio maps onto the stated requirements without needing an exception to be made.
_rec.recommendation: APPLY — this is the single best-matched find of the whole sweep for this candidate, and it is the one to build the portfolio year around. Three things line up that never line up together: the formal entry route explicitly accepts any three-year university degree; the admission assessment is portfolio-and-interview with no musicianship examination published; and the cost sits inside the Italian ISEE system, so a low Tunisian family income should translate into a low or zero contributo rather than a flat foreign surcharge. Foreign candidates are even exempt from the admission exam fee. Against that, two real conditions: B2 Italian is a stated requirement, not a suggestion, so Italian study must start now (his French will make this the fastest language on his list); and the degree's centre of gravity is composition for images and applied media sound, not club music — the 15-CFA core is music-to-picture. Shape the portfolio accordingly: three to five scored-to-picture cues, several original electronic pieces, and demonstrable mixing and post-production work. Contact the segreteria in autumn 2026 to request the Bando di ammissione and the Regolamento tasse, and ask whether the B2 must be certified or is tested in-house. If he lands one place from this entire research effort, this is the most likely one.

_rec.program: Master akademske studije MUZIČKA PRODUKCIJA (MAS Music Production) — Interdisciplinary Studies
_rec.institution: Akademija umetnosti (Academy of Arts), Univerzitet u Novom Sadu
_rec.institutionType: State art academy; a constituent faculty (članica) of the public University of Novi Sad. Departments: Music, Fine & Applied Arts, Drama. This programme sits under 'Interdisciplinarne studije', administered by the Drama Department (application e-mail aunsprijemni.dramski@uns.ac.rs).
_rec.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. Evidence: it is a članica of Univerzitet u Novom Sadu, a state university; the 2026/27 enrolment competition is issued on the basis of a decision of the Government of the Republic of Serbia on the number of students to be enrolled, and the official quota table lists state-BUDGET-funded places (2 budget + 8 self-financing for this programme). Budget places only exist at state-founded institutions.
_rec.language: Serbian (Serbian only). All programme documentation, the informator and the entrance exam are in Serbian. No English-taught track exists. Note the parallel programme 'Gluma' is explicitly labelled 'na srpskom jeziku', confirming language-specific delivery at this Academy.
_rec.languageRequirement: For foreign nationals the official 2026/27 konkurs requires 'доказ о познавању српског језика' (proof of knowledge of the Serbian language) at application. The required level, accepted certificate and issuing body are NOT published — UNVERIFIED. Ask: Služba za studije i studentska pitanja, +381 21 422-177 ext. 2 / aofarts@uns.ac.rs.
_rec.englishTest: None. No IELTS/TOEFL is demanded anywhere in the konkurs or informator. The barrier here is Serbian, not English.
_rec.qualification: Master akademske studije (MAS) — a real, state-recognised second-cycle degree (EQF/NQF level 7), 60 ECTS, 1 year. Professional title conferred: 'Мастер музички продуцент' (Master Music Producer). This is a degree, not a certificate.
_rec.accreditationStatus: Accredited. The Academy's official accreditation page lists 'Uverenje o akreditaciji studijskog programa Muzička produkcija' under 'Master akademske studije akreditovane 2023. godine' (certificate PDF: https://akademija.uns.ac.rs/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/Muzicka-produkcija-Uverenje-novo.pdf — a scanned image, so the decision number could not be machine-read). Accrediting body: the Serbian Commission for Accreditation and Quality Assurance / National Accreditation Body (NAT). Being a state HEI programme it is automatically listed in the Serbian register of accredited programmes.
_rec.durationEcts: 1 year / 2 semesters, 60 ECTS.
_rec.focus: Music production. This is the single closest match in the entire Western-Balkan academy sector to a 'producer/DJ' career goal — it is music production proper, not film sound.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Compulsory (from the official 2023-accreditation curriculum table, nastavni plan PDF): Muzička produkcija (2+2, both semesters); Zvuk i muzika na filmu (Sound and Music in Film, 2+1); Savremene tendencije u muzičkoj produkciji 1 and 2 (Contemporary Tendencies in Music Production); Muzika-događaj-publika (Music–Event–Audience); Master rad – istraživanje (research) and Master rad (thesis project). Electives, 12 ECTS to be chosen from: Istorija elektroakustičke muzike (History of Electroacoustic Music), Istorija popularne muzike (History of Popular Music), Produkcija muzike za nove medije (Music Production for New Media), Muzika u medijima (Music in Media), Dramaturgija savremenog filma, Metode u muzičkom obrazovanju u digitalnom okruženju.
_rec.entryRequirements: THERE IS A DOCUMENTED CONTRADICTION BETWEEN TWO OFFICIAL DOCUMENTS — he must get this resolved in writing before doing anything else. (a) The 2026/27 konkurs text states: 'Студијски програм – Музичка продукција: завршене основне академске студије у четворогодишњем трајању из уметничке области Музичка продукција, или сродан студијски програм (240 ЕСПБ)' — i.e. a four-year BA IN THE ARTISTIC FIELD of music production or a RELATED programme. (b) The 2026/27 Informator for this exact programme states only: 'Пријемни испит могу полагати лица која су завршила основне академске студије у четворогодишњем трајању (240 ЕСПБ)' — any four-year 240-ECTS bachelor. Second, hard problem for HIM: 240 ECTS / four years is mandatory in both readings. A Tunisian three-year Licence in Software Engineering (180 ECTS) does NOT meet this. He must check what his SMU MedTech BSc is worth in ECTS and years, and whether a Serbian diploma-recognition decision (rešenje o priznavanju strane visokoškolske isprave) will grade it as a four-year/240-ECTS first degree. If it is 180 ECTS he is ineligible regardless of portfolio. Foreign nationals additionally submit: diploma-recognition decision, proof of health insurance, proof of Serbian language.
_rec.portfolioSpec: With the application: (1) a PORTFOLIO of works created in the three years preceding the entrance exam; (2) motivation letter; (3) CV; (4) diploma/certificate of completed four-year BA (240 ECTS); (5) a MEDICAL CERTIFICATE INCLUDING AN AUDIOGRAM, signed by an ophthalmologist, an ENT specialist and a psychologist — an unusual and genuinely blocking requirement he must arrange in Tunisia in advance; (6) scanned ID; (7) photo min. 1200x800 px JPG under 1 MB; (8) proof of payment of the application fee. Submission is 100% electronic — one e-mail per candidate, all files under 12 MB total, each file named with the candidate's name. His one-year portfolio-building plan maps exactly onto the 'works from the previous 3 years' rule, so a portfolio built in 2026-27 is admissible for a 2027 application.
_rec.auditionSpec: Two-stage entrance exam. PART ONE (pass/fail): a written test in the professional-artistic field of Music Production; a written analysis/evaluation of a piece of music against subjective and objective criteria set by the commission; an interview with the commission. Candidates who pass proceed to multi-day exercises and PART TWO: assessment of the submitted works — up to 30 points; practical work using the Academy's own equipment — up to 20 points; oral examination of knowledge in the professional-artistic field of audiovisual media (interview with the commission) — up to 30 points. Separately, BA grade average scores up to 20 points (10.00 = 20 pts, down to 6.00-6.49 = 4 pts). A candidate who does not exceed 50 total points fails and is not ranked. The exam is conducted in Serbian.
_rec.equipmentRequired: Part two of the entrance exam is 'практичан рад на материјалу Академије' — practical work on the Academy's own material/equipment, so no personal studio rig is required for the exam. What he must bring is a portfolio of finished audio work. Studio equipment inventory not published — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.facilities: The programme is delivered with practical studio work at the Academy (the entrance exam itself is run on Academy equipment). No published inventory of studios, control rooms, consoles or immersive/Atmos capability — UNVERIFIED. Ask the Drama Department / Katedra za audiovizuelne medije directly.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Ambiguous and decisive for him — see entryRequirements. The Informator wording admits any 240-ECTS four-year bachelor (which would let a software engineer in); the konkurs wording restricts to the artistic field of music production or a cognate programme. Even on the permissive reading, the entrance exam is a subject-matter exam in music production plus a portfolio, so it is not a soft entry. He has no music degree and no portfolio yet, which makes this a stretch but not an automatic exclusion — unlike a conservatory performance master, there is no instrumental audition.
_rec.tuitionEU: Not applicable as a category in Serbia. Domestic self-financing students: 125,000 RSD per year (official 2026/27 konkurs quota table).
_rec.tuitionNonEU: EUR 1,800 per year — THE RATE HE WOULD PAY. The official 2026/27 konkurs quota table has a dedicated column 'Школарина за странце (евра)' showing 1800 for every study programme at the Academy, including this one. Note the anomaly: at ~117 RSD/EUR, 125,000 RSD is roughly EUR 1,065, so the foreigner rate is about 70% higher than the domestic self-financing rate but still very low by European standards.
_rec.otherFees: Application/entrance-exam fee: amount not stated in the extracted konkurs text — UNVERIFIED (paid to account 840-32790845-46; ask Služba za studije). Diploma and certificate issuing fees: 4,000 RSD to the University plus 4,000 RSD to the Academy (payment reference 300 for the Drama Department). Diploma recognition (nostrifikacija) fee at the University of Novi Sad — UNVERIFIED. Compulsory health insurance for foreign students — cost UNVERIFIED.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Tuition EUR 1,800 for the whole degree (it is a one-year, 60-ECTS master). Living costs in Novi Sad are not published by the Academy — UNVERIFIED; do not use third-party estimates as fact. This is nonetheless among the cheapest genuinely accredited music-production masters found anywhere in the region.
_rec.fundingLevel: Check. There are 2 state-budget (fee-free) places on this programme against 8 self-financing places. The konkurs says a foreign national may enrol 'под истим условима као и домаћи држављанин' (under the same conditions as a domestic citizen), yet it simultaneously publishes a separate foreigner tuition rate — so whether a Tunisian can actually take one of the 2 budget places is UNVERIFIED and must be asked in writing before applying. Realistically, plan for EUR 1,800.
_rec.scholarships: No programme-level or Academy-level scholarship for non-EU applicants is published on any official page opened for this record — UNVERIFIED. Do not assume one exists. Where to ask: (1) the Serbian Ministry of Education's bilateral/developing-country scholarship offers, which are distributed to candidates through their home ministry — he should ask the Tunisian Ministère de l'Enseignement Supérieur whether Serbia offers Tunisia places in a given year; (2) the University of Novi Sad international office. Erasmus+ credit mobility is inbound-only for enrolled students and is not an admission route.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes in principle — this is an accredited programme at a state university, which is the category that supports a Serbian temporary residence permit for the purpose of education (privremeni boravak radi školovanja). A Tunisian national requires a visa D (long-stay study visa) obtained before travel, then converts to temporary residence in Serbia. The konkurs itself confirms the institution enrols foreign nationals and lists the extra documents required (diploma recognition, health insurance, Serbian language proof). Exact visa D document list, fees and processing times are NOT published by the Academy — UNVERIFIED; the authoritative sources are the Serbian Ministry of Interior (MUP) and the Serbian embassy accredited to Tunisia. Serbia is not in the EU or Schengen, so this permit gives no EU mobility rights.
_rec.intakes: One intake per year, October start (Serbian academic year).
_rec.applicationOpens: For the 2026/27 cycle the konkurs text was published 29 May 2026 and the application portal/informator went live in July 2026. For his SEPTEMBER/OCTOBER 2027 target he should expect the 2027/28 konkurs to be published around May-June 2027 with the informator in July 2027 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
_rec.deadline: 2026/27 cycle (official, from the konkurs — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for 2027/28): electronic application 05.10.2026; entrance exam 07-13.10.2026; preliminary ranking list 15.10.2026; final ranking list 20.10.2026; enrolment of admitted candidates 20.10.2026. NOTE the timing trap: unlike Western European masters, applications close in EARLY OCTOBER of the year of entry, not the preceding winter. For a 2027 entry he applies around early October 2027 — but he must start the diploma-recognition process and the audiogram/medical certificate many months earlier.
_rec.recommendation: THE SINGLE BEST FIND IN THIS SLICE FOR HIS STATED CAREER GOAL, and cheap enough to be realistic (EUR 1,800 total tuition). But three hard gates, in order of severity: (1) the 240-ECTS / four-year first-degree rule — if his SMU MedTech BSc is a three-year 180-ECTS licence he is ineligible, full stop, so verify this FIRST via a Serbian diploma-recognition enquiry; (2) proof of Serbian language, level unspecified — with Arabic/French/English and no Slavic language, a year of Serbian study is a real commitment and he should ask now what certificate is accepted; (3) a subject-matter entrance exam in music production plus a three-year portfolio window plus an ENT audiogram. His IELTS/TOEFL gap is irrelevant here, which is a genuine advantage. Concrete next step: e-mail aofarts@uns.ac.rs and aunsprijemni.dramski@uns.ac.rs asking, in one message, (a) whether a 180-ECTS three-year foreign bachelor can ever be accepted, (b) which Serbian-language certificate and level satisfies the requirement, (c) whether foreign nationals may compete for the 2 budget places.

_rec.program: Master akademske studije DIZAJN VIDEO IGARA (MAS Video Game Design) — Interdisciplinary Studies
_rec.institution: Akademija umetnosti (Academy of Arts), Univerzitet u Novom Sadu
_rec.institutionType: State art academy, constituent faculty of the public University of Novi Sad. The programme sits under 'Interdisciplinarne studije' and is run out of the Drama Department's Katedra za audiovizuelne medije (Chair of Audiovisual Media).
_rec.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — same evidence as the Music Production entry: constituent of the state University of Novi Sad, enrolment numbers fixed by a Government of Serbia decision, 2 state-budget places published in the official quota table.
_rec.language: Serbian only. The official programme page states the programme is taught in Serbian; the entrance exam, informator and curriculum are Serbian. No English track.
_rec.languageRequirement: Foreign nationals must supply 'доказ о познавању српског језика' (proof of knowledge of Serbian) per the 2026/27 konkurs. Required level/certificate NOT published — UNVERIFIED; ask Služba za studije, +381 21 422-177.
_rec.englishTest: None required.
_rec.qualification: Master akademske studije (MAS), a genuine state-recognised second-cycle degree, 60 ECTS, 1 year. (The first-cycle sibling programme confers 'diplomirani umetnik digitalnih medija'; the exact master title was not machine-readable from the scanned accreditation certificate — UNVERIFIED, ask the Academy.)
_rec.accreditationStatus: Accredited. Listed on the Academy's official accreditation page as 'Uverenje o akreditaciji studijskog programa Dizajn video igara' under 'Master akademske studije akreditovane 2024. godine' (https://akademija.uns.ac.rs/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/MAS-Dizajn-video-igara-1.pdf, scanned). The first-cycle programme was accredited in 2017 and the Academy describes it as the first accredited video-game programme in the Western Balkans.
_rec.durationEcts: 1 year, 60 ECTS (official curriculum table 5.1b).
_rec.focus: Video game design — included here ONLY because game audio sits inside it as an elective strand. This is not an audio degree.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Compulsory (official curriculum table): MA701 Žanrovska analiza i sinteza video igara (12 ECTS); MA703 Studije video igara (4); MP2102 Grafičke komunikacije u interaktivnim medijima (6); MA7002 Imerzivne igre / Immersive Games (6); MAZRD Završni rad (12); MAZRI Završni rad – istraživanje (12). Electives, 12 ECTS chosen from a list that is where the audio content lives: MSMIM Muzika u medijima (Music in Media, 6); MA1003 Zvuk u filmskoj umetnosti (Sound in Film Art, 6); MA4003 Produkcija muzike za nove medije (Music Production for New Media, 6); MA1002 Audiovizuelna artikulacija (6); MA2002 Postprodukcija filmske slike (6); MLVIA Video art (6). At most 12 ECTS of the 60 can be audio.
_rec.entryRequirements: Clean and permissive, and identical in BOTH official documents (no contradiction here, unlike the Music Production programme): 'Студијски програм – Дизајн видео игара: завршене основне академске студије у четворогодишњем трајању' / 'лица која су завршила основне академске студије у четворогодишњем трајању (240 ЕСПБ)' — ANY four-year, 240-ECTS bachelor in any field. No artistic-field restriction. The 240-ECTS / four-year rule is still the gate for a Tunisian three-year licence. Foreign nationals additionally file a diploma-recognition decision, health insurance proof and Serbian language proof.
_rec.portfolioSpec: With the application: (1) an EXPLICATION of the artistic-research project the candidate intends to realise as the master's thesis; (2) a motivation letter; (3) a PORTFOLIO of the candidate's previous works in the field of video game design; (4) diploma/certificate of a four-year 240-ECTS bachelor; (5) CV; (6) scanned ID; (7) photo 1200x800 px; (8) proof of application-fee payment. NOTE: unlike Music Production, NO medical certificate or audiogram is demanded.
_rec.auditionSpec: Two stages. PART ONE (pass/fail): test of knowledge of the history and aesthetics of video games; a combined test of creative solution of design tasks; analysis of the submitted entry work plus interview with the commission. PART TWO (after multi-day exercises): assessment of works submitted with the application — up to 25 points; practical work in video game design — up to 25 points; oral examination in the professional-artistic field of video game design — up to 30 points. BA grade average adds up to 20 points. Under 50 total points = fail, no ranking. Conducted in Serbian.
_rec.equipmentRequired: Practical exam work is done at the Academy. No personal equipment requirement published. A demonstrable body of game-design work is the real requirement.
_rec.facilities: Not published — UNVERIFIED. Ask Katedra za audiovizuelne medije. The presence of a compulsory 'Imerzivne igre' (Immersive Games) course implies some interactive/VR capability but nothing is documented.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES — explicitly. Any four-year 240-ECTS bachelor qualifies, in both the konkurs and the informator. For a software engineer this is by far the most accessible second-cycle art-academy programme found anywhere in this eight-country slice, and his coding background is a direct asset rather than a handicap. The trade-off is that it is a game-design degree with only 12 ECTS of optional audio.
_rec.tuitionEU: Not an applicable category in Serbia. Domestic self-financing rate: 125,000 RSD per year.
_rec.tuitionNonEU: EUR 1,800 per year — THE RATE HE WOULD PAY, from the 'Школарина за странце (евра)' column of the official 2026/27 konkurs quota table, which shows 1800 for this programme. Total tuition for the degree is EUR 1,800 since it is one year.
_rec.otherFees: Application/entrance-exam fee — amount UNVERIFIED (paid to Academy account 840-32790845-46). Diploma and certificate issuing: 4,000 RSD to the University + 4,000 RSD to the Academy. Diploma recognition fee and compulsory health insurance — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: EUR 1,800 tuition for the whole master. Living costs in Novi Sad not published by the institution — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.fundingLevel: Check. 2 state-budget places and 8 self-financing places (2026/27). Whether a foreign national may compete for a budget place is UNVERIFIED — the konkurs says foreigners enrol under the same conditions as domestic citizens but publishes a separate foreigner tariff. Plan for EUR 1,800.
_rec.scholarships: None published at programme or Academy level for non-EU applicants — UNVERIFIED. Route to ask: Tunisian Ministère de l'Enseignement Supérieur (bilateral Serbian government scholarship offers, if any in a given year) and the University of Novi Sad international office.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes in principle — accredited programme at a state university, the category that supports a Serbian temporary residence permit for education. Tunisian nationals need a long-stay visa D first. Document lists, fees and timelines are not published by the Academy — UNVERIFIED; authoritative sources are the Serbian MUP and the Serbian embassy accredited to Tunisia. Serbia is outside the EU/Schengen.
_rec.intakes: One intake per year, October start.
_rec.applicationOpens: 2026/27 konkurs text published 29 May 2026, informator July 2026. Expect the 2027/28 equivalents around May-July 2027 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
_rec.deadline: 2026/27 cycle (PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for 2027/28): electronic application 05.10.2026; entrance exam 07-13.10.2026; preliminary list 15.10.2026; final list and enrolment 20.10.2026. Applications close in early October of the year of entry.
_rec.recommendation: Report this as his BACKUP / realistic-entry option in Serbia, not his first choice. It is the only programme found in this whole eight-country academy sweep whose published entry rule admits any four-year bachelor without an artistic-field restriction, and his software-engineering background is directly relevant. But be honest with him: it is a game-design master, audio is capped at 12 of 60 ECTS (Music in Media, Sound in Film Art, Music Production for New Media), it will not make him a DJ or a record producer, and it still requires a video-game-design portfolio he does not have. The same 240-ECTS/four-year gate and the same Serbian-language gate apply. If he wants Novi Sad, the Music Production MAS is the right target and this is the fallback if the artistic-field restriction blocks him.

The programme page says the studies are 'intended for musicians, music producers, performers, and any interested candidates who wish to create or advance a career in the music industry, in accordance with their interests and previously acquired experience', which reads permissively but is marketing copy, not a rule. _rec.facilities: A music studio at the Belgrade campus is referenced in the programme description. No inventory, no studio specification, no immersive/Atmos claim — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Probably yes on the marketing copy ('all interested candidates... in accordance with their previously acquired experience') and there is no published entrance exam or portfolio bar — but nothing in the official admission rules confirms it. Treat as UNVERIFIED until confirmed in writing. Note that a third of the curriculum is management/marketing, which a software-engineering graduate would handle comfortably.
_rec.tuitionEU: Not an applicable category in Serbia. The published rate of EUR 4,500 per year is explicitly headed 'CENA ŠKOLARINA ZA DRŽAVLJANE R. SRBIJE I BIVŠIH SFRJ REPUBLIKA' — i.e. it applies to citizens of Serbia and of the former Yugoslav republics only. Payable in monthly instalments.

The only fee table on the official page is expressly restricted to Serbian and ex-Yugoslav nationals; a Tunisian national falls outside it and the rate he would actually pay is nowhere stated. Do not assume it is EUR 4,500 — private Serbian universities commonly charge non-regional students more. He must ask upis@metropolitan.ac.rs / +381 11 20 30 885 for the written foreign-national tariff for MAS Muzička produkcija before considering this.
_rec.otherFees: Not published — UNVERIFIED. No application fee, enrolment fee, diploma fee or health-insurance cost is stated. The university advertises 'specijalni popusti i pogodnosti' (special discounts) — terms not published for foreign students.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Cannot be stated. Even the tuition input is unknown for a Tunisian national. As a floor, the ex-Yugoslav rate of EUR 4,500 for one year is 2.5x the Academy of Arts Novi Sad foreigner rate for a comparable one-year 60-ECTS master — so on published evidence this fails his 'only self-pay if genuinely cheap' test.
_rec.fundingLevel: None visible. It is a private university with no state-budget places. The scholarships page is aimed at competitions for domestic entrants; nothing for non-EU master applicants is published — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.scholarships: Nothing a Tunisian applicant can realistically win is published on the official site — UNVERIFIED. The 'Stipendije i takmičenja' page exists but no non-EU master scholarship is documented. Ask admissions directly.
_rec.visaEligible: Probably yes, but confirm. The university holds a Serbian work licence and its programmes are accredited, which is the class of institution whose enrolment supports a temporary residence permit for education in Serbia; a Tunisian would need a visa D first. However, the university publishes NOTHING about foreign-national enrolment, diploma recognition or visa support — UNVERIFIED. Before paying anything, confirm with the Serbian Ministry of Interior (MUP) and the Serbian embassy accredited to Tunisia that enrolment at this specific private university is accepted as the basis for a study residence permit, and ask the university for its international-student office. Serbia is outside the EU/Schengen.
_rec.intakes: Enrolment is advertised as open throughout the year for master studies, which in practice means rolling admission rather than a single fixed intake. October start is the standard Serbian academic-year start.
_rec.applicationOpens: Rolling — the official admissions page states master enrolment can be done without restriction all year. Online application via the university's admission portal.
_rec.deadline: No published deadline (rolling admission). For a September/October 2027 start this is administratively the easiest calendar in the whole slice, but the visa timeline, not the university deadline, becomes the binding constraint.
_rec.recommendation: A genuine gap-fill — an accredited Serbian master in music production that no earlier sweep caught — and the curriculum (two semesters of music production, a creative sound workshop, plus branding/marketing/entrepreneurship) is unusually well aligned with an aspiring producer-DJ who also wants to run himself as a business. But three warnings he must hear. First, the price he would pay is unknown: the only published figure, EUR 4,500/year, is expressly for Serbian and ex-Yugoslav nationals, so his rate is UNVERIFIED and likely higher. Second, at that price it is roughly 2.5x the public Academy of Arts Novi Sad, which teaches a deeper, more artistically serious music-production master for EUR 1,800 — so this only makes sense if Novi Sad's 240-ECTS or Serbian-language gates block him. Third, essentially nothing about admission requirements, portfolio, language or foreign-national procedure is published; a programme that will not tell you its entry rules before you enquire deserves caution even when accredited. Action: one e-mail to upis@metropolitan.ac.rs asking for (a) the foreign-national tuition for MAS Muzička produkcija, (b) the minimum prior degree in years and ECTS, (c) the language of instruction and any language certificate, (d) whether they support study-residence-permit applications.

_rec.language: Slovak only. Verified verbatim: "Štúdium sa uskutočňuje iba v slovenskom jazyku."

_rec.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED named courses on the official page: Mixáž a mastering (Mixing and Mastering); Zvuková tvorba – Audiovizuálna tvorba; Teória filmového zvuku (Film Sound Theory); Hudobná réžia (Music Direction); Zvuková syntéza (Sound Synthesis); plus music recording theory and practice and sound design theory. Master level explicitly targets film sound in surround, Dolby Surround 7.1 and Dolby Atmos, and film music. Official aim (portalvs description): to develop independent creative thinking and the ability to be a full partner in a film or TV crew across preparation, shooting and post-production; the graduate as a "zvukový majster" adapts sound expressive means to a dramaturgical intent, and is also equipped for radio production, classical-music recording, live recording and sound reinforcement, and work in music recording studios.
_rec.entryRequirements: Formal condition is simply a completed bachelor's degree ("Základnou podmienkou prijatia na magisterské štúdium je úspešné ukončenie bakalárskeho štúdia", §56 of the Higher Education Act), with conditional admission possible if the degree is awarded by enrolment day. LANGUAGE CONDITION NOW VERIFIED and lower than expected: "Minimálne kritérium na prijatie zahraničného uchádzača na študijný program uskutočňovaný v slovenskom jazyku, je znalosť slovenského jazyka na úrovni A2 doložená certifikátom" — a Slovak A2 certificate, not B1 or B2. Foreign applicants must also supply a recognition statement (uznávacia doložka) and officially certified, translated copies of prior qualifications. Note the framing caveat: "Magisterské štúdium študijného programu STRIHOVÁ A ZVUKOVÁ SKLADBA nadväzuje na bakalársky študijný program s rovnakým názvom" (the MA follows on from the bachelor programme of the same name). Application via ePrihláška; fee €40 electronic / €60 paper. Approximately 5 places.
_rec.portfolioSpec: Still UNVERIFIED at the level of exact specification — no number of works, duration or format is published. What IS now confirmed: home works must be submitted, and there is a hard upload deadline separate from the application deadline — "Domáce práce k prijímaciemu konaniu je potrebné nahrať podľa zaslaných inštrukcií najneskôr do 12. 6. 2026. Práce zaslané po termíne nebudú akceptované a uchádzač nebude pripustený k prijímaciemu konaniu" (works uploaded after the deadline are not accepted and the applicant is excluded). Instructions are sent individually after the application. Request the prospekt / požiadavky na prijímacie skúšky from the FTF study department (study coordinator Jana Mihoková, jana.mihokova@vsmu.sk, +421 2 2100 6511 ext. 511).
_rec.auditionSpec: On-site entrance examination in Bratislava. Form confirmed on portalvs as: talentová, písomná, ústna, testy (talent, written, oral, tests). Single published exam date — 23 June 2026 in the prior cycle, with home works due 12 June 2026. No remote or online option is published for FTF; the Music and Dance Faculty of the same university runs a different process with an online interview for internationals, but that is a separate faculty and does not apply here. Worth asking the study department directly whether any remote accommodation exists.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Check, leaning cautiously positive. The published basic condition is only "successful completion of bachelor's study" with NO named field — better than any other programme in this slice. The soft caveat is the statement that the MA "follows on from the bachelor programme of the same name", and the ateliér trains sound masters and sound engineers, so a strong practical portfolio would have to carry the case. No statement anywhere bars a non-music or non-film bachelor. Ask the coordinator directly.
_rec.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Prior cycles: application by 9 April 2025 (2025/26) and 8 April 2026 (2026/27); home works upload by 12 June 2026; entrance exam 23 June 2026. For September 2027 entry expect roughly early April 2027, a mid-June 2027 works deadline and a late-June 2027 exam. Nothing for 2027/28 is published as of July 2026.
_rec.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Via ePrihláška on the FTF VŠMU site; opening date not published. Fee €40 electronic, €60 paper.
_rec.tuitionIntl: €0 per year for full-time study in Slovak within the standard length of study — CONFIRMED: "Ročné školné — Štandardná dĺžka štúdia: bezplatne", and VŠMU states that study in Slovak-language programmes is free, with foreign students treated on the same terms as Slovak ones. Fees apply only in defined cases: exceeding the standard length or parallel study costs €2,150/year at master's level in the arts field for 2025/26 (CORRECTED — the prior record's €1,650 is the BACHELOR-level rate). Programmes delivered in a foreign language cost €4,500/year regardless of nationality, but that does not apply to this Slovak-taught programme.
_rec.scholarship: None found that this programme is eligible for. CRITICAL CORRECTION: the Slovak Ministry's "Scholarships for talented students from all over the world" (scholarships.portalvs.sk) is NOT available here. It is restricted to selected study programmes falling under the Smart Specialisation Strategy SK RIS3 2021+, and VŠMU does not appear anywhere in the official "List of selected smart specialization study programmes SK RIS 3 2021+" (checked directly — zero occurrences of VŠMU, Múzických, zvuk or skladba in the list). The scheme also requires an SAT score of at least 1100 or SCIO tests at the 63rd percentile, and pays €500/month up to €15,000 over two master's years — not the €1,025/month or €10,000 previously recorded, which conflated it with the separate National Scholarship Programme (NSP), a short-term mobility scheme for students already enrolled abroad, not a full-degree award.
_rec.fundingLevel: Partial (tuition-free only). NOT full — no stipend scheme is available to him for this programme.
_rec.stipend: None available. Tuition waiver by default. The €500/month national talent scholarship is closed to VŠMU programmes (not on the SK RIS3 list). The NSP is a mobility grant for stays of 1–10 months, not full degree study. Living costs in Bratislava would be entirely self-funded.
_rec.facilities: Founded 1999. Described on the official page as one of Slovakia's most modern audio complexes and holding DOLBY ATMOS MUSIC STUDIO certification: five sound mixing suites, a cinema hall, professional microphones and field-recording equipment, working from stereo through multichannel for cinema and streaming. A development project upgrades one mixing suite to Dolby Atmos 12.1 and the cinema to Dolby Atmos 39.2. Head: Mgr. art. Tobiáš Potočný, ArtD.; staff include prof. Peter Mojžiš, doc. Dušan Kozák, doc. Marek Piaček. Facilities claims come from the ateliér's own page and were not independently corroborated.
_rec.fitNotes: Still the best facilities-per-euro in the slice — Dolby Atmos Music certified, five mixing suites, 120 ECTS, and genuinely €0 tuition for a Tunisian. The formal entry bar is also the lowest here: any bachelor's degree, plus only Slovak A2 by certificate. But the funding case has collapsed on verification: there is no stipend he can win for this programme, so he would self-fund roughly two years of living costs in Bratislava. Add full instruction in Slovak, an unpublished portfolio spec with a hard June upload cut-off, an on-site June exam, only about 5 places, and a curriculum aimed at film/TV sound and immersive audio rather than club production.
_rec.verificationNotes: Programme confirmed to exist at Mgr. art. level in Bratislava, Slovak-taught, 4 semesters / 120 ECTS. Verified against: the ateliér programme page (sourceUrl) for courses, 120 ECTS, the 8 April 2026 deadline, 23 June 2026 exam and €40 fee; the official portalvs.sk record https://www.portalvs.sk/sk/studijny-program/vsmu-strihova-a-zvukova-skladba2 for the Slovak-only rule, the A2 certificate requirement, the general admission condition, exam form, ~5 places, the 12 June 2026 home-works deadline and free standard-length tuition; VŠMU's fee pages for the €2,150 master's overrun rate and €4,500 foreign-language rate; and the Slovak scholarship portal plus the official SK RIS3 programme list PDF. CORRECTIONS MADE: (1) the scholarship claim is reversed — VŠMU is absent from the SK RIS3 list, so the national talent scholarship is unavailable, and its terms are €500/month up to €15,000 with an SAT/SCIO test requirement, not €1,025/month and €10,000; funding therefore drops from 'potentially Full' to Partial; (2) a previously unrecorded Slovak A2 certificate requirement for foreign applicants is now documented, along with the uznávacia doložka and translation requirements; (3) the overrun fee is €2,150 at master's level, not €1,650; (4) a separate hard home-works upload deadline (12 June in the prior cycle) is now documented, distinct from the application deadline; (5) ~5 places and the caveat that the MA follows the same-named bachelor are now recorded. STILL UNVERIFIED: the exact portfolio specification; whether any remote exam option exists at FTF; the ateliér's Dolby Atmos certification and suite count beyond its own page.

This is UCAM's OWN diploma. It is NOT an official Máster Universitario, does not appear in the RUCT catalogue of official degrees, and does not give direct access to a Spanish doctorate.
_rec.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL AS A DEGREE. It is a título propio / Máster de Formación Permanente issued by UCAM under its own authority. The INSTITUTION is legitimate — UCAM is a recognised Spanish private university listed in RUCT and legally entitled to issue títulos propios under art. 7 of Ley Orgánica 2/2023. But THIS AWARD is not ANECA-verified and is legally a university certificate, not an official master's degree. In practice: credible and university-branded with genuine industry weight, but it will not be treated as a master's degree by a foreign ministry, a public-sector employer or a doctoral programme.
_rec.visaEligible: HIGH RISK — probably NOT, on the verified schedule. This is the decisive finding and it corrects the prior reasoning in both directions. First, the good news: Spain's official management criteria for student authorisations (Ministerio de Inclusión, June 2025, under RD 1155/2024) state explicitly that for higher education 'existen los títulos oficiales y los títulos propios. Ambos son admisibles para la obtención de una autorización de estancia por estudios' — and universities are named as centres entitled to offer them. So being a título propio is NOT itself disqualifying, contrary to the earlier assumption. Semipresencial delivery is also permitted, provided at least 50% of the programme is taught in person. Now the bad news, which is decisive. The same criteria set a weekly teaching load of 'un mínimo de 20 horas semanales' as the general rule, with an exception for intensive or concentrated programmes only where the applicant can justify that 'al menos 12 horas son presenciales' with the remainder being assessed coursework. UCAM's own official brochure publishes the timetable: Fridays 16:30–20:30 and Saturdays 09:30–13:30 and 15:30–19:30 — a total of 12 contact hours per week, delivered at weekends, in a SEMIPRESENCIAL format meaning not all 12 are in person. That falls far below the 20-hour general rule and sits exactly at, and realistically below, the 12-in-person-hour exception floor. The 50%-in-person test is also unverified and doubtful for a weekend hybrid course. CONCLUSION: he must not assume this supports a residence permit. He must obtain written confirmation from UCAM's international office, stating the in-person percentage and weekly presencial hours, before paying anything. On the published evidence the answer is likely to be no.
_rec.focus: Music production: composition techniques, production, artistic development, recording, mixing and mastering.
_rec.whatYouStudy: VERIFIED module structure and credit weights from the official brochure: I. Herramientas de trabajo para la producción musical (13.2 ECTS); II. Fundamentos de la Producción Musical (11.2 ECTS); III. Producción Musical Profesional (9.6 ECTS); IV. Trabajo Final de Máster (16 ECTS); V. Prácticas en empresa (10 ECTS). Total 60 ECTS. Note the shape: only 34 ECTS is taught content — 26 ECTS, well over a third, is final project plus work placement. Stated career outcomes: productor musical, técnico especialista en mezcla, técnico de mastering, técnico asistente en estudio de grabación. Graduates receive official Steinberg Cubase professional certification, and a Cubase licence is included in the materials.

_rec.scholarships: No scholarship specifically identified for non-EU applicants on the programme page or brochure — UNVERIFIED, and likely none for this título propio. UCAM's general postgraduate financing is described as payment plans and financing through partner banking entities, which realistically requires a Spanish bank relationship he will not have before arrival. _rec.paymentPlans: Yes — payment plans and financing through partner banking entities are advertised; exact terms UNVERIFIED.
_rec.facilities: Campus de los Jerónimos, Murcia. Industry partners VERIFIED in the official brochure: Sony Music España and the MasterFather platform. Named teaching producers, verified: Ludovico Vagnone, Antonio Escobar, Ed Is Dead, Pablo Rous, Baghira and Luis del Toro. Official Steinberg Cubase professional certification included, with the Cubase licence provided.
_rec.reputationSignals: Genuine industry partnership with Sony Music España; recognised Spanish producers on the teaching staff, with Ed Is Dead and Baghira being real names in Spanish electronic music; Steinberg Cubase certification is a concrete, verifiable, portable credential. The brochure name-checks Bizarrap, Baghira, Pablo Rous, Zef, Marz and Dani Ruiz as the model of the modern producer the course is aimed at, which is well aligned with his ambition. UCAM absorbed its older 'Máster en Ingeniería de Sonido y Producción Discográfica' into this programme, so any listing of that older master should be treated as superseded. RED FLAGS: only 12 places; the award is a certificate, not a degree; the timetable is weekend-only at 12 contact hours per week; over a third of the credits are TFM plus work placement rather than taught content; and the visa position is weak.
_rec.recommendation: On paper the best value in this slice by an enormous margin — EUR 4,194.12 all-in, verified to the cent, for a 60-ECTS university-branded music production master with Sony Music España involvement, named Spanish electronic producers teaching, an included Cubase licence and Steinberg certification. His software-engineering degree is named explicitly as a welcome entry profile, no portfolio is demanded, no IELTS is needed, foreign degrees are accepted without homologation, and it starts in September, matching his target. If he were already living legally in Spain, this would be the clear recommendation. But he is not, and that is where it breaks. THREE ISSUES, in order of severity. (1) THE VISA. I verified Spain's actual rules rather than assuming: títulos propios ARE admissible for a student authorisation, which is better than feared — but the binding constraint is the teaching load, and UCAM's own brochure publishes a weekend-only timetable of 12 contact hours per week in a semipresencial format. The requirement is 20 hours per week, or at minimum 12 hours that are genuinely in person for concentrated programmes, plus at least 50% in-person delivery overall. This programme sits at or below that floor. On the published evidence it likely does NOT support a student residence permit. (2) LANGUAGE. It is taught entirely in Spanish, including a 16-ECTS final project. (3) THE AWARD is a certificate, not a degree — acceptable for industry, worthless for a future PhD or any title-dependent role. VERDICT: outstanding return on euro, but probably not a relocation route. ACTION: before anything else, email UCAM's international office and ask three specific questions in writing — what percentage of the programme is delivered in person, how many presencial hours per week, and has UCAM successfully supported non-EU students onto a student visa for THIS programme. If the answers are weak, this option is worth nothing to him as a route to Europe, however cheap it is.
_rec.verificationNotes: Fetched the official UCAM programme page and, critically, extracted the full text of UCAM's official downloadable brochure PDF. Also extracted and read the Spanish Ministerio de Inclusión 'Criterios de gestión sobre autorizaciones de estancia por estudios' (signed 23 June 2025, under RD 1155/2024) directly from the PDF, plus Instrucción SEM 3/2025. ALL MONEY CONFIRMED EXACTLY: EUR 3,900 tuition, EUR 235 pre-enrolment, EUR 59.12 school insurance — total EUR 4,194.12. Award confirmed as Máster de Formación Permanente (título propio), 60 ECTS, semipresencial, 12 places, Murcia. NEWLY VERIFIED AND DECISIVE: the September start; the three-cuatrimestre calendar (Sept-Dec, Jan-Apr, May-Jul); the exact class timetable of Fridays 16:30–20:30 plus Saturdays 09:30–13:30 and 15:30–19:30, i.e. 12 contact hours per week; the full module credit breakdown showing 16 ECTS TFM and 10 ECTS work placement; the verbatim entry-profile sentence naming 'Ingenierías en Telecomunicaciones e Informática'; the no-homologation provision for foreign degrees; and the full named teaching roster. VISA ANALYSIS CORRECTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: the prior data implied título propio status was itself a visa problem — the official criteria say the opposite ('Ambos son admisibles'), and semipresencial study is permitted with at least 50% in-person delivery. However the verified 12-hour weekend timetable falls below the 20-hours-per-week general rule and at/below the 12-presencial-hour intensive exception, which is a stronger and better-evidenced objection than the prior speculation. Rating lowered to C on that basis despite the excellent price and content fit. STILL UNVERIFIED: in-person percentage, Spanish level required, portfolio requirement, scholarships, 2027 dates.

CRITICAL AND FAVOURABLE POINT FOR THIS CANDIDATE: unlike Музикознание, Композиция and Дирижиране — where the 2025/26 handbook explicitly states "Необходимо е кандидатът да притежава музикална образователно-квалификационна степен „Бакалавър"" (a MUSIC bachelor's is required) — the two Звукорежисура specialties carry NO such clause. A non-music bachelor (e.g. BSc Software Engineering) enters the two-year track. Non-EU applicants additionally need: NACID recognition of the foreign diploma, legalised/translated documents, passport copy, two photos, GDPR declarations.
_rec.auditionSpec: Single-stage oral interview (събеседване) on four set topics: (1) physical acoustics, behaviour of sound in space, sound phenomena; (2) sound-technical devices — electroacoustic transducers, mixing desks, amplifiers, processors; (3) spatial sound formats; (4) computer and electronic music technologies. No instrumental audition. No solfège test. This is a THEORY interview, not a performance audition — realistically preparable in a year by a technically-minded software engineer.
_rec.portfolioSpec: No portfolio is required by the published exam programme — admission is by interview on the technical syllabus only. This is unusual and materially advantageous for a candidate with no portfolio. Confirm with the faculty office, as practice can differ from the printed handbook.
_rec.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED. Not stated in the admission handbook. Ask the ТКДФ faculty office whether a personal laptop/DAW licence is expected.
_rec.facilities: UNVERIFIED for this specialty specifically. NMA operates recording studios attached to the sound-engineering department; no published equipment inventory was found. Ask the department directly.
_rec.tuitionEU: State-subsidised (държавна поръчка) places are free of tuition for Bulgarian and EU/EEA nationals who have not previously held a state-funded master's place; fee-paying Bulgarian/EU places exist at the academy's domestic rate (figure not published on the pages checked — UNVERIFIED).
_rec.tuitionNonEU: €8,500 per academic year. This is the rate he would pay as a Tunisian national. Quoted verbatim from NMA's own non-EU admissions page: "ГОДИШНИ такси за обучение за новоприети: … За магистратура – 8500 евро". If he needs the Bulgarian preparatory language year first, that is a further €5,500 for that year. Non-EU applicants are NOT eligible for the state-subsidised places.
_rec.otherFees: Application fee for domestic-channel candidates 100 leva; for non-EU candidates a candidate fee set by the number of entrance exams. Bulgarian-language exam fee €50. Expedited September application fee €230.08 (versus €153.39 for the June round). Living costs in Sofia are additional.
_rec.scholarships: No NMA scholarship for self-funding non-EU nationals was found on the official site. Bulgaria has no broad national scholarship equivalent to Stipendium Hungaricum open to Tunisia on the evidence found; state-subsidised places are reserved for Bulgarian/EU nationals and for persons of Bulgarian origin under ПМС 103/1993 and ПМС 228/1997, neither of which a Tunisian national qualifies for. The only realistic routes are (a) a Tunisian government bilateral scholarship — ask the Bulgarian Embassy in Tunis and the Tunisian Ministère de l'Enseignement Supérieur about the Bulgaria–Tunisia educational cooperation programme, and (b) after enrolment, Erasmus+ mobility. Treat this programme as effectively self-funded at €8,500/yr.
_rec.intakes: September (one intake per year)
_rec.applicationOpens: Non-EU documents are received from roughly spring; the 2026/27 non-EU deadline was 12 June 2026. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Domestic-channel master's document window for 2025/26 was 27 May – 4 June 2025 (ТКДФ). PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
_rec.deadline: For a September 2027 start expect a non-EU document deadline around 12 June 2027. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date — the exact 2027 date is published on nma.bg/priem each spring.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes. NMA runs an explicit non-EU ("извън ЕС") admission route culminating in a Ministry of Education and Science Certificate of Acceptance, which is the document required to apply for a Bulgarian type-D long-stay visa and then a student residence permit.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES — and this is the key finding. The 2025/26 official handbook imposes the "music bachelor's required" condition only on Musicology, Composition and Conducting; the two sound-engineering specialties are open to any prior higher education, taking the two-year route. A BSc Software Engineering is therefore an eligible entry qualification.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Approximately €17,000 in tuition for the two-year master's, plus roughly €5,500 if a Bulgarian preparatory language year is needed first (so up to ~€22,500 tuition over three years), plus Sofia living costs (UNVERIFIED — no official figure published; budget separately) and application/exam fees of a few hundred euro.
_rec.recommendation: WORTH A SERIOUS LOOK ON ACADEMIC FIT, BUT PROBABLY UNAFFORDABLE. This is the single best academic match found anywhere in this three-country slice: game audio, spatial sound, electronic music technology, entry by a technical interview rather than a music audition, no portfolio demanded, and — uniquely — no music bachelor's required. For a software engineer it is the most winnable admission in Hungary/Romania/Bulgaria. The two killers are money and language: €8,500/year with no scholarship he can win, and instruction entirely in Bulgarian with a certified Bulgarian-language requirement he cannot meet by September 2027 without a paid preparatory year. Realistic plan if he wants it: decide by autumn 2026, start Bulgarian immediately, budget ~€22.5k, and email the ТКДФ faculty office now to ask (a) whether the interview can be sat in English or with an interpreter, (b) the ECTS total, (c) whether any tuition reduction exists for non-EU students. If the answer on language is no, drop it.

Its defects are identical to the game-audio programme: €8,500/year unfunded and taught entirely in Bulgarian, plus a September application window that is very tight against non-EU visa timelines. Only pursue if he decides his real bottleneck is industry knowledge rather than production skill — and even then, only if the money is solved.

_rec.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. There is NO English-taught version of this master (only the Nordic Master in Folk Music is taught primarily in English).

It only says: 'Foreign students are warmly encouraged to follow language classes in order to learn Danish as quickly as possible after arriving in Denmark.' UNVERIFIED — ask admissions (Lene Kielsen, lki@sdmk.dk, +45 63119915) whether a Danish certificate is demanded of a non-EU applicant, because the residence-permit rules and the Danish-language group teaching pull in different directions.
_rec.focus: Electronic music, sound art, electroacoustic composition, sound-as-material practice
_rec.whatYouStudy: SDMK describes the master as giving 'specialised knowledge, skills and competences to work as an electronic musician, composer or sound artist at the highest artistic level' and developing 'your unique artistic profile'. The underlying discipline covers synthesis, electroacoustics, field recording, sound systems, studio and software work.

_rec.intakes: One intake per year, studies start in August
_rec.applicationOpens: 15 October (per SDMK's official 'Apply!' page)

Note the parenthesis — the second limb is ambiguous and is the only crack a non-music BSc could get through. SDMK's FAQ states more bluntly: 'You will only be accepted to the master study if you have a bachelor degree in music', with a recommendation test arranged. Treat a Software Engineering BSc as almost certainly insufficient without a written derogation.
_rec.portfolioSpec: 'one or more artistic works of a duration of no more than around 25 minutes', submitted as audio files or a multimedia presentation, all self-created with any collaborators clearly declared; plus a written statement of no more than 2 A4 pages covering concept, potential, planned artistic projects, artistic experience and motivation.

_rec.equipmentRequired: You bring your own computer/instrument to the entrance exam presentation.
_rec.facilities: Conservatoire studio facilities at the Esbjerg campus (Kirkegade 61, DK-6700 Esbjerg). Detailed studio inventory not published — UNVERIFIED, ask the programme coordinator.
_rec.tuitionEU: Free — EU/EEA/Swiss citizens pay no tuition at Danish conservatoires.
_rec.tuitionNonEU: EUR 10,000 per academic year for master programmes (SDMK's own Guide for International Students). Two years = EUR 20,000. SDMK adds: 'all prices listed above are due to yearly change according to indexation', so budget above this for 2027–2029.
_rec.otherFees: Application fee DKK 500 for master applicants. (Bachelor students already at SDMK applying to a master with no entrance exam are exempt.)
_rec.scholarships: NONE that he could win. SDMK states flatly: 'SDMK - Danish National Academy of Music does not offer any scholarships for foreign students.'
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Tuition EUR 20,000 over two years + DKK 500 application fee. Danish living costs and the immigration self-support requirement are UNVERIFIED here — check SIRI (nyidanmark.dk) for the current documented-means figure per month.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes in principle — a full degree at a state conservatoire under the Ministry of Culture supports a Danish student residence permit, and SDMK's own guide tells non-EU/EEA students they 'need to apply for and obtain the residence permit before coming to Denmark' and to register with the municipality within 5–8 days of arrival.
_rec.englishTest: None published for this programme (it is not English-taught).
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Effectively no. The FAQ wording ('only be accepted to the master study if you have a bachelor degree in music') is the operative barrier; the 'or equivalent' limb on the EMOL-KA page is untested and would need written confirmation.
_rec.recommendation: GENUINE FIND, WRONG FIT FOR HIM. This is the most on-target programme any Nordic sweep has missed — a dedicated electronic music and sound art master at a state conservatoire. But it fails him on three counts simultaneously: (1) group teaching is in Danish; (2) it demands a music bachelor; (3) EUR 10,000/yr with an explicit no-scholarships policy. File it as a target for 2029+ only if he first completes a music bachelor and learns Danish — which is not his plan. Worth one email to lki@sdmk.dk asking whether a non-music BSc plus a strong 25-minute portfolio has ever been admitted, because that answer is genuinely unknown.

_rec.whatYouStudy: Three profiles: 3D Audio and Music Technology, Visual Media Creation, and Computer-Generated Imagery, each with mandatory core modules plus electives. The programme combines research, design and engineering, with students developing audiovisual concepts, prototypical media applications and scientific solutions for the media industry. The 3D Audio and Music Technology profile works on current audio-technology questions with a focus on 3D audio applied to sound design, radio drama (Hörspiel) and interactive audio installations, in modern studios. Engineering- and research-flavoured, not track production.
_rec.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED and stricter than previously recorded: an internationally recognised first degree (Bachelor, Diplom, First State Exam or equivalent); the programme "builds on a bachelor's degree in media technology or design" and expects approximately 210 ECTS — with fewer credits "eine individuelle Prüfung hinsichtlich der Anerkennung von Kompetenzen" (individual competency review) is carried out, with up to 30 ECTS potentially credited. Applicants must evidence at least 15 ECTS in engineering fundamentals ("Mathematik, Informatik, Physik, Nachrichtentechnik, Elektronik") AND at least 15 ECTS in media-related applications ("visuelle Gestaltung, Bild-/Ton-/Textkonzeption, Sounddesign"). German C1. The NC "lay in recent years approximately in the range of 2.2" (German grading), varying annually.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Check — half yes, half no. No music degree is required and the FAQ lists many qualifying bachelors from engineering, film and design fields "oder andere ähnlich geartete Studiengänge/Hochschulen", so non-media backgrounds are not excluded outright. His BSc easily covers the 15 ECTS in engineering fundamentals (mathematics, informatics). The problem is the second, equally mandatory 15 ECTS in media-related applications — visual design, image/sound/text conception, sound design — which a software-engineering curriculum almost certainly does not contain, plus a 180-vs-210 ECTS shortfall triggering an individual competency review. Formally arguable, practically weak without documented media/sound coursework.

Exemptions exist for a placement semester or leave of absence.

A Tunisian family income will generally place him in the lowest bracket. The EDISU bando normally opens in the summer preceding the academic year. The MAECI Italian Government scholarship (already in the database) is the other route. Programme-specific scholarships: none advertised. _rec.visaEligible: Yes. A Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello at a state conservatoire supports an Italian student visa (visto per studio) and permesso di soggiorno per studio. Non-EU applicants resident abroad must pre-enrol through the Universitaly portal before sitting the entrance exam, and are admitted against an annually published non-EU contingent (a reserved quota of places) — check the conservatoire's contingente for Musica Elettronica, as it can be very small.
_rec.recommendation: APPLY — this is one of the two best Italian targets for him and should be on the shortlist. The formal door is open to a foreign three-year degree holder, the conditional composition task is sample-based rather than score-based, and the technical test is non-binding — which is as accommodating as an Italian state conservatoire gets. Two things must be started immediately in the portfolio year: (1) Italian to B2, which his French will make faster than he expects, and (2) a genuine 'portfolio compositivo' of original electroacoustic work, not DJ mixes — the examiners want composition and DAW-based analytical fluency. The cost warning is real: at €3,500/year for non-EU non-residents Torino is the most expensive Italian conservatoire in this sweep and, unlike Bologna and Cuneo, that flat rate appears not to be reducible by proving low family income. Offset it by applying to EDISU Piemonte in the same cycle. Verify the non-EU contingent for Musica Elettronica early — a tiny quota can make an otherwise open programme unreachable.
