_rec.tuitionEU: Precise, from the official Regolamento tasse e contributi a.a. 2025/2026. For Corsi accademici di II livello (Bienni) in Direzione d'Orchestra, Direzione di Coro, Musica Applicata, MUSICA ELETTRONICA and Corsi Jazz: imposta di bollo €16.00 + assicurazione €10.00 + tassa regionale per il diritto allo studio €140.00 + contributo di funzionamento MAXIMUM €2,000.00. So the maximum all-in is €2,166.00 per year. Other bienni are capped at €1,800.00 contributo; trienni at €1,600.00. The contributo is reduced on a sliding ISEEU scale: students with ISEEU at or below €22,000 and meeting merit conditions are fully exonerated from the contributo; between €22,001 and €40,000 the contributo is computed as a percentage (6% or 7% depending on band) of the ISEEU amount exceeding €13,000, producing figures such as €154, €455, €787.50 and €1,071 across the sub-bands; the €30,001–€40,000 band shows €1,150. Above €40,000 the maximum applies. Admission application fee: €100.00 for Bienni (non-refundable, payable per application).
_rec.tuitionNonEU: THE RATE HE WOULD PAY, and this is the most important Italian finding in the sweep. Bologna's Art. 14 'Studenti internazionali non UE' states verbatim: 'Per gli studenti aventi la cittadinanza di Stati non appartenenti all'Unione Europea e non residenti in Italia sarà possibile accedere alle agevolazioni sul contributo di funzionamento solamente presentando le certificazioni ISEEE rilasciate dagli enti autorizzati.' In plain terms: a non-EU student CAN access the full income-based reduction — but ONLY by obtaining an ISEEE (Indicatore della Situazione Economica Equivalente all'Estero), the foreign-income equivalent of the ISEE, from an authorised body (a Patronato or CAF in Italy). Without it the rules are explicit and unforgiving: 'la mancata presentazione dell'ISEEE comporta l'attribuzione della Fascia di contribuzione più alta', and an ISEEE returning €0.00 'verrà in ogni caso rifiutato' and also triggers the highest band. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE: with a correctly filed ISEEE reflecting a typical Tunisian family income, he would very likely fall at or below the €22,000 threshold and pay little or no contributo — roughly €166/year in bollo, insurance and ER.GO tax. Without the ISEEE he pays the full €2,166/year. The paperwork is worth roughly €4,000 over two years.
_rec.otherFees: Imposta di bollo €16.00/year; assicurazione €10.00/year; tassa regionale ER.GO per il diritto allo studio €140.00/year (payable separately by postal order or bank transfer, not through PagoPA, and NOT reducible by ISEE). Admission application fee €100.00. Late-payment penalties (indennità di mora) apply. Students from the second year fuori corso pay a higher contributo (bands rising to €1,790 and a maximum around €2,000+). Diploma issue fee applies at graduation — amount UNVERIFIED.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Best case with ISEEE filed: roughly €166/year in unavoidable charges, i.e. approximately €330 over two years, plus the €100 admission fee. Worst case without ISEEE: €2,166/year, approximately €4,332 over two years. Bologna living costs are high for Italy — roughly €900–1,300/month, and student housing is notoriously scarce. Two-year all-in estimate approximately €25,000–34,000 depending on housing, before any ER.GO scholarship.
_rec.scholarships: ER.GO (Azienda Regionale per il Diritto agli Studi Superiori dell'Emilia-Romagna) runs income-based scholarships open to non-EU students, covering a maintenance grant, fee exemption and subsidised accommodation and meals. Combined with a low ISEEE this is the closest thing to full funding available in the Italian state conservatoire system. The ER.GO bando typically opens in summer. Obtaining the ISEEE through a Patronato or CAF is the prerequisite for both the fee reduction and the scholarship — treat it as the single most valuable piece of Italian paperwork. MAECI government scholarships (already in the database) are the alternative national route.
_rec.intakes: Autumn — Italian academic year. Admission exams in the spring/summer preceding.
_rec.applicationOpens: For a.a. 2025/26, applications for AMMISSIONI (all courses) and TRASFERIMENTI ran 17 March – 12 April 2025 (PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date). Expect a comparable mid-March opening in 2027 for a 2027/28 start. Non-EU applicants must separately complete Universitaly pre-enrolment before enrolling for the entrance examinations — this runs on the Ministry's own earlier calendar.
_rec.deadline: For a.a. 2025/26 the application deadline was 12 April 2025 (PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date). After the ranking list is published, admitted candidates must enrol within 10 days — a very short window that requires funds and documents to be ready in advance.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes. State conservatoire second-level diploma supports an Italian student visa and permesso di soggiorno per studio. The official international students page confirms: 'non-EU citizens not residing in Italy, before proceeding with their enrollment to the entrance examinations, will have to present a pre-enrollment request on the Universitaly portal.' Do not skip or delay this — missing the Universitaly window invalidates the whole application regardless of academic merit.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: UNCERTAIN, and less open than Torino, Rovigo or Cuneo. The stated requirement is completion of three-year electronic music studies 'or equivalent', which reads as pointing at a triennio in the discipline rather than at any bachelor's degree. Whether a Software Engineering BSc plus portfolio counts as equivalent must be confirmed in writing before investing in an application.
_rec.recommendation: WORTH PURSUING, but ask the eligibility question first. The syllabus is the best technical fit in this entire sweep for a software engineer — Sound Design Programming Techniques, Audio Systems and Programming Languages, Multimedia Programming, Interactive Multimodal Environments and Digital Audio Spatialisation are modules where his background is an asset rather than a gap. And the money can be close to zero if he files an ISEEE. But the entry wording is the strictest of the four Italian conservatoires here, so the very first action is an email to the segreteria didattica asking whether a foreign three-year Computer/Software Engineering degree plus a documented electronic music portfolio is accepted as 'equivalent' for DCSL34 admission. Do that in autumn 2026, before spending the portfolio year optimising for this specific programme. Two non-negotiable preparations regardless: Italian to a tested B2, and the ISEEE paperwork route mapped out with a Patronato well before enrolment. Caution him that this is an electroacoustic composition and sound design degree, not a route to commercial dance-music production — it would make him a far better sound designer and audio programmer than DJ.

Taught by working electronic-music composers/producers (Antanas Jasenka, Jonas Jurkūnas, Titas Petrikis, Andrius Laucevičius). Officially described as 'the first Master's degree of its kind in Lithuania'.

A mandatory entrance exam must be passed — failing or not taking it removes the applicant from the competition. Competition score = pass the entrance exam + motivation assessment (oral, 10-point scale, weight 0.1) + up to 4 bonus points (up to 2 for scientific/artistic activity; 0.5 each for ≥1 year field work experience, partial studies abroad ≥24 ECTS, completion of a talent-development programme, diploma with distinction).

Separately, the Lithuanian state master's scholarship scheme (2026 call, 70 grants) is restricted by nationality to Armenia, Azerbaijan, China (PRC and Taiwan), Georgia, Indonesia, Israel, Japan, Kazakhstan, Moldova, New Zealand, Philippines, South Korea, Ukraine, USA, Uzbekistan, Vietnam and foreign citizens of Lithuanian origin — TUNISIA IS NOT ON THE LIST (source: LMTA official admission page reproducing the national call).

On academic prerequisites it is unusually open (any bachelor's degree accepted, which suits a software-engineering graduate), and the syllabus is a near-perfect match for his stated goals (electronic music composition and performance, sound design studio, music programming, virtual instruments, game/film music). It is nevertheless unusable for him on three independent grounds: (1) teaching and assessment are 100% in Lithuanian, a language he does not have and cannot realistically reach by September 2027; (2) there are zero state-funded places, so he would self-pay roughly €15,900 in tuition alone for 90 ECTS — not 'genuinely cheap'; (3) Tunisia is excluded from the Lithuanian state master's scholarship nationality list, so no full funding route exists. Paying €11,200 for a communication master that touches sound once, in a language he does not speak, would be a poor use of a budget-sensitive candidate's money. _rec.program: Postgrado en Producción Musical y Artística (with The Music Station)

_rec.institutionType: Private university (Catholic, private, Madrid).
_rec.qualification: TÍTULO PROPIO, and specifically a 'Postgrado' of 30 ECTS lasting THREE MONTHS. VERIFIED on the official UFV page, which labels it 'Título Propio', '30 CTS', 'Duración 3 meses'. THIS IS NOT A MASTER. It is a short postgraduate certificate issued by UFV under its own authority.
_rec.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL. A UFV título propio at postgraduate-course level. Not ANECA-verified, not an official master, no RUCT entry, no doctoral access. At 30 ECTS it carries half the credit weight of a 60-ECTS master and one quarter of a 120-ECTS one. It should not be compared with the master's-level programmes elsewhere in this slice despite being marketed alongside them.
_rec.visaEligible: NO. This is now established on the regulation rather than inferred. Spain's official management criteria for estancia por estudios (Ministerio de Inclusión, June 2025, under RD 1155/2024) require studies of at least 91 calendar days, full-time enrolment defined as at least 90% of the credits, and a weekly teaching load of 'un mínimo de 20 horas semanales', with a narrow exception for intensive or concentrated programmes only where at least 12 of those hours are delivered in person. UFV publishes the timetable as Monday to Friday, 18:00 to 20:00 — exactly 10 contact hours per week. That fails the 20-hour general rule outright AND falls below the 12-in-person-hour exception floor. The programme's four-month span (September 2026 to January 2027) does clear the 91-day minimum, but the teaching load does not clear either threshold. He should treat this as definitively NOT a relocation route, not as an open question. Its only viable use is as a paid short course taken while already legally resident in Spain on some other basis.
_rec.focus: Practical music production: audio fundamentals, songwriting, pre-production, production and creative direction, post-production, mixing, mastering, industry contracts.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Module 1 — audio fundamentals, music theory, songwriting, Pro Tools training (41 hours). Module 2 — pre-production techniques and workflow (22 hours). Module 3 — production processes and creative direction (32 hours). Module 4 — post-production, mixing, mastering and industry contracts (57 hours). Roughly 152 contact hours in total. Taught inside a working production facility.
_rec.durationEcts: 30 ECTS over 3 months. Advertised edition runs September 2026 to January 2027, face-to-face on the Madrid campus and at The Music Station, Monday to Friday 18:00–20:00.
_rec.language: Spanish (castellano). No English option. HARD BLOCKER unless his Spanish is strong.

DISCREPANCY CONFIRMED on the official page: UFV separately publishes 'Reserva de plaza 960 €' and 'Matrícula 5.540 €', which sum to EUR 6,500 — EUR 400 more than the EUR 6,100 headline. This inconsistency is genuinely present on UFV's own live page and he must get the correct figure in writing before paying anything.

Note the contrast with UCAM, which names computer engineering graduates as a welcome profile, and with La Salle, which requires no music background at all.

_rec.facilities: Taught inside The Music Station, a professional production facility in Madrid, with practical work alongside industry professionals from Warner Music Spain. Includes Avid Pro Tools 100-level certification (PT101 + PT110) and a perpetual Ableton Live 12 Suite licence.
_rec.reputationSignals: Genuine industry setting (The Music Station) and a real Warner Music Spain collaboration, plus two concrete, portable, vendor-recognised credentials — the Avid Pro Tools certification and the Ableton licence are worth having in their own right. RED FLAGS: it is marketed alongside master's programmes but is a 30-ECTS, three-month, two-hours-a-night evening certificate; UFV's own published price breakdown does not add up (EUR 6,100 headline versus EUR 6,500 in components); and there is no degree at the end of it.
_rec.recommendation: AVOID for his purposes, and the reason is now legal rather than a judgement call. This is not a master — it is a 30-ECTS certificate delivered over three months of two-hour evening classes, and at 10 contact hours per week it falls below BOTH thresholds in Spain's student-authorisation criteria (20 hours per week generally, or at minimum 12 in-person hours for concentrated programmes). It therefore cannot support a student residence permit, which makes it useless as a September 2027 relocation plan regardless of its merits. Compounding that: its published entry profile expects prior music or sound training that he does not have; it is taught entirely in Spanish; it costs more per credit than La Salle's official Máster Universitario; and UFV's own page contradicts itself on the price by EUR 400. On the positive side it is a genuinely good short skills course — real facilities, Warner Music Spain professionals, and two portable certifications (Avid PT101/PT110 and a perpetual Ableton Live 12 Suite licence) that he would otherwise pay for separately. The only scenario where it makes sense is as a paid upskilling course taken once he is already legally resident in Madrid on some other basis. Do not build a relocation plan around it, and if he does ever enrol, get the correct total price in writing first.
_rec.verificationNotes: Fetched the official UFV programme page and cross-checked the visa position against the Spanish Ministerio de Inclusión 'Criterios de gestión sobre autorizaciones de estancia por estudios' (June 2025, RD 1155/2024), whose PDF text I extracted directly. CONFIRMED EXACTLY: Título Propio; 30 ECTS; 3 months; September 2026 to January 2027; Monday–Friday 18:00–20:00; presencial Madrid; taught in castellano; total price EUR 6,100 with reserva EUR 960 and matrícula EUR 5,540; perpetual Ableton Live 12 Suite licence; Avid Pro Tools PT101 + PT110 certification; Warner Music Spain collaboration. THE PRICE DISCREPANCY IS REAL AND REPRODUCED — EUR 960 + EUR 5,540 = EUR 6,500 against a stated total of EUR 6,100. VISA CONCLUSION UPGRADED FROM SPECULATION TO ESTABLISHED: the prior data called it 'effectively no' and 'unverified'; the published 10 hours per week can now be tested against the verified regulatory thresholds of 20 hours per week (general) and 12 in-person hours (intensive-programme exception), and it fails both, so the answer is a firm no rather than a probable one. The 91-day minimum duration is met, but that is not sufficient on its own. _rec.tuitionPerYear: €6,100 total for the 3-month programme, broken down as a €960 enrolment deposit plus €5,540 in tuition fees. (Note the components sum to €6,500 as published, so ask UFV to reconcile the arithmetic before paying.)
_rec.tuitionTotal: €6,100 total as headlined by UFV for the whole postgrado. No separate non-EU rate is published.
_rec.otherFees: €960 enrolment deposit (included in the headline total). No other application, materials or exam fees are published. The Pro Tools PT101 + PT110 certification and the Ableton Live 12 Suite perpetual licence are INCLUDED — a genuine and unusually transparent inclusion worth several hundred euros.
_rec.equipmentRequired: A laptop is implied. Crucially, the two big software costs are covered: an Avid Pro Tools official certification (PT101 + PT110) and a PERPETUAL Ableton Live 12 Suite licence are both included in the fee. This is the only programme in the slice that bundles a perpetual DAW licence.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: €6,100 in fees for three months, plus Madrid living costs for that period (roughly €3,000–€4,500), plus a laptop. Total around €10,000–€12,000 — but with no visa and no master-level qualification at the end.
_rec.paymentPlans: A €960 enrolment deposit followed by €5,540 in tuition fees. No instalment schedule, early-bird or referral discount is published.

_rec.facilities: In-person at the UFV Madrid campus, with direct collaboration with Warner Music Spain professionals — the strongest named industry partnership in this slice.
_rec.reputationSignals: The Warner Music Spain partnership is a real, checkable industry link rather than vague marketing, and the inclusion of Pro Tools certification plus a perpetual Ableton Live 12 Suite licence signals a school that expects students to actually work. UFV is an established private university. Honest naming ('Postgrado', not 'Máster'). RED FLAG: the published cost components (€960 + €5,540 = €6,500) do not match the stated €6,100 total — get the real number in writing.
_rec.recommendation: The best industry connection in the slice and refreshingly honest about what it is. But it is THREE MONTHS and 30 ECTS — it cannot be his primary plan. It will not get him a visa, it is not a master, and at €6,100 it costs almost as much as a full 9-month master elsewhere. My verdict: not a route to Spain. Genuinely interesting as a later add-on if he is already resident and wants a Warner-adjacent network plus Pro Tools certification. Listed here so he is not tempted by the 'Warner Music' branding into treating it as a degree.

Why that chance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's, but taught in Czech — language is the real gate

_rec.program: Zvuková tvorba (Sound Design) — navazující magisterský studijní program (N0211A310015)
_rec.university: Akademie múzických umění v Praze — FAMU (Film and TV School)
_rec.institutionType: Public film school / academy of performing arts (FAMU is one of the oldest and most famous film schools in the world)
_rec.focus: Film/Game Sound; Sound Design; Immersive Audio
_rec.language: Czech (the master's Sound Design track is NOT offered in English; FAMU's English-taught MFAs are Directing, Cinematography, Montage, Photography only)
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS (104 credits across 42 compulsory courses + 8 elective + 8 required-elective)
_rec.whatYouStudy: Film sound as the organising premise, taught as theory + studio practice: film sound mixing theory and spatial/multichannel formats, sound design and sound composition technique, sound dramaturgy, interactive audio for game design, multichannel post-production processing, and 'post-cinematic' uses of the audio component. Students run the sound on FAMU student films end-to-end (pre-production, production, post-production) and graduate as sound supervisors / sound designers / re-recording mixers. Roughly 7 students admitted per year — extremely small, high-contact cohort.
_rec.entryRequirements: Completed bachelor's degree (any institution). The department states candidates from other schools/fields may apply, but must demonstrate theory + practice at the level of the programme's own BA graduates. Czech-language study means a Czech certificate at B2/C1 (CCE) is in practice required to enrol and to keep tuition-free status. Full-time attendance only — no distance form. IELTS/TOEFL is irrelevant here; Czech is the gate.
_rec.portfolioSpec: Round 1 (documents only, candidate not present): (1) a LIST of all own sound works made during bachelor's study — audiovisual/multimedia works, music recordings, radio and theatre sound design — each with title, genre, director, production company, duration, year; (2) TWO audiovisual works on which the applicant made a substantial sound contribution, each with a detailed written explication; (3) the applicant's own theoretical work or an essay in the field; (4) a written project/statement for the master's study at FAMU (intended specialisation, expected outcomes, elective courses wanted at FAMU or other universities, interest in international internships). All works must be the applicant's own authorship, confirmed by a signed declaration. Works are uploaded by the separate works deadline (1 Sept in the 2026/27 cycle), not with the application form.
_rec.auditionSpec: Round 2 is an IN-PERSON oral examination in Prague: interview testing technical and artistic knowledge of the field, musical competence, and readiness for master's-level work, plus defence of the submitted works and the study project.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Check — formally yes, practically hard. The department page states candidates from other schools and fields may apply with any bachelor's degree, but adds they should show theoretical and practical knowledge equivalent to graduates of the programme's own bachelor track. There is no wording excluding a software-engineering BSc, but the portfolio (two finished audiovisual works with sound by the applicant) is the real filter.
_rec.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 2026/27 cycle (from the official specific-conditions PDF): applications 1 June – 13 August 2026; works/portfolio upload by 1 September 2026; Round 1 on 14 September 2026; Round 2 on 17 September 2026. NOTE the unusual summer cycle — for a September 2027 start expect an analogous June–August 2027 window, i.e. much later than most European deadlines.
_rec.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 1 June (2026 cycle opened 1 June 2026 via prihlaska.amu.cz). Application fee 990 CZK.
_rec.tuitionIntl: 0 CZK for study in Czech at a Czech public university — nationality is irrelevant under Czech law; only study in a foreign language is charged. (For comparison, FAMU's English-taught MFA programmes cost CZK 550,000 per year in 2026/27 — but none of those is Sound Design.)
_rec.scholarship: No dedicated scholarship found for Tunisians. Czech Government Scholarships (Developing Countries) do NOT cover Tunisia — the 2026/27 eligible list was Bosnia & Herzegovina, Georgia, Ukraine, Belarus (democratic forces), Guatemala and Jordan. AMU offers internal accommodation, social and merit scholarships (eligibility for non-EU students UNVERIFIED).
_rec.fundingLevel: Partial (tuition-free if studying in Czech; living costs self-funded)
_rec.stipend: Tuition waiver by law (Czech-taught). No stipend identified. UNVERIFIED whether AMU internal scholarships reach non-EU first-year master's students.
_rec.facilities: FAMU's Department of Sound (Katedra zvukové tvorby, Smetanovo nábřeží 2, Prague 1) runs mixing and post-production rooms integrated with the school's film production pipeline; the department describes 'a combination of technologies allowing students to finish films in first-class quality' and active collaboration with the Czech film industry for placements and contacts. Audio-recording teaching is partly delivered by HAMU's Sound Studio. Exact Dolby Atmos certification of FAMU rooms: UNVERIFIED. FAMU alumni include Miloš Forman, Věra Chytilová, Jiří Menzel, Emir Kusturica, Agnieszka Holland.
_rec.fitNotes: The most prestigious name on this slice and genuinely hands-on, but it is a FILM sound school, not a music-production school — nothing here trains him as a DJ or a club/electronic producer. Two obstacles compound: Czech at B2/C1 for the free route, and a portfolio of two finished audiovisual works with his own sound design, which he does not have. Realistic only as a 2028+ target after building a film/game sound reel; the June–August application window at least gives him a full extra year of preparation.

Why that chance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's, but taught in Spanish — language is the real gate

_rec.program: Máster en Producción de Música Electrónica
_rec.institution: SAE Institute Spain (SAE Creative Media Education)
_rec.institutionType: Specialist audio academy — international chain (SAE Institute, global network); SAE Barcelona additionally holds status as a private higher artistic-education school in music
_rec.qualification: DUAL AWARD, both non-official: (1) 'Máster de Formación Permanente' of 25 ECTS accredited by UDIMA (Universidad a Distancia de Madrid, a private university) — i.e. a TÍTULO PROPIO, plus a 'Máster Profesional' route for those without a degree; and (2) a Professional Diploma from SAE Creative Media Education.
_rec.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL. This is a Máster de Formación Permanente / título propio issued under UDIMA's own authority. It is NOT a 'Máster Universitario Oficial', it is NOT ANECA-verified, it does not confer EHEA official master status and it does not give access to a Spanish PhD. NOTE THE ECTS: 25 ECTS is very small — an official Spanish master is 60–120 ECTS. Calling a 25-ECTS course a 'máster' is legal in Spain for a título propio but it is exactly the marketing trap to be sceptical about. Separately, SAE Barcelona's UNDERGRADUATE Título de Grado en Música (240 ECTS, four specialities including Composición de Música Electrónica) IS official — authorised by the Generalitat de Catalunya and validated by AQU Catalunya — but that is a bachelor-level award and is a different thing entirely from this master.
_rec.visaEligible: UNVERIFIED / LIKELY PROBLEMATIC AS SOLD. SAE Spain publishes an international-students section that explicitly covers 'student visa' guidance for non-EU applicants, and states international applicants need a student visa. However a 25-ECTS, 8-month, non-official título propio is a weak basis for a Spanish student visa, which normally expects a full-time programme of substantial duration at a recognised centre. He must get written confirmation from SAE that THIS specific programme generates a visa-supporting acceptance letter before paying anything.
_rec.focus: Electronic music production, sound design, synthesis, live electronics, DJ-adjacent performance, mixing and mastering — the closest published match in Spain to this candidate's stated goal.
_rec.whatYouStudy: First semester: sound theory, music theory, MIDI protocol, audio processing, synthesizers, sampling, and mixing in Ableton Live and Logic Pro X. Second semester: advanced production, hardware synthesizers (Moog, Prophet/Dave Smith, Doepfer, Elektron, Roland, Akai), sound design, live performance, mastering, and industry career management. Includes the official Ableton Live Production Certificate.
_rec.durationEcts: 8 months full-time; 25 ECTS.
_rec.language: Spanish. SAE states Spanish-language proficiency is required for international students — a real obstacle for a Tunisian applicant with no Spanish.
_rec.intakes: Two intakes per year. Madrid: February 2026 and October 2026. Barcelona: October 2026 and February 2027. (These are the currently published dates; the SEPTEMBER/OCTOBER 2027 intake is not yet published — PRIOR CYCLE pattern, confirm new dates.)
_rec.entryRequirements: An official university degree (Grado, Licenciatura, Ingeniería, Arquitectura or Diplomatura) for the 60-ECTS Formación Permanente route; alternatively at least 2 years of documented professional experience for the 'Máster Profesional' route. Minimum age 18. Spanish-language proficiency. Completion of an admission questionnaire and an access interview.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES, explicitly. The stated requirement is 'una titulación universitaria oficial (Grado, Licenciatura, Ingeniería, Arquitectura o Diplomatura)' with no subject restriction — a BSc in Software Engineering satisfies it directly. No music degree, conservatory training or prior audio experience is demanded. This is the most accessible entry route in the whole slice for his exact profile.
_rec.portfolioSpec: No portfolio is published as a requirement. Admission is by questionnaire plus an 'entrevista de acceso' (access interview).
_rec.auditionSpec: No audition. An admission interview only.
_rec.englishTest: No IELTS required — and no English-language route either. Instruction and admission are in SPANISH, and SAE states Spanish proficiency is required of international students. He would need to reach a working level of Spanish (realistically B1–B2) before October 2027.
_rec.applicationOpens: Rolling — SAE runs continuous admissions with Open House Days that carry enrolment discounts.
_rec.deadline: No published hard deadline; rolling admission tied to the February and October start dates. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for a 2027 start.
_rec.tuitionPerYear: UNVERIFIED. SAE Spain does not publish the price of this master anywhere on its site. Do not accept a verbal quote — insist on a written fee schedule.
_rec.tuitionTotal: UNVERIFIED. For scale only, and from third-party listings rather than SAE's own pages: SAE's Audio Engineering Diploma (a different, undergraduate-level product) is quoted at around €8,700, ranging roughly €8,000–€10,000 depending on payment plan; SAE's BA/BSc (Hons) Audio Production is quoted at €14,000–€16,000 depending on plan. Neither figure is the price of this master and neither is officially published.
_rec.otherFees: UNVERIFIED — enrolment fee, materials fee and exam fees are not published.
_rec.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED as a formal requirement, but the syllabus is built on Ableton Live and Logic Pro X, so a capable laptop and at minimum an Ableton Live licence should be budgeted. An official Ableton Live Production Certificate is included in the programme.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED — SAE publishes no price for this programme. Estimating would be irresponsible.
_rec.paymentPlans: SAE España operates a published plan structure: Plan A is a single payment that carries an early-payment discount; Plan C is monthly instalments without the discount. Enrolling during an Open House Day reportedly lets students take monthly instalments at the discounted Plan A price. Exact figures UNVERIFIED.
_rec.scholarships: SAE Barcelona publishes an institutional discount schedule, but almost none of it reaches a Tunisian non-EU applicant. Available in principle: Active-student/alumni 40%; family members (siblings/cousins/relatives) 20%; disability ≥33% 30%; large-family status 10%; unemployment/ERTE 10%; excellence (9+ GPA in Spanish bachillerato or in SAE's own first year) 60%. The government routes — MEC scholarships and the Generalitat de Catalunya 2026-2027 non-university grants (income-based €1,700, relocation €2,700, basic €300–350, academic performance €50–125) — are for Spanish/resident students and do NOT apply to a newly arrived non-EU student. The Yamaha Europe Foundation grant (€1,000–€2,000, musicians under 25 at recognised European institutions) is the one realistically open award. Net realistic scholarship for this candidate: close to zero, other than possibly the Yamaha grant.
_rec.facilities: Barcelona campus: 2,700 m², seven professional audio studios, a production studio with an ICON D-CONTROL digital console, three post-production suites with colour correction, MIDAS F-16 analogue routing stations, MIDI stations with analogue and digital synthesizers, and a cinema mixing suite with 7.1 JBL monitoring and surround panner. Madrid campus: Solid State Logic 4000G+ console and a RAVEN MTX II Slate Digital console (SAE claims to be the only school in Europe with it). Official certification partners: Avid Pro Tools, Steinberg Cubase, Ableton Live, Wwise, Autodesk, Adobe.
_rec.reputationSignals: SAE is a large, long-established international audio-school chain with genuinely serious studio infrastructure — the equipment list is among the best in this slice. Positive signal: SAE Barcelona's undergraduate degree is officially recognised by the Generalitat and AQU, which shows the institution can meet Spanish quality standards. RED FLAGS: no published price for the master anywhere; a 25-ECTS award marketed as a 'máster'; the UDIMA título propio branding is easy to mistake for an official university degree; and a heavy discount architecture that is essentially inaccessible to non-EU students.
_rec.recommendation: The best CRAFT fit in Spain for his stated goal — this is literally an electronic-music-production master taught on Ableton and hardware synths, with no music degree required and his software-engineering BSc accepted outright. But three things make me cautious. First, it is a 25-ECTS título propio, not an official master: he must not be sold it as a Spanish degree. Second, the price is not published anywhere, which for a budget-sensitive self-payer is a serious governance problem — get it in writing before engaging. Third, it is taught in SPANISH and he has none, so he would need a year of language work before October 2027. My verdict: pursue it as a strong second option behind Berklee, but treat the unpublished fee and the visa question as blockers to clear in writing first.

_rec.university: Conservatorio Statale di Musica "Santa Cecilia"

_rec.degree: Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello (2nd-cycle diploma, EQF 7 — master-equivalent)
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 CFA (= 120 ECTS), 60 per year — VERIFIED from the official accreditation study-plan PDF (Riepilogo: Totale 120)
_rec.language: Italian. Foreign non-EU visa applicants enter via Universitaly pre-enrolment; Italian proficiency verification applies. Exact CEFR level for Santa Cecilia NOT published on the pages read.
_rec.focus: Electronic Music / Live Electronics; Electroacoustic and computer composition, sound technologies, multimedia, audio programming
_rec.whatYouStudy: VERIFIED module-by-module from the official DCSL34 accreditation PDF. YEAR 1 (60 CFA): Storia della musica elettroacustica 6; Ritmica della musica contemporanea 6; Esecuzione e interpretazione della musica elettroacustica — Ambienti esecutivi e di controllo per il live electronics 6; Composizione musicale elettroacustica 18 (INDIVIDUAL lesson); Informatica musicale 6; Tecnologie e tecniche della ripresa e della registrazione audio 2; Analisi compositiva 6; Acustica degli spazi musicali 4; Lingua straniera comunitaria 6. YEAR 2 (60 CFA): Storia della musica elettroacustica 6; Esecuzione e interpretazione — Ambienti esecutivi multimodali e interattivi 6; Composizione musicale informatica 18 (INDIVIDUAL); Informatica musicale 6; Tecnologie e tecniche della ripresa e della registrazione audio 2; Acustica degli strumenti musicali 4; a scelta dello studente 6; Prova finale (COME/02, composizione musicale elettroacustica) 12. THE DECISIVE DETAIL, newly verified from the published syllabus of Prof. Mario Salvucci (Informatica musicale COME/05): BIENNIO YEAR 1 = programming in Max MSP + java/javascript/nodejs; gen~/genexpr/C++ implementation of synthesis algorithms; adaptive filters; deterministic chaos, self-similar structures, strange attractors, flocking; MACHINE LEARNING — Markov chains, generative grammars, genetic algorithms, neural networks, GAN/StyleGAN/VAE, Stable Diffusion and GPT; ML libraries in Max (ml5js, MediaPipe, Magenta, Essentia); TensorFlow. BIENNIO YEAR 2 = introduction to C++ (control structures, functions, classes, pointers, dynamic memory) and to JUCE, culminating in implementing a full subtractive synthesizer AS A PLUGIN (MIDI in/sound out, oscillators, envelopes, polyphony and voice handling, modulation, filtering, GUI, host parameter communication); sound design of dynamic systems (artificial, natural, idiophone, mechanical, organic sources); Jitter, matrix/tensor operations, real-time video-audio interaction, OpenGL pipeline and SHADER PROGRAMMING, glitch/pixel-sort/databending algorithms, raytracing/raymarching; physical modelling (mass-spring, string, bowed instrument, waveguides). The composition syllabus (Prof. Silvia Lanzalone, COME/02) biennio year 1 covers composing the soundscape and acoustic ecology, intermedia Sound Art, SOUND INSTALLATION projects, multimedia/intermedia interaction with image and dance, electronic lutherie and sound design for augmented instruments (sensors, feedback systems, embedded systems); year 2 covers generative music, open forms, ecosystems and non-deterministic processes. Each year you deliver an original composition project supervised by the teacher.
_rec.entryRequirements: Diploma accademico di primo livello, OR a university degree (laurea) or equivalent recognised foreign qualification, plus passing the entrance exam. Non-EU visa applicants pre-enrol through Universitaly (the conservatory's own admission notice points explicitly to www.universitaly.it for entry, residence, enrolment and credential recognition). Registration is on Esse3 Cineca (https://consrm.esse3.cineca.it/) and the conservatory warns NOT to use SPID or CIE when registering. IELTS/TOEFL are irrelevant here — Italian is the operative language.
_rec.portfolioSpec: NOW VERIFIED — this was previously marked unverified and the actual spec is far lighter than assumed. From the official PDF 'PROGRAMMA DI AMMISSIONE A.A. 2025/2026 — CORSO ACCADEMICO DI SECONDO LIVELLO IN MUSICA ELETTRONICA' (https://conservatoriosantacecilia.it/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/musica-elettronica-biennio-25-26.pdf), there are TWO tracks. Candidates holding a first-level academic diploma IN MUSICA ELETTRONICA: Prova 1 = presentation and discussion of their first-level graduation thesis; Prova 2 = individual interview. CANDIDATES HOLDING ANY OTHER FIRST-LEVEL DEGREE — this is his track: Prova 1 = 'Presentazione di almeno due lavori originali – acustiche, elettroniche e/o audiovisive' (presentation of AT LEAST TWO original works — acoustic, electronic and/or audiovisual); Prova 2 = 'Colloquio individuale volto a verificare la motivazione e l'interesse all'approfondimento degli argomenti caratterizzanti il percorso di studi, nonché la coerenza del profilo formativo con gli obiettivi del corso' (individual interview on motivation, interest, and the coherence of the applicant's profile with the course objectives). NO minimum duration, NO minimum channel count, NO score requirement and NO stylistic restriction are published. 'Audiovisivi' is expressly allowed, so a video/audio piece counts. Caveat: this is the 2025/26 programme; confirm the 2027/28 version is identical.
_rec.auditionSpec: Two-part admission exam (works presentation + individual interview), on-site in Rome, Via dei Greci 18, registered through Esse3 Cineca. No live instrumental performance and no on-the-day improvised composition test is published for this course — a genuine advantage over Turin. Italian proficiency verification applies to foreign candidates; the exact format/level is NOT published on the pages read. NOT confirmed as remote-sittable.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — and the admission programme is explicitly built around it. The official programma di ammissione has a dedicated track headed 'Candidati in possesso di altro Diploma di Primo Livello', which is precisely a BSc holder from outside music. A Laurea/equivalent foreign qualification satisfies the title requirement; the two original works plus the coherence interview are the actual gate.

CORRECTION: the previously stated teaching attribution to Nicola Bernardini is NOT supported by the current published syllabi. The composition chair (COME/02) is M° Silvia Lanzalone, with M° Gemini also publishing programmes (Composizione Musicale Elettroacustica, Composizione Audiovisiva Integrata); Informatica musicale (COME/05) is M° Mario Salvucci. _rec.fitNotes: The strongest single find in this batch. Two things now verified change the picture completely: (1) the admission bar for a non-music graduate is just TWO original works plus an interview — the lowest documented bar of the six; (2) the biennio informatics syllabus is, in substance, an audio-software-engineering degree — he would spend year 2 writing C++ and building a polyphonic synthesizer plugin in JUCE, and year 1 doing ML for music in Max/TensorFlow. His BSc is a direct, compounding asset, not a handicap. The composition side is also more craft-oriented than assumed: sound design, DAW editing and montage, installations, augmented instruments, generative music. THE OBSTACLE IS ITALIAN — instruction is in Italian, the exam is on-site in Rome, and non-EU entry runs through Universitaly. Also note the aesthetic: this is art electronic music and sound art, not club or dancefloor production; it will make him a formidable sound designer and audio programmer, not a house producer. Realistic path: start Italian now (roughly 12 months to a usable level before the spring 2027 exam), and build two strong original audiovisual/electronic works.
_rec.verificationNotes: CONFIRMED on official sources: programme exists at 2nd-cycle level (DCSL34); full 120 CFA study plan verified module-by-module from the official accreditation PDF (MUSICA-ELETTRONICA.Biennio2021.2022.pdf, text extracted directly); portfolio spec verified verbatim from the official 2025/26 programma di ammissione PDF; biennio syllabi for Informatica musicale (Salvucci) and Composizione musicale elettroacustica (Lanzalone) extracted in full from official PDFs; 2026/27 admission cycle and its reopening for Musica Elettronica confirmed. CORRECTIONS MADE: (a) the previous claim that exercises 'explicitly require Csound or SuperCollider, Python for tendency masks, Pure Data and LilyPond, with audio editors expressly forbidden' is NOT supported by any current published syllabus and has been removed — SuperCollider and Pure Data appear in the TRIENNIO year 1, Python and LilyPond appear nowhere, and Lanzalone's triennio year 1 in fact teaches 'Sound Design tramite editing e montaggio sonoro tramite DAW', i.e. DAW editing is taught, not banned; (b) teaching attributed to Nicola Bernardini is not supported by current published programmes — corrected to Lanzalone/Gemini/Salvucci; (c) the 'progetti individuali di specializzazione' framing is not in the current admission programme and has been replaced with the verbatim published spec; (d) 'Composizione musicale informatica 18 CFA yr2' and the 12 CFA final project are confirmed correct. NOT CONFIRMED: tuition amount, LAZIODISCO figures, Italian language test level/format, studio inventory, 2027/28 dates.

_rec.program: DCSL34 — Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello in Musica Elettronica, indirizzo Composizione e Sound Design (Biennio)
_rec.institution: METS — Scuola di Musica Elettronica, Conservatorio di Musica "Giorgio Federico Ghedini" di Cuneo
_rec.institutionType: Specialist electronic music school (METS) within a state conservatoire in the AFAM system, under the Ministero dell'Università e della Ricerca
_rec.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. METS is the electronic music school of the Conservatorio di Musica 'G.F. Ghedini' di Cuneo, a state conservatoire; the conservatoire's own Manifesto degli Studi describes it as an 'Istituto di Alta Formazione Artistica e Musicale' and its contribution system runs on ISEE with the standard state-conservatoire machinery. METS uses its own domain (metscuneo.it) but it is the conservatoire's department, and its programmes are linked from and administered by conservatoriocuneo.it.
_rec.qualification: Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello in Musica Elettronica. The conservatoire's own Manifesto degli Studi states these biennio courses give 'il massimo titolo di studio musicale, equiparato alla Laurea specialistica ai fini dell'accesso ai pubblici concorsi' — a real state second-cycle degree, EQF 7.
_rec.accreditationStatus: State-accredited under ministerial course code DCSL34 in the MUR AFAM register. Genuine second-cycle qualification.
_rec.language: Italian. No English-taught route advertised.
_rec.languageRequirement: UNVERIFIED — no explicit level is published on the METS admission pages, which is unusual and worth confirming. Italian state conservatoires generally require or test B2. The oral admission components (motivational interview, discussion of works, music history) are conducted in Italian. Ask mets@conservatoriocuneo.it.
_rec.englishTest: None.
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years. Standard 120 CFA for a biennio di II livello — the METS study-plan page does not state CFA values inline (UNVERIFIED at source; request the piano di studi).
_rec.focus: Electronic music with a Composition and Sound Design track. METS is one of the few Italian conservatoires with a dedicated, separately branded electronic music school running a full ladder — a preparatory course, two triennio tracks (DCPL34 Musica Elettronica indirizzo compositivo, DCPL61 Tecnico del suono) and two biennio tracks.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Composition and sound design at second level. Detailed module list UNVERIFIED — request the piano di studi. The sister track (DCSL61, reported separately) covers sound engineering and multimedia.
_rec.entryRequirements: A 'titolo di primo livello' — a first-level diploma. Ideally a first-level academic diploma in Electronic Music or Sound Engineering, BUT the school states explicitly that holders of other conservatoire diplomas OR three-year university degrees may also apply if they have 'adeguata e documentata preparazione' in relevant subjects, with additional bridging coursework (debiti formativi) assigned to close gaps. The candidate's BSc plus a documented portfolio is a recognised route, with the 'documented preparation' condition being the thing his portfolio year must satisfy.
_rec.auditionSpec: IMPORTANT AND TWO-PART, and this is where the honest difficulty lies. FIRST EXAM (typically early September): a written component — waived for holders of first-level diplomas in Electronic Music or Applied Music, otherwise 'Analisi di un brano elettroacustico', analysis of an electroacoustic excerpt supplied by the examiners; plus an oral component covering presentation of the candidate's own electronic music pieces with documentation of live-set performances, demonstrated proficiency with audio editing, mixing and sound-processing software, knowledge of twentieth-century music, the history of electroacoustic music, acoustics and psychoacoustics, and a motivational interview. SECOND EXAM: waived for holders of first-level CONSERVATOIRE academic diplomas — but NOT waived for university graduates, so it WOULD apply to this candidate. It covers sung reading (lettura cantata), intonation and rhythm, ear training, and music history and historiography. That is a conventional musicianship examination and it is a genuine obstacle for someone with no conservatoire training. Note also, encouragingly, that the METS FAQ describes the biennio admission as consisting of a motivational interview with faculty at which candidates may present previous works — there is some tension between the FAQ's lighter description and the detailed exam page, which must be resolved directly with the school.
_rec.portfolioSpec: Before the exam date, candidates email to mets@conservatoriocuneo.it their audio and multimedia works plus a CV, using permanent sharing links (Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive). The oral exam then requires presentation of the candidate's own electronic compositions WITH DOCUMENTATION OF LIVE-SET EXECUTIONS — a requirement that directly rewards a DJ/producer practice, and is the only place in this entire sweep where live electronic performance is explicitly credited. His career direction is an asset here, not a liability.
_rec.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED — not published. Proficiency with audio editing, mixing and sound-processing software is examined, so a personal DAW setup is assumed.
_rec.facilities: UNVERIFIED in detail. METS is a dedicated electronic music school with its own identity and staff, which normally implies better-than-average studio access. Ask for a visit or a facilities list at mets@conservatoriocuneo.it.
_rec.tuitionEU: UNVERIFIED as to amounts. The conservatoire's Manifesto degli Studi 2025/2026 confirms the mechanism: 'Le tasse di frequenza — suddivise in massimo tre rate laddove previsto — sono organizzate in fasce di reddito', requiring a valid ISEE for university right-to-study purposes to be presented at first-year enrolment or re-enrolment, per a separate 'regolamento sulla contribuzione studentesca' annexed to the Manifesto. The METS FAQ confirms tuition is income-based (ISEE-dependent). Exact band amounts are in the Regolamento contributi — request it from the segreteria.
_rec.tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED as to amount, but the mechanism is documented and stated bluntly in the Manifesto: 'Gli studenti stranieri devono presentare l'attestazione ISEE parificato' — foreign students MUST present an ISEE parificato — and 'chi non presenta certificazione ISEE, verrà inserito nella fascia reddituale più alta', i.e. anyone who does not file it is placed in the highest income band. So, exactly as at Bologna: the ISEE parificato is the lever. Filed correctly on a Tunisian family income it should place him at or near the bottom band; not filed, he pays the maximum. Obtain the exact band table by requesting the Regolamento contributi from the segreteria before applying.
_rec.otherFees: Tassa regionale per il diritto allo studio (EDISU Piemonte) plus marca da bollo, payable with the first instalment via PagoPA through the Isidata platform. Amounts UNVERIFIED for Cuneo specifically — for reference the neighbouring Conservatorio di Torino bundles EDISU tax plus bollo at €156. Contributory irregularity blocks exam sittings, so payment discipline matters.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Cannot be stated precisely. On the Italian ISEE pattern with an ISEE parificato filed, expect low hundreds of euros per year; without it, the top band. Cuneo is a small Piedmontese city with the lowest living costs of any location in this sweep — roughly €550–800/month — and it is about 90 minutes from Turin. On a cost basis this is probably the cheapest genuinely relevant option found anywhere in the three countries.
_rec.scholarships: EDISU Piemonte income-based scholarships are open to non-EU students and can cover fee exemption, a maintenance grant and subsidised housing. In addition, METS itself advertises paid collaboration contracts (contratti di collaborazione) and a limited number of scholarships to offset costs — an unusual and genuinely useful provision for a self-funding student. MAECI government scholarships are the national alternative.
_rec.intakes: Autumn. Admission exams typically in early September, with teaching beginning in November.
_rec.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED as to the exact window. The conservatoire publishes an annual 'AMMISSIONI A.A. 20XX/20XX' notice — the 2026/2027 notice appeared in July 2026 (PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date). Admission exams typically take place in September, teaching starts November. Non-EU applicants must complete Universitaly pre-enrolment on the Ministry's separate and earlier calendar.
_rec.deadline: UNVERIFIED — governed by the annual ammissioni notice. Note that portfolio materials must reach mets@conservatoriocuneo.it before the exam date.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes. State conservatoire second-level diploma supports an Italian student visa and permesso di soggiorno per studio, subject to Universitaly pre-enrolment and the annual non-EU contingent.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: PARTIALLY. The formal entry route is open — three-year university degrees are explicitly named, with debiti formativi assigned to close gaps. But university graduates are NOT exempt from the second exam, which tests sung reading, intonation, rhythm, ear training and music history. That is a real musicianship hurdle for someone with no conservatoire background, and it is the single most important thing to resolve before committing. Set against it, the oral exam's demand for documented live-set performances is a requirement his intended practice actually satisfies.
_rec.recommendation: APPLY, alongside Rovigo — but resolve the second-exam question first, because it is the difference between a realistic target and a wasted application. Email mets@conservatoriocuneo.it in autumn 2026 and ask three things plainly: (1) as a holder of a foreign three-year Software Engineering degree, must I sit the second exam covering lettura cantata, ear training and music history, and if so what standard is expected; (2) can documented live-set and production work substitute for conservatoire musicianship in the assessment; (3) what does the Regolamento contributi charge a student in the lowest ISEE parificato band. If the answer on the second exam is workable, this becomes arguably the best-value option in the entire sweep — a dedicated electronic music school, the cheapest living costs of any location found, an ISEE-based fee system that should reduce his cost to very little, paid collaboration contracts available from the school itself, and an admission process that explicitly credits live electronic performance. If the answer is that a full musicianship examination stands, he should put Rovigo first and treat Cuneo as the second choice. Either way, the ear-training and basic musicianship gap is worth closing during the portfolio year — it is the recurring obstacle across every conservatoire route in Italy and Spain.

The national DCSL61 admission profile points toward an aptitude and motivational interview rather than a musicianship examination, and a sound-engineering degree has less reason than a composition degree to demand solfège and ear training. If that holds at Cuneo, the second exam that burdens the composition track may not apply here — which would make this the single most accessible state-recognised second-cycle audio qualification in all three countries for a software engineer with no music training. _rec.recommendation: INVESTIGATE AS A PRIORITY — potentially the best fit of all, and the most important open question left by this research. DCSL61 Tecnico del Suono is a real state second-cycle degree in sound engineering, at the same institution and cost base as the Cuneo composition track, but with an admission profile that appears to rest on an aptitude and motivational interview rather than conservatoire musicianship. For a software engineer with no music degree, that combination — an engineering-framed degree, an interview-based entry, an ISEE-scaled fee that a Tunisian family income should drive close to zero, and the cheapest living costs in the sweep — is potentially decisive. But the METS admission page did not publish separate requirements for this track, so nothing here is confirmed. Write to mets@conservatoriocuneo.it in autumn 2026 with the specific question: 'Per il biennio DCSL61 Tecnico del Suono — Ingegneria del Suono e Multimedia, quali sono i requisiti e le prove di ammissione per un laureato triennale straniero in Ingegneria Informatica? Si applica anche la seconda prova di lettura cantata ed ear training?' Get that answered before deciding between the Cuneo tracks. Meanwhile build a technical portfolio — multitrack recordings, mixes, masters, any DSP or audio-software work from his engineering degree — rather than a compositional one, since that is what this track will reward. _rec.institution: Žilinská univerzita v Žiline / University of Žilina, Fakulta elektrotechniky a informačných technológií (FEIT)
_rec.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. A verejná vysoká škola under Slovak Act No. 131/2002 Z.z.; the faculty's own admission rules state that students studying in Slovak pay no tuition, which is the statutory public-university regime. Programme is listed in the national register portalvs.sk (Portál vysokých škôl, run by CVTI SR under the Slovak Ministry of Education).
_rec.language: Slovak. Teaching, the entrance interview and the state examinations are in Slovak. No English-taught version of Multimediálne inžinierstvo is advertised.
_rec.languageRequirement: SLOVAK AT B1 — a certificate is explicitly required of applicants educated abroad (Czech-educated applicants exempted). This is a materially LOWER bar than the B2 Polish demanded by Polish public universities and lower than the de-facto fluency needed for a Czech talent exam. UNIZA also runs its own Slovak preparatory courses, which it points applicants toward.
_rec.qualification: Ing. (inžinier) — a real, state-recognised second-cycle degree in the Slovak system.
_rec.accreditationStatus: Accredited programme in the Slovak national register of accredited study programmes (portalvs.sk); supports a Slovak temporary residence permit for the purpose of study for a non-EU national.
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years, full-time (denná forma), 120 ECTS. UNVERIFIED - confirm on the faculty's programme sheet.
_rec.focus: Multimedia engineering with a declared audio specialization track — a genuine hybrid of technical and creative training, unusually so for an electrical-engineering faculty.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Theoretical foundations of informatics; digital and analogue processing of IMAGE AND SOUND SIGNALS; processing and transmission of multimedia streams over communication technologies, networks and services; interface and application development. Crucially, through the choice of compulsory-elective subjects a student can SPECIALISE NARROWLY IN AUDIO INFORMATION PROCESSING (as opposed to image or graphics). Creatively oriented subjects are built in so graduates can 'create and process multimedia works at an appropriate technical, aesthetic and artistic level'; the faculty names 'audio technician and designer' as a target job.
_rec.entryRequirements: A completed first-cycle (bachelor) degree. Foreign graduates need recognition of the equivalence of their qualification from a Slovak institution, or may request UNIZA itself to evaluate it — UNIZA doing the evaluation in-house is a significant convenience versus a separate ministry nostrification. Standard route: Slovak/Czech graduates in the same field with a weighted average up to 2.0-2.5 are admitted WITHOUT an entrance exam; others sit a test on bachelor state-exam topics requiring at least 61%. HOWEVER Multimedia Engineering is different — see audition/portfolio.
_rec.portfolioSpec: YES, AND IT IS THE UNUSUAL FEATURE THAT MAKES THIS PROGRAMME INTERESTING FOR HIM. Multimediálne inžinierstvo uses a SELECTIVE INTERVIEW that scores general IT knowledge TOGETHER WITH A CREATIVE PORTFOLIO AND MOTIVATION, up to 70 points combined. So a portfolio helps but is weighed alongside IT knowledge — exactly the blend he will have after a portfolio-building year on top of a software-engineering degree. It is not a conservatory-style talent examination and there is no aural/solfège test. Exact portfolio format UNVERIFIED — request the current 'Zásady a pravidlá prijímacieho konania' for Ing. study from the FEIT study office.
_rec.auditionSpec: No audition. An interview only.
_rec.equipmentRequired: None specified. He should assemble a portfolio of audio/multimedia work he can demonstrate and discuss.
_rec.facilities: FEIT multimedia and audio/video processing laboratories. UNVERIFIED specifics — ask the faculty whether there is studio access.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: YES. No music degree, conservatory training or performance ability is required or assessed. The interview tests IT knowledge plus creative motivation. His BSc Software Engineering is directly relevant to the informatics half of the assessment.
_rec.englishTest: None required. Slovak is the operative language; no IELTS/TOEFL is demanded for a Slovak-taught programme.
_rec.tuitionEU: 0 EUR for full-time study in Slovak within the standard length of study.
_rec.tuitionNonEU: 0 EUR — THE SAME AS FOR SLOVAKS. FEIT's own admission rules state that international students studying IN SLOVAK pay no tuition, while those studying in another language pay fees set by UNIZA regulations. As in the Czech Republic, the fee attaches to the language of instruction, not to nationality. A Tunisian national on this Slovak-taught Ing. programme pays zero tuition. Foreign scholarship recipients are governed by their sponsorship agreements.
_rec.otherFees: Application fee UNVERIFIED (Slovak public universities typically charge 20-40 EUR) — check the e-application portal at https://vzdelavanie.uniza.sk/prijimacky/index.php. Žilina living costs are the lowest in this slice, roughly 450-700 EUR/month.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Tuition 0. Realistic total ~11,000-17,000 EUR for the two years, entirely living costs. Add a Slovak preparatory course if he takes UNIZA's.
_rec.scholarships: The Governmental Scholarships of the Slovak Republic (already in the database) is the full-degree funding vehicle for non-EU nationals and would apply here. UNVERIFIED whether UNIZA offers its own entry scholarship — ask the FEIT study office.
_rec.fundingLevel: Full (tuition free) — and potentially fully funded if combined with the Slovak Government Scholarship.
_rec.intakes: One annual intake, September start.
_rec.applicationOpens: Typically opens in the winter/spring preceding the academic year via the UNIZA e-application portal.
_rec.deadline: 30 April 2026 for entry in 2026/2027. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. For SEPTEMBER 2027 entry expect a deadline around 30 April 2027 — again later than his assumed Oct 2026-Feb 2027 window. But the Slovak Government Scholarship application, if he pursues it, will close much earlier and drives the real timeline.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes — accredited public university, full-time Ing. programme, supports a Slovak temporary residence permit for study. Note the qualification-recognition step must be arranged before enrolment; UNIZA can perform the evaluation itself.
_rec.recommendation: THE BEST BALANCED OPTION AND A CLEAR GAP FIND — Slovakia was thinly covered and this programme is the country's most under-recognised audio route. Free tuition for a Tunisian, an admission process that scores a creative portfolio ALONGSIDE IT knowledge rather than instead of it, an explicit audio-processing elective track, no audition, no aural test, no music degree needed, and the lowest living costs of any option here. The only real gate is Slovak at B1 with a certificate — the mildest language requirement in this slice, and genuinely reachable in the twelve months he has before an April 2027 deadline. Actions: (1) enrol in a Slovak course now and target a B1 certificate by early 2027; (2) e-mail the FEIT study office for the current 'Zásady a pravidlá prijímacieho konania' for Ing. study and ask what the creative portfolio must contain for Multimediálne inžinierstvo; (3) run the Slovak Government Scholarship application in parallel. Rank this second only to ČVUT, and first if he is willing to learn a language.

It is the only programme in this whole four-country sweep that puts immersive/spatial audio in the master's core. But three things close it. THIRD, HE IS THE WRONG APPLICANT: entry runs through an undisclosed creative competition in a screen-sound discipline, with no published open-entry rule, no portfolio spec, and no published price. VERDICT: do not apply. _rec.visaEligible: NO in practice — and the legal reasoning in the previous record needed correcting rather than just repeating. The correction: part-time study is not legally excluded. Section 16b(1) AufenthG grants a residence permit as an ENTITLEMENT ('wird erteilt') for Vollzeitstudium — full-time study. Part-time study appears separately in section 16b(5), where the permit 'kann erteilt werden' — purely DISCRETIONARY. So the honest statement is not 'part-time is refused by law' but 'part-time carries no entitlement, only official discretion'. That discretion will not be exercised in his favour, for a reason specific to this programme: it delivers roughly 20 attendance days over two years and presupposes concurrent employment in the German media industry. An Ausländerbehörde will not accept five contact days a semester as a residence purpose, and he cannot hold the German media job that would supply an alternative residence basis, because he would need a residence permit to take it. The requirement and the remedy are circular.
_rec.recommendation: AVOID — and the case against it is now stronger than the previous record made out, on three independently fatal grounds. First, entry: the German page requires a year of experience in the media and communications industry, not merely a year of any work; the English page's looser wording is not the governing text and the previous record was misled by it. He has none. Second, visa: this is a part-time programme with about 20 attendance days total, built for people already employed by Central German media companies. Part-time study carries no residence entitlement under section 16b(1), only discretion under 16b(5), and no authority will grant it on this contact load. He cannot take the job that would fix the problem without the permit the job is supposed to justify. Third, and new: the programme itself is listed as not accredited — the university's system accreditation (held since April 2023) covers the institution and lets it seal its own programmes, but this one launched in winter 2025/26 and has not yet been sealed. None of this is a knock on the institution, which is a legitimate state UAS charging EUR 0 tuition and EUR 107 a semester. It is simply not a migration route, and it is not open to him. Spend no application effort here for September 2027.

_rec.program: Künstlerische Musikproduktion (Artistic Music Production) – Master of Music
_rec.university: Robert Schumann Hochschule Düsseldorf – Institut für Musik und Medien (IMM)
_rec.institutionType: Public conservatory / Musikhochschule
_rec.durationEcts: 4 semesters (2 years). ECTS total not stated on the programme page or the Modulplan page — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.language: German. Confirmed on the RSH Deutschkenntnisse page: Goethe-Institut certificate B2 is required specifically for 'die Master-Studiengänge Klang und Realität sowie Künstlerische Musikproduktion'. Online language courses without a final examination are NOT accepted; a certificate of attendance is NOT accepted. Useful nuance: an applicant who passes the aptitude test but lacks the certificate at semester start may supply it during the first year, enrolling meanwhile with the legal status of a 'Kollegstudierender'.
_rec.focus: Music Production; Recording / Engineering (two majors: classical acoustic, and jazz/pop)
_rec.whatYouStudy: Two majors: Classical Acoustic Music Production, and Jazz and Pop Music Production. Three interwoven strands over four semesters: practical production work across genres and formats using the most recent production methods; instrumental/vocal tuition with ensemble performance; and technical methodology plus musical analysis including acoustics and ear training. Goal is artistically independent, methodically grounded professional production work. CONFIRMED on the official page — genuinely the most production-focused public master in this batch.
_rec.entryRequirements: CRITICAL CORRECTION — the official Eignungsprüfungsanforderungen page states: 'Voraussetzung ist der Nachweis eines abgeschlossenen künstlerischen Bachelor- oder Diplomstudiums oder eines gleichwertig anerkannten künstlerischen Studiengangs mit Schwerpunktsetzung im Bereich Musikproduktion (z.B. Tonmeister, Soundengineering, Musikregie etc.). Im Sinne eines künstlerischen Abschlusses gilt auch ein Bachelorstudium im Studiengang Ton und Bild.' A completed ARTISTIC bachelor or diploma (or equivalent recognised artistic degree) WITH AN EMPHASIS IN MUSIC PRODUCTION is mandatory. Plus German B2 (Goethe), plus passing the concentration-specific Eignungsprüfung. Aptitude-test fee €50 for the first application, €10 for each additional application (confirmed).
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: No — this is a hard correction to the earlier 'Check'. The requirement is not merely 'a bachelor's degree': it must be an artistic bachelor/diploma with a music-production emphasis, and the examples given are Tonmeister, sound engineering, Musikregie, or RSH's own Ton und Bild bachelor. A BSc in Software Engineering is neither artistic nor production-focused in the sense meant, so he is formally ineligible, before the audition is even considered.
_rec.portfolioSpec: NOW EXACT (from the official Eignungsprüfungsanforderungen page). Jazz/Pop major pre-selection: a portfolio of FOUR TO SIX already-realised works (or excerpts) in different styles from the jazz/popular-music production field; one audio file/track package per work sample; TOTAL DURATION 15–20 MINUTES; accepted formats stereo, 5.1/7.1 or Atmos; stereo mixes as stereo .wav, multichannel as clearly labelled mono .wav files (5.1/7.1) or as an ADM file (Atmos); each work sample accompanied by a short description of how it was made. PLUS unedited videos of the applicant's own artistic performance on instrument/voice (jazz/pop) with improvisation or ad-libs, tempi and styles varying, own composition allowed, max 20 minutes total — with an important alternative for keyboard/jazz piano: 'die Einreichung von bis zu drei Stücken mit Improvisation mit Hilfe von elektronischen Instrumenten wie Keyboards, Synthesizern, DAWs (z.B. Ableton live) mit deutlich erkennbarem spielerisch-handwerklichem Anteil sowie erkennbar eigener Soundgestaltung' (up to three pieces with improvisation using keyboards, synths or DAWs such as Ableton Live, with clearly recognisable playing craft and own sound design). PLUS a motivation letter referencing the chosen major and a CV with certificates. (Classical major differs: 5–6 works, 30–45 minutes, plus three works from different stylistic periods on video.)
_rec.auditionSpec: Yes — a substantial ON-SITE examination (Präsenzprüfung) in Düsseldorf, in four parts: (1) artistic presentation on instrument or voice with the same repertoire as the pre-selection, plus a prepared solo transcription (or a short a cappella piece for jazz/pop voice) AND sight-reading / sight-singing; six copies of the scores or lead sheets must be brought. (2) An UNPREPARED practical task in the chosen major, e.g. a mix or an edit, typically one to two hours. (3) Written examinations of both musical and technical hearing: musical ear (~40 min: dictations from piano and from recordings, intonation hearing, error detection, short aural analysis, instrumentation hearing) and technical ear (~40 min: listening examples including technical artefacts, level judgement, formant hearing). (4) A Fachgespräch with the selection panel, max 30 minutes. Fee €50.
_rec.applicationOpens: Not published; the muvac application links are opened roughly one month before each deadline (as stated for the sister programme).
_rec.deadline: 1 March, published as a standing annual deadline: 'Der Bewerbungsschluss zum Wintersemester ist der 1. März.' Aptitude tests for Künstlerische Musikproduktion are held for the WINTER SEMESTER ONLY ('Für die Masterstudiengänge Künstlerische Musikproduktion und Musikfilmregie ... gibt es Eignungsprüfungen ausschließlich zum Wintersemester'). So a September/October 2027 start means applying by 1 March 2027. The date is a standing rule rather than a prior-cycle artefact, but confirm it is unchanged when the 2027 links open. (The earlier note that entry is possible in winter OR summer was wrong for this programme.)
_rec.tuitionIntl: No tuition fees (NRW; no non-EU tuition). €50 aptitude-test fee for the first application, €10 for each further application, non-refundable even if the application is withdrawn. Semesterbeitrag payable; the RSH page only links a PDF for WS 2026/27 and the amount could not be read — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.fundingLevel: Partial (tuition-free) — but academically inaccessible to him, so the funding position is moot
_rec.scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies for Artists and Architects (music); RSH lists 'Stipendien' internally but no scheme open to a first-year non-EU student was confirmed — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.stipend: DAAD figures as above (€992/month plus insurance, €460/year study allowance, travel allowance). No RSH institutional stipend confirmed — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.facilities: Institut für Musik und Medien studios. The Atmos requirement in the portfolio spec ('Atmos-Mischungen ... als Audio-Definition-Model (ADM) Datei') implies immersive-capable facilities, and RSH runs the Ton und Bild engineering degree jointly with HS Düsseldorf. Specific console, room and immersive-suite inventory is not published on the pages checked — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.fitNotes: Content-wise this is the best genuine music-production master in the batch — a real Jazz/Pop production track, Atmos-aware, with mixing and editing as examined craft. It is also the most firmly closed to him. The prerequisite is an artistic bachelor with a music-production emphasis (Tonmeister, sound engineering, Musikregie, or RSH's Ton und Bild), which a software-engineering BSc is not; and even if that were waived, the on-site exam demands an instrumental/vocal performance with sight-reading, a live mixing task, and 80 minutes of written musical and technical ear tests, all in German at B2. Realistic only after a production-focused artistic bachelor plus years of instrument and ear training. Worth noting as a long-term aspiration and as a source of a training checklist — the Ableton/synth alternative for the keyboard performance shows what standard would eventually be expected — but not a 2027 target.
_rec.verificationNotes: Programme page fetched (majors, four semesters, three strands, B2, proficiency test, 1 March deadline all confirmed). The German Eignungsprüfungsanforderungen page (rsh-duesseldorf.de/studienbewerbung/anforderungen/master/kuenstlerische-musikproduktion) was scraped in full, which produced two major corrections: (1) the required prior degree is an ARTISTIC bachelor/diploma with a music-production emphasis — so acceptsNonMusic moves from 'Check' to 'No'; (2) the portfolio spec is now exact (4–6 works, 15–20 min total, stereo/5.1/7.1/Atmos, .wav or ADM, short descriptions, plus max 20 min of unedited performance video, plus motivation letter and CV). The official deadlines page confirmed the standing 1 March winter deadline and that this programme has a WINTER-ONLY aptitude test — correcting the earlier 'winter or summer' note. The Deutschkenntnisse page confirmed B2 Goethe, rejected online courses without an exam, and the Kollegstudierender grace route. The Eignungsprüfungsgebühr page confirmed €50 / €10. For a related degree the examination committee decides equivalence on the file, a letter of motivation and possibly an interview. _rec.facilities: Shared with the Hochschule für Musik Detmold / Musikwissenschaftliches Seminar Detmold-Paderborn.
_rec.intakes: CONFIRMED: winter semester primarily; summer semester only if winter places remain unfilled.
_rec.applicationOpens: CONFIRMED: winter semester from early June; summer semester from early December.
_rec.deadline: CONFIRMED on the official page: winter semester 23 October, summer semester 21 March. WARNING RESTATED AND STILL VALID — a 23 October deadline falls AFTER the semester has started and leaves no time whatever to obtain a visa. Paderborn's own general winter-semester application deadline is 21 September with enrolment by 30 September (extended to 23 October), which confirms these are late domestic dates, not international ones. An international applicant must apply far earlier via uni-assist; he should ask the Studierendensekretariat in writing for the international deadline before building any plan on 23 October.
_rec.tuitionEU: No tuition fee. CONFIRMED.
_rec.tuitionNonEU: CONFIRMED IDENTICAL — no tuition for non-EU nationals in NRW.
_rec.otherFees: CONFIRMED: semester contribution for winter semester 2026/27 is EUR 351.15 in total, published as Sozialbeitrag EUR 110.00 + AStA EUR 12.50 + Deutschlandsemesterticket EUR 226.80 + Kulturticket EUR 1.85. The semester ticket is already included in that figure. uni-assist handling fee extra (EUR 75 first application, EUR 30 further).
_rec.totalCostEstimate: About EUR 702/year in semester contributions at the confirmed 2026/27 rate, plus German-course fees, plus living costs in Paderborn (one of the cheaper German university towns), plus the blocked account for the visa.
_rec.scholarships: None programme-specific. DAAD / Deutschlandstipendium only.
_rec.englishTest: None — German-taught. IELTS/TOEFL is not the relevant test.
_rec.visaEligible: YES. Full-time state M.A. at a state university.
_rec.recommendation: Every factual claim in the previous record held up: M.A., zulassungsfrei, 20 places, no audition, deadlines 23 October and 21 March, EUR 351.15 a semester. The problem is not accuracy, it is fit. This is an academic degree ABOUT popular music — he would spend two years analysing the music industry in German, not producing. It does not advance the DJ/producer craft by a single hour of studio time, and it demands DSH/TestDaF-level German, which is the same 12-18 month investment TH Köln demands but for a much smaller payoff in his chosen direction. Two specific risks the previous record understated: the committee may simply rule a software-engineering BSc not fachverwandt to musicology and reject him on subject grounds regardless of how open the admission is, and the published 23 October deadline is a domestic date that is visa-impossible for a Tunisian national. Keep it only as a low-priority visa-and-network route into Germany, and only if he independently decides he wants the academic study of music culture for its own sake.

Austria's FH system is genuinely ambiguous by design: FH programmes are run by a legally separate provider company (here FH OÖ Studienbetriebs GmbH) but are publicly co-financed by the federal government per study place and are state-accredited under the Fachhochschulgesetz by AQ Austria. How I know it is on the public side: it charges exactly the statutory federal tuition rates (EUR 363.36 / 726.72) and collects the ÖH fee — a purely private provider sets its own price. The company's shareholding (the Province of Upper Austria) is not stated on the pages I opened — that ownership detail is UNVERIFIED; confirm at studienbeitrag@fh-ooe.at or in the company register if it matters to him.

Austrian FH master's degrees are accredited under the Fachhochschulgesetz and quality-assured by AQ Austria; the award here is 'Master of Arts in Arts and Design', a standard Austrian FH master title. Admission supports the §64 NAG student residence permit for a non-EU national.
_rec.qualification: Master of Arts in Arts and Design (MA). 4 semesters, full time. A genuine second-cycle degree — not a 'Lehrgang' or a certificate.

It fills a real gap in the database (FH OÖ Hagenberg was not covered) and it is genuinely cheap and genuinely accredited, but for this candidate two independent things block it: teaching is entirely in German with 'good proficiency in German' written into the admission rule, and admission demands 60 ECTS of audio/video/multimedia/animation credit in the bachelor, which a Software Engineering BSc will not have. He should not spend time on it unless (a) his transcript unexpectedly shows 60 ECTS of media coursework AND (b) he commits to German to B2, in which case the 2028 intake, not 2027, is the realistic target. Sound reinforcement and sound design can be taken as additional emphases regardless of specialisation. A master project is central.

Diplom) in einem facheinschlägigen Studium Tonmeister_in" — i.e. a Tonmeister-type degree.
