(b) Instrument/voice video: for Popularmusik, 2 jazz/popular works with improvisation or ad libs (an own composition is allowed; for piano, one piece may be improvisation using keyboards/synths/DAWs such as Ableton Live with clearly audible playing craft and own sound design); band or play-alongs permitted; total video duration max 15 minutes. (c) Piano video if piano is not your main instrument. (d) PORTFOLIO — Popularmusik: SIX popular-music productions in different styles, produced, recorded and mixed substantially by you, at least three with vocals and at least two involving recording of acoustic instruments, all delivered as stereo audio (5.1/Dolby Atmos versions optional), each at least 2:30 and max 30 minutes in total, plus written documentation of 7,000–12,000 characters (approach, microphone choices, session photos, DAW screenshots, challenges, critical reflection). Klassik: three music-recording projects, two pure stereo audio productions with different ensembles plus one free project (audio or video, stereo/5.1/Dolby Atmos, with a stereo version supplied), total 20–40 minutes, plus the same 7,000–12,000-character documentation. Filmton: three film-sound projects (production sound, sound design, mixing), two with more complex sound design or mixing and one at least in 5.1, plus documentation. Formats: one work per file, .wav (5.1 as labelled single wavs), ADM BWF for Atmos, .mp4/.mov video, max Full HD, max 8 GB per file, documentation as PDF.
_rec.auditionSpec: Two-part commission exam. Part 1 is the submitted video/audio package. If the commission invites you, Part 2 is an ON-SITE oral exam at the mdw in Vienna: a practical studio task (e.g. editing, mixing or sound design), questions on music theory and music literature, ear-training tasks, analysis of a listening or film example, questions on acoustics and audio/studio technology, and a technical discussion of your portfolio.

_rec.program: Master mention Musicologie — parcours Création-Production en musiques actuelles (CPMA) (the faculty also lists the track under the name 'Écoute critique et production en musiques actuelles')
_rec.institution: Université de Strasbourg, Faculté des arts, Département de musique
_rec.institutionType: Public university (EPSCP)
_rec.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. How I know: Université de Strasbourg is a state university; its own tuition page publishes the ministerially-set national rate (255 €) and the differentiated non-EU rate, and its exemption decisions are taken by an institutional committee — both public-sector mechanisms.
_rec.qualification: Diplôme national de master, mention Musicologie. Real second-cycle state degree supporting a student residence permit. RNCP number not shown on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.accreditationStatus: State-accredited diplôme national de master at a public university.
_rec.language: French (stated explicitly on the official catalogue page). An English course is included in the curriculum but instruction is French.
_rec.languageRequirement: French at C1 — listed as a mandatory prerequisite on the official catalogue page ('bonne maîtrise de l'expression et de la rédaction en français', C1). He is fluent in French, so this is one of the few programmes where his language profile is an advantage; but he should expect to have to evidence C1 with a DELF/DALF or TCF certificate for the visa file.
_rec.englishTest: None required.
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years, 120 ECTS, 724 total teaching hours, in-person only (no distance option). Ends with a dissertation articulated with a public recital/production of roughly 60 minutes.
_rec.focus: Music production and studio technology in the service of creation, in popular/contemporary music (musiques actuelles) — the closest thing in this sweep to his stated goal of music production and electronic music.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Named on the official faculty page: critical listening and technical ear training; composition and orchestration with digital audio workstations; sound recording, mixing and mastering; analogue synthesis; composition for audiovisual and video games; sound design and artistic direction; professional practice in music production, publishing and copyright. Project-based pedagogy with substantial autonomous work; a 120-hour internship. Named outcomes: sound engineer, music producer, composer for audiovisual/games, sound designer, artistic director.
_rec.entryRequirements: The official page states eligibility as 'Tout étudiant titulaire d'une licence de musique (ou d'un diplôme étranger équivalent)'. Mandatory prerequisites listed: advanced DAW skills; strong practical musicianship; composition and/or production competence; knowledge of sound reinforcement, acoustics or popular-music instrumentation; knowledge of the contemporary music industry; C1 French; academic research and writing competence; and music-theory fundamentals (score reading, analysis, composition), history and aesthetics of popular music.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: NO, in practice. The official entry rule is a music licence or an equivalent foreign degree, and the published prerequisites include score reading, analysis and orchestration. A BSc Software Engineering with no conservatoire training and no portfolio does not meet the stated conditions. He could only argue equivalence, and would still have to demonstrate the musicianship prerequisites.
_rec.portfolioSpec: Not explicitly published on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED. Given the prerequisites, expect production work to be assessed; ask the programme director, Sébastien Lebray (lebray@unistra.fr).
_rec.auditionSpec: Not published — UNVERIFIED. The degree concludes with a public recital of ~60 minutes, which indicates a performing/producing standard is expected at entry. Confirm with the department.
_rec.equipmentRequired: Not published — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.facilities: Studio-based teaching (recording, mixing, mastering, analogue synthesis) at the Faculté des arts, 14 rue René Descartes, Campus Esplanade. Specific studio inventory not published — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.intakes: September (annual).
_rec.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — no dated calendar on the pages I opened. Route: applications go through Mon Master (monmaster.gouv.fr), EXCEPT non-European candidates resident in a country covered by the Études en France procedure. Tunisia is an Études en France country, so he would apply through Campus France Tunisie / Études en France, not Mon Master — and that calendar opens in autumn.
_rec.deadline: UNVERIFIED — confirm with the Faculté des arts and with Campus France Tunisie for the Études en France campaign closing date for a September 2027 intake.
_rec.tuitionEU: 255 € for master level, published on the University of Strasbourg's own tuition page (2025-2026).
_rec.tuitionNonEU: THIS IS THE RATE HE WOULD PAY: 3 950 € at master level for non-EU (extracommunautaire) students, published on the University of Strasbourg's own tuition page (2025-2026). Strasbourg operates a Tuition Fee Exemption Committee through which international students may individually request exemption from the differentiated fees — the exemption rate and criteria are not stated on the page I opened (UNVERIFIED; ask the Service de la vie universitaire). A transitional exemption exists only for students already enrolled at Unistra in 2023/24 and 2024/25, which would not cover him.
_rec.otherFees: CVEC payable in addition — amount not stated on the page I opened, UNVERIFIED.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: ~3 950 €/year plus CVEC plus Strasbourg living costs, unless the exemption committee reduces the fee to the national 255 €. No official living-cost figure — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.scholarships: None specific to this programme on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED. The relevant lever is the Unistra Tuition Fee Exemption Committee plus the national Eiffel route already in the database.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes — public university, national master; but note the applicant route for Tunisians is Études en France rather than Mon Master.
_rec.recommendation: On content this is the best match in France for what he actually wants — mixing, mastering, analogue synthesis, DAW composition, music for games, and the business of production, in a real state master's degree at low national fees if he wins an exemption. On eligibility it is the worst match in this batch: the official entry rule is a music licence, and the published prerequisites (score reading, analysis, orchestration, existing production competence) describe someone with years of formal musical training. He has none. Do not build the plan around it. If he wants to keep it alive, the only route is (a) write to Sébastien Lebray in autumn 2026 asking whether a non-music bachelor with a strong production portfolio can be considered under 'diplôme étranger équivalent', and (b) spend 2026-27 producing enough finished, mixed and mastered work to make that argument. Realistically this is a 2028 target, not 2027.

_rec.program: DNSEP Design mention Design sonore (années 4 et 5)
_rec.university: École supérieure d'art et de design TALM — site du Mans (TALM-Le Mans), in partnership with IRCAM, ENSCI-Les Ateliers and Le Mans Université / LAUM
_rec.degree: DNSEP (Diplôme National Supérieur d'Expression Plastique) conférant le grade de master
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years (années 4 and 5, semesters 7-10). Entry requires 180 ECTS for semester 7 or 180+60 for semester 9. Total programme ECTS not stated on the official pages — UNVERIFIED (French DNSEP 2e cycle = 120 ECTS).
_rec.focus: Sound Design (industrial, object, environmental, multimodal, UX) + Sonic Arts + some Immersive/Spatial Audio
_rec.institutionType: Public école supérieure d'art et de design (Ministère de la Culture), partnered with a research institute (IRCAM), a design school (ENSCI) and a university acoustics lab (LAUM/CNRS)
_rec.language: French. CONFIRMED: 'Les candidat·s étranger·ères non-francophones doivent maîtriser suffisamment la langue française pour lire et dialoguer. Ils et elles doivent également justifier au minimum du niveau B2 au TCF … ou au DELF.' A compulsory English module ('Anglais, le langage comme matière, matériau et matériel') sits in UE3.
_rec.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED (livret de formation). Semesters 7 and 9 modules: 'Création sonore appliquée', 'Workshop applicatif', 'Production, diffusion et perception du son, appliquées au design sonore', 'Informatique sonore et technique son', 'Workshop arduino', 'Méthodologie créative en design sonore', 'Atelier Radio', 'Éléments scientifiques', 'Concepts de design et cognition auditive appliqués au design sonore', 'Histoire et théorie du sonore', 'Ateliers de recherche et création (ARC)', 'Anthropocène : usage et mésusage du monde', histoire des arts, pratique professionnelle, pré-mémoire then mémoire. Semester 8 is an international exchange or a company placement. Semester 10 = mémoire and plastic-work defence before a jury of professionals. The year opens with a two-week 'workshop applicatif' answering a real brief from an industrial or institutional partner, in mixed teams with ENSCI design students — past clients include Décathlon, SETRAM / Le Mans Métropole (tram sonification), Groupe PSA (gestural and sound interfaces), SNCF Direction Innovation, Maison de la Radio / Radio France, RATP, GHT Psychiatrie Sainte-Anne. Students run radio on the school station and produce work for Le Mans Sonore, the city's international sound biennial (4th edition in 2026). NEW AND CONFIRMED: 'En 5ᵉ année, TALM offre à ses étudiant·es la possibilité d'effectuer leur master en alternance' — a paid apprenticeship route in the final year.
_rec.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED from the live admissions page, which SUPERSEDES the older brochure. 'Cette commission est destinée : aux candidat·es déjà inscrit·es dans une autre école d'art agréée par le ministère de la Culture ; aux candidat·es ou diplômé·es d'un autre cursus artistique français ou étranger.' Credits: 'Les candidat·es doivent justifier de 180 crédits (intégration en semestre 7) ou 180 crédits + 60 crédits (intégration au semestre 9)'; non-EU diplomas 'feront l'objet d'un contrôle de leur comparabilité avec les diplômes français'. Language: minimum B2 TCF or DELF plus certified translations of diplomas. Fee: 'frais de gestion de dossiers … 55 euros', payable per site (a separate €55 for each site applied to). The 2022 brochure adds the accepted-diploma list: 'diplômé.e d'une filière artistique ou d'électroacoustique des universités (ou … inscrit.e en licence au moment du concours) ; d'une école d'art ou de design équivalent au niveau licence (DNA ou équivalents étrangers) ; d'une école d'enseignement musical spécialisé équivalent au niveau licence (DNSPM ou équivalents étrangers), d'un DEM de composition ou électroacoustique … à condition de posséder en plus une licence scientifique ou en sciences humaines.' Selection criteria: 'La motivation, l'ouverture d'esprit, la faculté d'adaptation à des contextes spécifiques, le potentiel à travailler en équipe'. About ten places: 'accessible à une dizaine de jeunes diplômé.e.s'.
_rec.portfolioSpec: NOW CONFIRMED (was previously recorded as unverified). 'Pièces constitutives du dossier de candidature : 1 – Dossier administratif … 2 – Dossier personnel : Curriculum vitae détaillant les acquis de formation sonore, acoustique design, pratique artistique, projets personnels ; Une lettre de motivation argumentée sur la conception du design sonore, les domaines d'intérêt ; Catalogue de réalisations artistiques, dessins, vidéos, musiques, photos, peinture, sculpture, etc. ; Catalogue de réalisation sonore – 1 ou plusieurs extraits pour un total de 5 minutes maximum. Pour chaque extrait il est nécessaire de définir par écrit l'objectif artistique ou de design, la nature originelle du document et le format du fichier ; Un projet d'échange international ou de stage qui a lieu au deuxième semestre ; Un projet de mémoire.' The downloadable dossier de candidature for the chosen mention is the authoritative version each year — request/download it from esad-talm.fr in January.
_rec.auditionSpec: CONFIRMED, and CORRECTED: the interview is REMOTE, not on site at Le Mans. Three steps. 1st: submit the completed dossier by the deadline to the mailbox indicated. 2nd: 'Présélection — Evaluation des dossiers de candidature par un jury d'enseignant·es.' 3rd: 'en distanciel … Le ou la candidat·e présente devant un jury son dossier personnel. Lors de l'entretien, les membres de la commission évaluent le dossier artistique du ou de la candidat·e et apprécient l'effective capacité de celui-ci ou de celle-ci à intégrer le domaine choisi.' Held 'via la plateforme Teams. Il ne sera pas nécessaire d'installer de logiciel, mais une caméra est obligatoire.' No written test, no on-site travel — a significant practical advantage.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: NO / CHECK — probably not eligible on his current profile. The live admissions page restricts the commission to candidates already enrolled in a Ministry-approved art school, or holders/graduates of 'un autre cursus artistique français ou étranger'. A software-engineering BSc is neither. In the brochure's diploma list a scientific licence appears only as an ADDITIONAL condition bolted onto the DEM route ('à condition de posséder en plus une licence scientifique ou en sciences humaines'), never as a standalone qualification. His 180 ECTS satisfy the credit rule, and the school does say the DNSEP 'sadresse à tout type de créat.eurs.rices sonores … dont la pratique sonore et musicale peut s'adapter', so there is discretion — but he must get written confirmation from contact-lemans@talm.fr / olivier.houix@talm.fr before investing.
_rec.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Pattern published by the school: 'Les dossiers d'inscription à la commission sont mis en ligne chaque année sur notre site internet mi-janvier. La présélection puis l'entretien avec le jury se déroulent entre début avril et mi-mai selon les années.' Expect mid-January 2027 for the Sept-2027 intake.
_rec.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 2026 cycle (confirmed on the live admissions page): 'Date limite de candidature 2026 : le 22 mars'; presélection follows; interviews '1er, 2 ou 3 avril 2026 – en distanciel'. A supplementary September commission exists but for 2026 it covered only the Design computationnel mention (deadline 14 August 2026), not Design sonore. No 2027 dates published as of July 2026.
_rec.tuitionIntl: CONFIRMED (official TALM 'Les droits d'inscription 2026-2027' page, délibération n°693-2024 of 19 Feb 2024): 'pour les élèves originaires de pays hors Union Européenne (hors mobilité) : 1 500 €' per year (vs €1,000 for EU students in 2e/3e cycle). Of this, €150 is payable to confirm the place and the balance at dossier submission. Add CVEC €105 (2025-26 rate; the school's own cost page cites €95 for non-scholarship students — the two official pages differ slightly), a compulsory €15 Abaho association fee, a €50 cleaning deposit cheque for Le Mans students, and the €55 per-site application fee. 'Les élèves boursiers ou boursières sont exonéré·es de frais d'inscription.'
_rec.fundingLevel: Partial — modest non-EU tuition (€1,500/yr) and full exemption for CROUS bursary holders, but no entry stipend. The year-5 alternance (apprenticeship) route is a genuine paid-study option worth investigating.
_rec.scholarship: None found reserved for non-EU degree-seeking candidates. The school runs a 'Les bourses d'étude' page and exempts CROUS bursary holders from tuition entirely, but CROUS eligibility for a newly arrived Tunisian national is UNVERIFIED. Best lead beyond that is the 5th-year alternance contract, plus Campus France Tunisie / French Embassy funding.
_rec.stipend: None at entry. UNVERIFIED what a year-5 alternance contract pays.
_rec.facilities: CONFIRMED: 'Studio son, équipé d'une écoute en 5.1'; multitrack digital recorders, an ambisonic microphone, an octophonic diffusion system, assorted microphones, audio interfaces, amplifiers and loudspeakers; MIDI controllers and a radio studio; plus full art-school workshops (métallerie, sérigraphie, menuiserie, impression 3D, robotique, découpe laser, volume, photo, video, gravure, peinture, mécatronique) and a computer park with ProTools, Premiere Pro, the Adobe suite, Rhino and 3DsMax. Partners: IRCAM (Labo STMS, équipe Perception et Design Sonores — Nicolas Misdariis, Patrick Susini), ENSCI-Les Ateliers Paris (Roland Cahen, head of the sound studio), and Le Mans Université's LAUM (CNRS, Christophe Ayrault). Teaching team: Olivier Houix (IRCAM researcher, doctor in acoustics, coordinator), Rodolphe Alexis, Fabien Bourdier, Ludovic Germain (ENSCI graduate, founder of the LAPS sound-design agency). The school states it is 'le seul établissement à assurer sur le plan international une formation supérieure diplômante et qualifiante dans le secteur d'activité du design sonore'. Host of the Le Mans Sonore biennial.
_rec.fitNotes: Exceptional industry exposure — live briefs from SNCF, RATP, PSA, Radio France, Décathlon — and the IRCAM / ENSCI / LAUM triangle has no European equivalent. Cost is manageable at €1,500/yr non-EU, admission is remote (no travel), the portfolio spec is now known, and the 5th year can be done as a paid alternance. But two things count against it for him. Discipline: this is FUNCTIONAL sound design — product, transport, museum, UX signage, radio — explicitly positioned AGAINST specialised music tracks ('Contrairement aux formations proposant des objectifs très spécialisés (design musical, son à l'image, jeux vidéos…)'), so it does not serve a DJ/producer goal. Eligibility: the commission is written for candidates coming from an art, design or electroacoustic cursus, and a software-engineering BSc is not one. Only pursue after written confirmation from the school, and only if he has by then built a real sound/art portfolio.

_rec.program: ΠΜΣ «Οπτικοακουστικές Τέχνες στην Ψηφιακή Εποχή» / MA in Audiovisual Arts in the Digital Age
_rec.university: Ionian University — Department of Audio and Visual Arts, School of Music and Audiovisual Arts
_rec.city: Corfu — but note that only 10% of teaching hours are delivered on site
_rec.institutionType: Public university
_rec.degree: Δίπλωμα Μεταπτυχιακών Σπουδών — 2nd-cycle postgraduate diploma. No specialisations: the programme is deliberately undivided "λόγω του ιδιαίτερου προσανατολισμού του σε υποψηφίους οι οποίοι θα πρέπει να έχουν μια συνολική εικόνα του πεδίου της Οπτικοακουστικής Τέχνης".
_rec.durationEcts: 3 semesters (minimum registration), maximum total registration 3 years; full-time only, "δεν παρέχεται η δυνατότητα μερικής φοίτησης". Modules run across semesters 1–2 and the thesis occupies semester 3. The ECTS total is NOT stated in the 2026-27 call; the structure (3 compulsory + 2 of 5 electives per semester, then a thesis) is consistent with 90 ECTS but that figure is not published in the documents read.
_rec.language: GREEK — VERIFIED verbatim in the current call: "Η γλώσσα διδασκαλίας είναι η Ελληνική. Εν τούτοις, η συγγραφή των Μεταπτυχιακών Διπλωματικών Εργασιών μπορεί να γίνει και στην Αγγλική ύστερα από επιλογή του φοιτητή σε συνεννόηση με τον επόπτη διδάσκοντα." Only the thesis may be written in English. This corrects the prior record's "UNVERIFIED — presumed".
_rec.focus: Digital and new-media audiovisual art; sound art is one strand among visual, moving-image, interactive and mixed-reality work
_rec.whatYouStudy: Verified from the 2026-27 call. Semester A, three compulsory modules: Τεχνολογία και Τέχνη (Technology and Art), Ψηφιακή Αφήγηση (Digital Narrative), ΗΧΗΤΙΚΗ ΤΕΧΝΗ (Sound Art); plus two electives from five: Digital Illustration and Motion Graphics, Semiotic Analysis of New Media, Creative Web Technologies, Digital Poetics, Organic Open-Source Programming. Semester B, three compulsory: Διαδραστικά Περιβάλλοντα – Εγκαταστάσεις (Interactive Environments and Installations), Τέχνη Κινούμενης Εικόνας (Moving Image Art), Απεικονίσεις Μεικτής Πραγματικότητας (Mixed Reality Representations); plus two electives from five: Digital Multimedia Content Design, Digital Art and Public Space, ΜΟΥΣΙΚΗ, ΠΟΛΥΜΕΣΑ ΚΑΙ ΑΛΓΟΡΙΘΜΟΙ (Music, Multimedia and Algorithms), Performative Interventions, From Idea to Screen: Film Direction and Production. Semester C: the thesis. At least 50% of the teaching load of each module must consist of applied individual or group creative work. Students participate in the department's annual Audiovisual Arts Festival each May as part of the curriculum. DELIVERY MODEL, newly verified and significant: 10% of teaching hours in person, 90% at a distance via a synchronous tele-education platform.
_rec.entryRequirements: Holders of a first-cycle degree from a Greek HEI or an equivalent foreign institution under Article 34 of Law 4485/2017 — BUT with a decisive restriction, quoted from the 2026-27 call: "Βάσει της ανωτέρω ιδιαίτερης στοχοθεσίας του ΠΜΣ, το πτυχίο των υποψηφίων που θα γίνονται δεκτοί στο ΠΜΣ θα πρέπει να έχει σχέση πρωτίστως με τις παραδοσιακές μορφές τέχνης" — the candidate's degree must relate primarily to TRADITIONAL ART FORMS. The three eligible categories are (a) Arts, Design and Architecture (Fine or Applied Arts, Cinema, Graphic Arts, Photography, Industrial Design, Architecture), (b) Music Science and Art (Music Studies), (c) applied art and audiovisual technology and communication (Cultural Environment Management and New Technologies, Cultural Technology and Communication, Mass Media). Exception clause: "Κατ' εξαίρεση, είναι δυνατή η εισαγωγή στο ΠΜΣ αποφοίτων τμημάτων λοιπών γνωστικών πεδίων, υπό την απαραίτητη προϋπόθεση ότι αυτοί ήδη έχουν καλλιτεχνική δραστηριότητα και έχουν να επιδείξουν προς κρίση δημιουργικό καλλιτεχνικό έργο (αρχείο καλλιτεχνικών εργασιών)." Required documents: online application; ID copy; recent photograph; degree certificates (with a place-of-study certificate for foreign awards and a DOATAP national-register check — no formal act of academic equivalence is needed if the institution is on the DOATAP National Register of Recognised Foreign HEIs); a foreign-language certificate; full CV; Statement of Purpose; AT LEAST TWO recommendation letters; the mandatory portfolio; and any further supporting evidence.
_rec.portfolioSpec: MANDATORY — this corrects the prior record's UNVERIFIED. Item 9 of the 2026-27 call's document list reads: "Υποχρεωτικό φάκελος που να τεκμηριώνουν την υποψηφιότητα όπως, εργασιακή εμπειρία, φάκελος καλλιτεχνικών έργων (Σχέδιο, Ζωγραφική, Φωτογραφία, Μουσική, Βίντεο, Πολυμεσικό Έργο, Animation, Κόμικ, Οπτικοακουστικές Εγκαταστάσεις, και οποιοδήποτε άλλο δημιουργικό έργο)." A portfolio of artistic works — drawing, painting, photography, MUSIC, video, multimedia work, animation, comics, audiovisual installations or any other creative work — is compulsory. No number, duration or format is prescribed. For a candidate entering via the exception clause the portfolio is doubly load-bearing, since it is the evidence of the pre-existing artistic activity the clause requires.
_rec.auditionSpec: No audition. Candidates meeting the criteria may be called for interview if the evaluation committee deems it necessary, within one month of the application deadline, and "Οι συνεντεύξεις θα πραγματοποιηθούν διαδικτυακά" — the interviews are held ONLINE. Performance in the interview is counted in the final evaluation under the programme regulation.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: NO as a matter of ordinary eligibility — this reverses the prior record's "Likely yes". A BSc in Software Engineering is not in any of the three named categories; the published rule is that the degree must relate primarily to traditional art forms. He could only enter through the "κατ' εξαίρεση" clause, which is conditional on already having artistic activity and a body of creative artistic work to submit for judgement. Since he has no released or documented artistic output yet, that clause is not currently open to him either.
_rec.tuitionIntl: €2,400 total — VERIFIED in the 2026-27 call, payable in full on enrolment or in six instalments of €400: on acceptance, then 1 December 2026, 1 March 2027, 1 June 2027, 1 September 2027 and 1 December 2027. Non-refundable if studies are interrupted.
_rec.scholarship: Υποτροφίες Αριστείας / excellence provisions: up to 30% of admitted students are fully exempt from all tuition under Article 35 of Law 4485/2017. The entrance exam content (melodic dictation, transposing-instrument notation, timbral hearing, instrument recognition) shows the discipline is built on classical-music aural skill, not electronic production.

Melodic dictation and transposing-instrument notation are skills acquired over years of formal solfège training. Someone with no conservatoire background and no music degree cannot pass this within a year of self-study.

_rec.deadline: UNVERIFIED — not published. Ask UNMB's Studii Postuniversitare office.
_rec.visaEligible: ALMOST CERTAINLY NOT. A 146-hour, 15-ECTS postgraduate certificate is not a degree programme and will not support a Romanian long-stay study visa or student residence permit for a third-country national. Romania's Letter of Acceptance machinery is built around bachelor's, master's and doctoral study cycles. Do not plan a move to Romania around this.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: NO in practice. Although the formal condition is only a bachelor's degree, the entrance examination requires melodic dictation, notation of transposing instruments, and aural instrument/timbre recognition — conservatoire skills. Without a music background he would fail the exam.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: €1,600 tuition plus 250 RON in fees, plus Bucharest living costs for the duration. Irrelevant in practice, because it neither confers a degree nor supports a residence permit.
_rec.recommendation: DO NOT PURSUE — RECORDED AS A TRAP. Searching 'music direction Romania master' or 'regie muzicală' will lead him straight here, at Romania's national music university, at an apparently affordable €1,600 for international students. It is not a master's degree. It is a 146-hour, 15-ECTS professional certificate — one-eighth the volume of a real second-cycle degree — it will not support a student residence permit, it is taught in Romanian, and its entrance exam (melodic dictation, transposing-instrument notation, timbral hearing) is a conservatoire aural test he cannot pass without years of solfège training. The low price is a signal of what it is, not a bargain. Note also that UNMB's actual master's portfolio contains NO sound-technology programme at all: the Faculty of Composition, Musicology and Music Pedagogy offers only Stil și limbaj compozițional, Sinteză muzicologică, Stilistică dirijorală, Jazz și culturi muzicale pop, Educație muzicală contemporană and Culturi muzicale religioase, and the Faculty of Musical Interpretation offers only performance-stylistics masters. UNMB is therefore a dead end for him and should be closed off entirely.

CGL's own cost worksheet for a non-EU student over the whole programme: EUR 200 + EUR 1,240 semester fees + EUR 10,000 tuition + EUR 22,416 living costs, and the EUR 22,416 must be proved to the Immigration Office to obtain the residence permit.
_rec.scholarship: No programme scholarship. The official FAQ only signposts external routes: TH Köln's scholarship advice service (stipendienberatung@th-koeln.de), daad.de/scholarships for international students, and applicaid.org. DAAD is a genuinely separate application track with its own much earlier deadlines and would need its own research.
_rec.entryRequirements: Three hard conditions, quoted from the official application page: (1) "The successful completion of a university degree with the degree 'Bachelor of Arts' or 'Bachelor of Sciences' or with an equivalent or higher degree... in any field." (2) "Proof of at least 12 months of professional experience relevant to the course of study, completed AFTER earning the first university degree... should be accumulated by the start of the program. It can, however, be acquired cumulatively... gained within the last five years prior to the application." (3) A portfolio documenting creative and scholarly achievements, plus English at minimum B2. International applicants must ALSO have their degree validated by uni-assist in parallel, by the same deadline, with certified copies and certified translations if the documents are not in English or German. He can pre-check whether SMU MedTech is recognised at anabin.kmk.org (needs status H+).
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Yes, without qualification — "a university degree... in any field", and the FAQ adds "The MA Game Development and Research program welcomes applicants from all professional backgrounds." A software-engineering degree is an asset here, not a problem. The real gate is not the degree but the 12 months of post-bachelor professional experience in a games/media-relevant field: he graduates in 2026 with none, so for a September 2027 start he would need roughly a year of relevant work between graduation and enrolment (employment, self-employment, project work, internships and research-assistant posts all count, and can be accumulated in pieces).
_rec.portfolioSpec: Now fully documented. The portfolio is free-form work samples, explicitly NOT required to be game work: "These do not need to be works in game design, since we do not require that applicants have previous experience in that field." Submit as a PDF, a Dropbox/Google Drive link or an online portfolio; analogue work must be scanned or photographed. CGL's own list of acceptable content includes, under 'Samples of other Audiovisual Artwork': "Audio Work: If you have sound design or music composition skills, present examples" — so his production work would count. Alongside the portfolio, every MA GDR applicant must complete the annual application TASK, which consists of a project idea, an application video of maximum 10 minutes, and three short written assignments; the exact brief is published only when the portal opens on 1 March. Other uploads: CV, portrait photo, scanned certificates and degree, proof of the 12 months' experience (contracts or dated project documents), and optionally an English certificate.
_rec.auditionSpec: No audition. The formal selection is an "artistic-scientific aptitude test" made up of the submitted documents and application tasks. An interview is only sometimes used: "In some cases, the committee may invite applicants to an individual online-interview (approximately 10 minutes)... The interview is an additional method to evaluate an applicant's language skills." It is ONLINE, short, and about English proficiency, not performance. CORRECTION to the prior entry: the '11 and 13 June' interview dates came from a one-off news post about an extended cycle, not from the standing admission process.
_rec.applicationOpens: 1 March each year — "The application tasks are always published on March 1st", which is also when the application portal opens. For a September 2027 start, expect 1 March 2027.
_rec.deadline: 31 March at 23:59 CEST — published as a standing annual rule: "The application deadline is always March 31, at 23:59 CEST", with the uni-assist submission deadline also 31 March, and successful applicants notified in June to start in September. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date only for the extension: the news page that was originally cited as the source announced a one-off extension to 24 April with interviews on 11 and 13 June; that is not the standing rule and must not be planned around. Practical timing for September 2027: begin uni-assist paperwork by roughly January 2027 (evaluation takes up to four weeks or longer at peak), watch for the tasks on 1 March 2027, submit by 31 March 2027.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Confirmed module structure, four semesters. Semester 1 'Equalization & Exchange' — levelling projects 'Playing with Theater', 'Playing with Cinema', 'Playing with Video Games', plus Media and Game Studies 101, Visual Design 101, Game Design Theory 101. Semester 2 'Critical Play & Adaptation' — projects on Board Games, Serious Games and Non-Linear Adaptation, plus the 102-level theory courses. Semester 3 'Professionalization & Experimentation' — the commercial games market, financing, self-publishing versus publishers, pitch and marketing strategy, plus a larger experimental third-semester project and the 103-level theory courses. Semester 4 — Master's Project: thesis with a theoretical and a practical part, plus a colloquium. Only 20 students per year. THE DECISIVE FINDING: there is no audio, sound-design, music, Wwise/FMOD or middleware module anywhere in the published structure. The programme describes itself as research into "non-linear audio-visuality", which reads as audio-related but in practice means audiovisual media as a whole; the taught strands are game design, visual design, media and game studies, programming and professionalization. Graduate profiles listed by CGL: Game Designer, Game Artist, Game Programmer, Interactive Designer, Concept Author, Stage Director, Project Manager — no audio role.
_rec.facilities: Not itemised on the official pages. Confirmed instead: a dedicated games institute with its own building in Cologne, six named professors (Bartholdy, Freyermuth, Guardiola, Hoffmann, Klemke, Limpach) plus industry guest lecturers, a cohort of only 20, the Clash of Realities international games conference hosted in-house, and an incubator strand (The Game Starter Foundry, Broken Paternoster Games). No studio, console or audio facility is claimed.
_rec.fitNotes: Verified as existing, well-run and genuinely open to a software engineer — and verified as the wrong programme for him. It is English-taught, accepts any bachelor, accepts an audio portfolio, needs no audition, needs no IELTS, and costs a manageable EUR 10,000 plus fees. But it does not teach sound. If his goal shifts to games programming or games research it is a strong option; for becoming a producer, DJ or sound designer it teaches him nothing he needs. Secondary blocker even then: 12 months of post-degree professional experience in a media-relevant field, which he will not have until roughly late 2027 at the earliest. Recommend excluding from the audio shortlist.

_rec.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED that Electronic Music is one of five specialisations, alongside Performing Music, World Music, Songwriting, and Music Business and Management. The programme balances practice, composition, programming and production with theoretical grounding in popular musicology; the Electronic Music strand centres on music technology and sound design in the studio, and on the use of live electronics in a concert context, including performance and its relationship to music technology and sound design. Indicative course structure (2023 plan): Aesthetics (5 ECTS), Audience Development and Marketing (5 ECTS), Arts Entrepreneurship (5 ECTS), Individual Performance and Interpretation I–IV (15 ECTS each), musicological theory, and a 30-ECTS master's thesis. UiA also runs a Bachelor in Electronic Music, so the department has an established teaching base in the field. Course-level detail beyond the specialisation description: partly UNVERIFIED.
_rec.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED: a bachelor's degree or equivalent education of at least three years (180 credits), with a specialisation unit of at least 80 credits, of which 'At least 20 credits in the specialisation unit must be level 2'. For the ELECTRONIC MUSIC specialisation specifically: 80+ credits in performing or electronic music, a music technology bachelor's degree, or equivalent. Minimum grade average of C. Performance-track applicants must also document music theory/analysis coursework equivalent to UiA's own bachelor. A project proposal must be approved five weeks before the entrance exam. Programme coordinator: Per Elias Drabløs (per.e.drablos@uia.no).
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: NO as published. The Electronic Music route requires '80+ credits in performing or electronic music, music technology bachelor's, or equivalent' plus a C average and documented music theory/analysis. A pure software-engineering BSc carries none of those credits. The 'or equivalent' wording is the only opening and, unlike NTNU, UiA publishes no explicit individual-assessment promise. Treat as blocked unless the coordinator says otherwise in writing.
_rec.portfolioSpec: PARTIALLY CONFIRMED. A PROJECT PROPOSAL is required and must be APPROVED FIVE WEEKS BEFORE the entrance exam — a hard intermediate gate that is easy to miss. The audio/video portfolio specification (number of works, durations, formats) is NOT published on the pages read — UNVERIFIED. Request it from the programme coordinator.
_rec.auditionSpec: CONFIRMED and it is the decisive obstacle. The entrance exam has two equally weighted parts: an AUDITION worth 50% of the score, requiring a minimum of 10 out of 20 to pass, and an INTERVIEW worth 50% (also scored 10–20), held only after the audition is passed. Whether the audition may be submitted as a recording or held online for overseas applicants is NOT published — UNVERIFIED, and must be confirmed before budgeting travel to Kristiansand.
_rec.tuitionIntl: CONFIRMED on UiA's official current-rates page: NOK 135,000 per academic year, Category B, which explicitly covers the Master in Popular Music and the Master in Popular Music – Music Business and Management. (For context, Category B is UiA's most expensive band — its other master's programmes sit at NOK 63,000–92,000.) Payment deadline 1 September for active students; 10 March for those admitted in February. Still the cheapest Norwegian option in this batch by a wide margin — roughly a third of NMH and two-thirds of NTNU.
_rec.scholarship: CONFIRMED none: 'The University of Agder does not offer any scholarships for 2026/2027.' No fee waivers or reductions mentioned anywhere.

NOT CONFIRMED: the audio/video portfolio specification, whether the audition can be taken remotely, and the full current course list.
_rec.fitNotes: This is by a distance the best CONTENT match in the batch for what he actually wants — an explicit Electronic Music specialisation covering studio sound design and live electronics, taught in English, with entrepreneurship and audience-development modules that map unusually well onto building a DJ career, at NOK 135,000/year rather than NMH's 220,000. If he had a music background this would be an A. He does not, and the rubric puts it at C for two published reasons that compound: the specialisation requires 80 credits in performing or electronic music that he lacks, and the entrance exam is 50% AUDITION with a hard pass threshold, which he cannot currently clear and may not even be able to sit remotely. Add a flat no-scholarship policy against his funding preference. That said, this is the one C in the batch worth actively contesting rather than abandoning — the 'or equivalent' clause plus a genuinely strong body of electronic-music work is the most plausible argument available anywhere in this slice. Highest-value action: email Per Elias Drabløs (per.e.drablos@uia.no) in autumn 2026 with a portfolio, asking directly (a) whether an engineering BSc plus documented electronic-music practice can satisfy the 80-credit rule, and (b) whether the audition can be submitted as a recording from Tunisia. _rec.program: Master of Arts in Music, Major Komposition — combined with Minor Electronic Music Composition, Minor Media Composer or Minor Groove und Electronics
_rec.institution: Hochschule Luzern – Musik (Lucerne School of Music, Lucerne University of Applied Sciences and Arts)
_rec.institutionType: University of applied sciences and arts (Fachhochschule), music department
_rec.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. Hochschule Luzern is the university of applied sciences and arts of central Switzerland, carried by the six central Swiss cantons under the inter-cantonal FH Zentralschweiz concordat — its own site footers as 'FH Zentralschweiz'. It is institutionally accredited under the Swiss federal HFKG (the site states 'Institutionell akkreditiert nach HFKG 2019–2026'). It is not a private conservatory or a foundation school.
_rec.accreditationStatus: Real, state-recognised second-cycle degree. Institutionally accredited under the Swiss Hochschulförderungs- und -koordinationsgesetz (HFKG) 2019–2026, as published on its own pages. A Swiss MA from an accredited hochschule supports a Swiss student residence permit (B permit for studies) for a non-EU national, subject to cantonal quota and proof of funds.
_rec.qualification: Master of Arts in Music (MA), with a declared Major and optional Minors. A genuine second-cycle Swiss degree. HSLU – Musik offers exactly two masters: MA in Music and MA in Musikpädagogik.
_rec.focus: THIS IS THE FIND: the MA in Music carries an official Minor Electronic Music Composition, a Minor Groove und Electronics, and a Minor Media Composer, alongside Minor Komposition, Minor Jazz, Minor Improvisation, Minor Digitale Kompetenzen für Musik, Bildung und Kultur and others. Central Switzerland's electronic-music teaching sits inside this minor structure and is easy to miss because the minors are not marketed as standalone programmes.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Major Komposition is deliberately open: the curriculum is explicitly 'not profile-specific' and is set by individual target agreements, with Classical and Jazz orientations that 'can be individually modified and mixed'. On top of the major, the student stacks minors — Electronic Music Composition, Groove und Electronics, and Media Composer being the three that map onto electronic music production and scoring.
_rec.durationEcts: Master's programmes build on the bachelor; the standard Swiss MA in Music is 4 semesters / 120 ECTS but the exact ECTS is not stated on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED, ask musik@hslu.ch. IMPORTANT ADDITIONAL RULE, published officially: applicants WITHOUT a bachelor's degree from a Swiss music university may be required to sit a 'Standortbestimmung Theorie' (theory placement assessment), and depending on the outcome must pass an Auflagenmodul (bridging module) in the first master semester covering the target competences of the HSLU bachelor. Continuation beyond the first semester depends on passing it. For a candidate with no music degree at all, this bridging module is not a formality — it is a second exam.
_rec.language: GERMAN. Teaching is in German; the studienführer, curricula and fee regulations are published in German only, and the language rule below confirms German is the working language.
_rec.languageRequirement: Published officially and specific: B1 German for most master's programmes (including MA Music); B2 for Major Instrumental/Vocal Pedagogy and Church Music; C1 for Major Musiktheorie and School Music II. Crucially, HSLU states 'Knowledge of German is not required for the entrance examination, but knowledge of the German language must be proven in a language test' before studies begin. So he could sit the audition without German, but must certify B1 German before starting. No English certificate is required for the MA (C1 English is required only for the doctorate).
_rec.entryRequirements: A bachelor's degree plus a successful entrance examination ('Access to the Master of Arts in Music with majors including Composition is possible with an entrance examination'). Plus, for non-Swiss-music-bachelor holders, the theory placement assessment and possible bridging module described above. There is no published route that waives the entrance examination.
_rec.portfolioSpec: For a composition major, a portfolio of scores/works is the normal basis of the entrance examination. HSLU does not publish the composition portfolio specification on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED; request the Aufnahmeprüfung requirements for Major Komposition from musik@hslu.ch.
_rec.auditionSpec: Entrance examination required — this is a music-university audition/assessment, not an interview. HSLU charges 'CHF 200 per entrance examination (will be credited upon enrolment)', and the admission fee schedule refers to CHF 390 for two practical examinations, which implies the practical exam is a real, separately-priced component.
_rec.equipmentRequired: None published — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.facilities: Not published on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED. Given the Minor Electronic Music Composition and Minor Groove und Electronics exist, electronic-music studios must exist; ask musik@hslu.ch for a studio and equipment list before applying.
_rec.intakes: Autumn (September) start, one intake per year — consistent with a single 28 February application deadline.
_rec.applicationOpens: Not published as a fixed opening date — UNVERIFIED; online registration runs up to the 28 February deadline. Ask musik@hslu.ch.
_rec.deadline: 28 FEBRUARY ANNUALLY (29 February in leap years) for all degree programmes — stated as a standing annual rule, not a one-off cycle date, so this one does not need the prior-cycle caveat. Entrance examination fees are due at online registration. THIS IS THE ONE PROGRAMME IN THIS SWEEP WHOSE DEADLINE ACTUALLY FALLS INSIDE HIS OCTOBER 2026 – FEBRUARY 2027 WINDOW: for a September 2027 start he applies by 28 February 2027.
_rec.tuitionEU: CHF 800 per semester for domestic students. Note that Switzerland's split is Swiss/resident versus foreign-domiciled, NOT EU versus non-EU — an EU national who moves to Switzerland to study pays the same surcharge he would.
_rec.tuitionNonEU: CHF 1,300 PER SEMESTER — the rate he would pay. HSLU's exact official wording: 'CHF 1'300.– for international students (for students with foreign citizenship who enter or have entered Switzerland for the purpose of studying.)' That is CHF 2,600 per year, CHF 5,200 tuition over a 4-semester master. The surcharge exists because students entering Switzerland to study do not attract cantonal FHV subsidies.
_rec.otherFees: All published officially and all mandatory, and they add up: per semester — module examination CHF 150, photocopying CHF 45, service fee CHF 45, university sport CHF 25 (= CHF 265 per semester on top of tuition). One-off — enrolment fee CHF 390, HSLU card CHF 50, admission fee CHF 200 plus CHF 390 for two practical examinations, degree and certification CHF 220. Other — break from studies CHF 200 per semester, student exchange application CHF 200.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Fees only, over 4 semesters: tuition 4 × CHF 1,300 = CHF 5,200; compulsory per-semester extras 4 × CHF 265 = CHF 1,060; one-off admission/enrolment/card/diploma ≈ CHF 1,250 (200 + 390 + 390 + 50 + 220). Total institutional cost roughly CHF 7,500. Living costs in Lucerne are the dominant expense and are NOT published — Switzerland is the most expensive country in this slice, and the Swiss student permit requires proof of sufficient means (figure set cantonally — UNVERIFIED, confirm with the Swiss representation in Tunis and Kanton Luzern migration office).
_rec.scholarships: Nothing published at programme level. The database already holds the Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships – Art Scholarships stream, which is the one instrument that genuinely funds a first master's at a Swiss conservatory for a foreign national; Tunisia's eligibility and the art-stream country list change yearly, so confirm on the SERI/FCS official list for the 2027 call. UNVERIFIED for this programme specifically.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes in principle — an accredited Swiss hochschule degree programme supports a student residence permit, but Swiss student permits for non-EU nationals are discretionary, require proof of funds and of intent to leave, and are handled cantonally. Budget time for this.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: NO, not realistically. There is no music-degree requirement written as such, but the entrance examination for a composition major, plus the explicit theory placement assessment and bridging module for anyone without a Swiss music bachelor, together amount to a conservatory-level gate. A candidate with no music degree, no conservatory training and no portfolio cannot clear it in one year.
_rec.recommendation: IMPORTANT AS A DATABASE GAP, NOT AS A 2027 APPLICATION. Hochschule Luzern – Musik was absent from the database entirely, and its Minor Electronic Music Composition / Minor Groove und Electronics / Minor Media Composer are the closest thing to electronic-music-production training in central Switzerland — that is worth recording. But for THIS candidate the verdict is negative and should be stated plainly: a composition entrance examination, a theory placement test with a first-semester bridging module he must pass to continue, B1 German certified before he starts, roughly CHF 7,500 in institutional fees plus Swiss living costs, and no funding he is known to be eligible for. The single thing worth doing now, cheaply: the deadline is a standing 28 February, which does fit his planning window, so if in eighteen months his portfolio and German have both moved further than expected, this becomes reachable for a 2028 or 2029 start. File it, do not chase it.

Institution: Scuola universitaria di Musica, Conservatorio della Svizzera italiana (affiliated to SUPSI — University of Ap…

_rec.program: Master of Arts in Music Composition & Theory — Major in Composition
_rec.institution: Scuola universitaria di Musica, Conservatorio della Svizzera italiana (affiliated to SUPSI — University of Applied Sciences and Arts of Southern Switzerland)
_rec.institutionType: University-level music school (scuola universitaria di musica) operated by a foundation and affiliated to a public university of applied sciences
_rec.publicPrivate: AMBIGUOUS BY DESIGN — and this is exactly the case where the country's system makes the label unsafe, so here is the structure rather than a guess. The Conservatorio della Svizzera italiana is run by a private-law foundation, NOT by the canton directly. However, since 2006 its University School of Music has been affiliated to SUPSI, the public university of applied sciences of Italian-speaking Switzerland, and its degrees are issued in the Swiss public UAS system. Two pieces of hard evidence that it operates on the public side despite the private carrier: it charges the regulated Swiss two-tier fee (CHF 750 for Swiss nationals and residents versus CHF 1,500 for everyone else) and it explicitly grants the lower rate 'under the Intercantonal Agreement on Universities' — a private school has no access to intercantonal subsidy mechanisms. Practical answer: treat it as a state-recognised public-system music university with a private-foundation carrier. If the distinction matters for a scholarship application, get it in writing from the Conservatorio.
_rec.accreditationStatus: Real, state-recognised second-cycle Swiss degree. It is a Swiss KMHS (Konferenz Musikhochschulen Schweiz) member programme delivered in the SUPSI/UAS system, awarding a Master of Arts. It supports a Swiss student residence permit for a non-EU national — the institution runs its own 'Visas and permits' guidance for exactly this.
_rec.qualification: Master of Arts in Music Composition & Theory — Major in Composition. 4 semesters, 120 ECTS, full time. A genuine second-cycle degree, not a MAS/CAS. NOTE THE TRAP: the same institution separately offers a 'MAS in Music Composition' under continuing education — a MAS is a post-master continuing-education certificate, NOT a second-cycle degree, and it will not do the same job for a visa or for further study. He must apply for the MA, not the MAS.
_rec.focus: Composition and music theory, emphasising 'the creative dimension of composition, integrating reflection and craftsmanship'. Electronic music IS present but through an external arrangement: 'The electronic music section is arranged in partnership with the IRMus of the Accademia Internazionale della Musica in Milan.' That is a meaningful qualification — the electronic strand is delivered via a Milan partner institute rather than in-house, so ask what that means in practice for contact hours, travel and studio access.
_rec.whatYouStudy: Composition, with an electronic music section run in partnership with IRMus (Accademia Internazionale della Musica, Milan). Only one major is offered — composition; there are no alternative majors within this MA.
_rec.durationEcts: 4 semesters, 120 ECTS, full time. Officially described as requiring 'total dedication in terms of time and emotional involvement'.
_rec.language: ITALIAN. The course descriptor is published in Italian and the institution's language rule targets Italian, not English or German. Web pages are available in English, which is misleading — the teaching language is Italian.
_rec.languageRequirement: Published officially and unusually generous in timing: 'A sufficient level of Italian is equivalent to level B2 according to the CEFR, or CELI 3. Those who do not have this language level at the start of their studies must nevertheless demonstrate a sufficient level of Italian and reach level B2 or CELI 3 by the end of their first year of study.' So B2 Italian is not required at entry — it must be reached within the first year. No English certificate is mentioned. For a French-fluent Arabic native, Italian to B2 in a year is more achievable than German to B2, which is worth noting even though the rest of this record is negative.
_rec.entryRequirements: Application review followed by entrance examinations by invitation: 'Candidates will receive timely invitations by email to the various examinations, which will take place in April.' A bachelor-level qualification plus the composition entrance examination. Specific academic prerequisites are not itemised on the programme page — UNVERIFIED; request the admission dossier for the MA Composition from the Conservatorio.
_rec.portfolioSpec: Not published on the programme page — UNVERIFIED. For a composition major a portfolio of scores and/or recordings will be required; the institution publishes per-programme admission pages (e.g. 'Admission BAM Composition') so ask for the master-level equivalent directly.
_rec.auditionSpec: Entrance examinations held in APRIL, by invitation only after application review. This is a music-university admission examination, not an interview.
_rec.equipmentRequired: None published — UNVERIFIED.
_rec.facilities: Not published — UNVERIFIED, and materially important here because the electronic music section is run through a Milan partner (IRMus) rather than in-house. Ask specifically: what electronic-music studio facilities exist in Lugano, and how much of the electronic strand is taught in Milan.
_rec.intakes: Autumn start, single annual intake (consistent with a 20 February deadline and April examinations).
_rec.applicationOpens: Not published — UNVERIFIED. Applications close 20 February, so the window opens some months earlier; ask the Conservatorio.
_rec.deadline: 20 FEBRUARY, with entrance examinations in April (2026 cycle: application deadline 20 February 2026). PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date, though the 20 February date is presented as the standing master's deadline. For a September 2027 start, expect 20 February 2027 — INSIDE his October 2026 – February 2027 planning window.
_rec.tuitionEU: CHF 750 tuition + CHF 250 administrative fee = CHF 1,000 per semester — but ONLY for Swiss nationals and residents qualifying under the Intercantonal Agreement on Universities. There is no EU rate as such; EU nationals arriving from abroad pay the higher rate below.
_rec.tuitionNonEU: CHF 1,500 tuition + CHF 250 administrative fee = CHF 1,750 PER SEMESTER — this is the rate he would pay as a Tunisian national ('all other students'). CHF 3,500 per year; CHF 7,000 over the 4-semester master.
_rec.otherFees: Matriculation CHF 250 one-time; student union CHF 5 per semester; final exam CHF 250; reassessment of main subject CHF 200; reassessment of a non-main subject CHF 100; deferred exam CHF 500. The CHF 500 deferred-exam fee is worth noting — Swiss music schools price re-sits aggressively.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: Institutional fees over 4 semesters: 4 × CHF 1,750 = CHF 7,000, plus matriculation CHF 250, student union CHF 20, final exam CHF 250 — roughly CHF 7,520 before any re-sits. Living costs in Lugano are not published and are high by any non-Swiss standard. Swiss student permit requires proof of means — figure UNVERIFIED, confirm with the Swiss representation in Tunis and the Ticino migration authority.
_rec.scholarships: Nothing published at programme level. The relevant instrument is the Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships Art Scholarships stream (already in the database) — confirm Tunisia's inclusion in the art-stream country list for the 2027 call, because that list is narrower than the research-scholarship list and changes yearly. UNVERIFIED for this institution.
_rec.visaEligible: Yes — and the Conservatorio publishes its own 'Visas and permits' guidance with a critical operational warning for him: 'EU/EFTA citizens do not need to get a visa for sitting admission examinations; citizens from all other countries must check the updated list of requisites on the portal of the State Secretariat for Migration (SEM). In many cases, candidates must request a visa to be able to come to Lugano for the admission exam.' A Tunisian applicant may therefore need a visa merely to ATTEND the April entrance examination, months before any study permit. That is a real cost and a real timeline risk that almost no directory site mentions.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: NO. A composition entrance examination by invitation, at a KMHS music university, is not passable by a candidate with no music degree, no conservatory training and no existing portfolio.
_rec.recommendation: RECORD IT, DO NOT APPLY. This closes a genuine hole — the Conservatorio della Svizzera italiana was absent from the database, and it is the only Italian-language music university in this slice with an electronic-music strand. Three findings from it are useful to him even though the programme is not: (1) the visa-to-attend-the-audition problem, which applies to every Swiss music-school audition he might ever consider and must be planned around months in advance; (2) the MA-versus-MAS trap at this institution — the 'MAS in Music Composition' is continuing education, not a degree, and would be the wrong thing to apply for; (3) the Italian B2-by-end-of-first-year rule, which is the most forgiving language regime found anywhere in this sweep and worth remembering if he ever looks at Italian-language options. As an application target for September 2027 it fails on the audition, on the CHF 7,500+ fees with no funding he is known to qualify for, and on the fact that composition is not music production.

_rec.university: Koninklijk Conservatorium Antwerpen (AP School of Arts, AP Hogeschool)
_rec.degree: Master in de Muziek / Master of Music — Jazz, Live Electronics
_rec.durationEcts: 2 years — CONFIRMED ("Na je bacheloropleiding van drie jaar zet je jouw opleiding verder in de tweejarige master"). ECTS total NOT published; a two-year Flemish master is conventionally 120 ECTS but AP does not state it, so treat 120 as inference, not fact. This matters for the fee calculation below.
_rec.language: No formal language requirement — CONFIRMED and a genuine advantage. AP states: "In 2026-2027 there are no official language requirements for the bachelor, master and postgraduate programmes Music" / "Voor de master- en postgraduaatsopleidingen Muziek zijn er geen officiële taalvoorwaarden." B2 Dutch is recommended, not required: "students are advised a B2 Dutch proficiency level for an effective day-to-day communication and high quality written assignments." (By contrast the educational master in Music requires mandatory B2 Dutch.) He would need no IELTS/TOEFL to enrol — though see the scholarship note, where IELTS 6.5 IS required.
_rec.institutionType: Conservatoire within a university of applied sciences and arts (AP Hogeschool)
_rec.focus: Live Electronics / Performance; Electronic Music Production; Immersive Audio (8-speaker system); algorithmic and live-coded music
_rec.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED on the official page. Live electronic performance and improvisation using live-coding environments (Sonic Pi, TidalCycles, Strudel, Vortex); modular synthesis on a vintage Roland System 100M plus modern eurorack; custom instrument building with Axoloti, Raspberry Pi, Arduino and Max; artificial intelligence for generating music in both audio and MIDI; performance at algoraves and jam sessions through an immersive eight-speaker system for spatial composition; both open-source and commercial DAWs. "Everything revolves around your artistic ambitions" — a personalised trajectory rather than a fixed syllabus. Teaching staff: Dago Sondervan, Lennart Heyndels, Inne Eysermans.
_rec.entryRequirements: Verified verbatim from the official registration page: "een diploma academische bachelor Muziek, afstudeerrichting Jazz of Jazz/lichte muziek geeft toegang tot de masteropleiding Muziek, afstudeerrichting Jazz" — Live Electronics sits inside the Jazz afstudeerrichting. A professional (non-academic) bachelor requires a bridging programme. A foreign diploma goes to the admissions committee: "De toelatingscommissie kan een kandidaat-student toelaten die een buitenlands diploma of getuigschrift heeft behaald ... voor zover de toelatingscommissie het behaalde diploma en het specifieke opleidingsprofiel van de student van voldoende niveau acht" — request to toelating@ap.be, uiterlijk 1 oktober. An artistic entrance exam (toelatingsproef) is required on top of the diploma condition; a voorbereidingsprogramma may be imposed.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: NO in practice — corrected from the earlier draft's 'Check'. The registration page is much stricter than the marketing page's "open to all music students with an undergraduate degree": direct access requires an academic bachelor in MUSIC with a Jazz or Jazz/lichte muziek specialisation. The foreign-diploma clause is not a general-purpose escape hatch — the committee must judge "het behaalde diploma EN het specifieke opleidingsprofiel van de student" to be of sufficient level for this programme, which a Software Engineering BSc with no music training will not satisfy. The realistic published path for him is a voorbereidingsprogramma (preparatory year) before the master, and he should ask toelating@ap.be directly about it, well before the 1 October deadline.
_rec.portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED for Live Electronics specifically. AP publishes no portfolio specification (number of works, durations, formats) for this specialisation. Related data point: for Jazz, AP allows audition via media uploaded to an "online platform (YouTube, Vimeo, soundcloud, etc.)", and for Composition it requires recordings plus scores. Ask the jazz department.
_rec.auditionSpec: An artistieke toelatingsproef is compulsory for all master applicants: "All master applicants must pass an orientation-based artistic test", with content varying by specialisation. The content for Live Electronics is NOT published. Given the live-performance and improvisation orientation (algoraves, jam sessions) expect a practical performance component. Administrative fee €30 per separate School-of-Arts enrolment, never refunded.
_rec.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — AP does not publish an opening date for the artistic entrance-exam registration.
_rec.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Two dates are published and they are different things: the foreign-diploma admission request to toelating@ap.be is due "uiterlijk 1 oktober"; and 1 May is cited as the application deadline covering the full academic year / both semesters. Neither is given as a 2027-specific date. Confirm both directly with the jazz department and toelating@ap.be before relying on them.
_rec.tuitionIntl: €25,065 per year for a 60-credit year — NEWLY VERIFIED and the single biggest correction here. AP publishes for 2026-2027: non-EEA "tuition fee fixed part: 2.500,00 euro + 375,00 euro / ECTS + 65 euro course related fee" (confirmed independently in AP's official Reglement Studiegelden 2026-27: "Studiegeld buitenlandse studenten — Diploma- en creditcontracten 2500 375"). At 60 credits that is 2,500 + 22,500 + 65 = €25,065; across a two-year 120-credit master, roughly €50,130 total. For comparison, an EEA student pays €305.40 + €14.60/ECTS + €65, i.e. about €1,246 a year. Non-EEA students lost Flemish basic financing from 2026-2027, which is what produced this.
_rec.scholarship: Government of Flanders Master Mind. AP University of Applied Sciences and Arts IS a confirmed participating host institution, with a deadline of 1 March 2026 for the 2026-2027 call — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date; expect roughly 1 March 2027 for a September 2027 start, which fits his timeline if he starts early. Three hard obstacles: (a) GPA of 3.5/4.0 on his BSc; (b) IELTS overall band minimum 6.5 for schools of arts, certificate no older than 3 years — he has not sat it; (c) the master must be ENGLISH-TAUGHT, and AP's music master has no official language requirements at all rather than being an English-taught programme, so eligibility must be confirmed with AP's international office before counting on it. No Tunisia-specific allocation exists; reserved places go to Japan (3), Mexico (3), Palestine (2), USA (5).
_rec.fundingLevel: Partial at best; realistically None unless Master Mind is won
_rec.stipend: Master Mind, if awarded: €10,225 per academic year plus a tuition-fee waiver, with the host permitted to charge only the lowest local rate (€136.50 for 2026-2027); two academic years for a 120-ECTS master. Not combinable with Erasmus+, Erasmus Mundus, BAEF or Fulbright. Previous degree must not have been obtained at a Flemish institution (he is fine). Without it he faces roughly €50,000 of tuition across the two years.
_rec.facilities: CONFIRMED on the official page: immersive eight-speaker audio system for spatial composition; vintage Roland System 100M plus modern eurorack modular; Axoloti / Raspberry Pi / Arduino / Max instrument-building environment; live-coding stack (Sonic Pi, TidalCycles, Strudel, Vortex); AI music generation in audio and MIDI; open-source and commercial DAWs; algoraves and jam sessions as the regular performance outlet. Three working electronic musicians as principal study teachers.
_rec.fitNotes: Still the most code-native music master in the slice, and the language position is genuinely favourable — no official language requirement, no IELTS needed to enrol. But two facts that were UNVERIFIED in the earlier draft have now resolved badly. First, admission: direct access needs an academic bachelor in Music (Jazz or Jazz/lichte muziek), not merely 'a bachelor'; his route would be the foreign-diploma committee plus almost certainly a voorbereidingsprogramma, adding a year. Second, cost: €25,065 a year, about €50,130 for the two-year master, with no automatic funding. Practical next steps if he wants to keep it alive: email toelating@ap.be now about whether a Software Engineering BSc plus a self-built electronic-music portfolio can reach the committee at all and what preparatory year would be required, and separately ask AP's international office whether the music master counts as English-taught for Master Mind. Both answers are needed before this can be ranked above C.

CONFIRMED: 120 ECTS / 2 years, English as catalogue language of instruction, Malmö, the music-bachelor entry requirement, the full 3–4 work-sample portfolio spec with .mov and PDF notation, the three-part admission process including the on-site week-10 interview, and — newly — tuition of SEK 390,000 total / SEK 97,500 first instalment and the existence of Lund University Global Scholarship and Faculty of Fine and Performing Arts tuition grants. NOT CONFIRMED: whether the intake is truly biennial (one Lund page says 'open for applicants every second year', the others do not restate it), the exact application fee amount on the programme page, and the precise Swedish/English teaching split.
_rec.fitNotes: The admission process here is the most transparently documented in the whole Nordic slice, and the take-home exam — compose a theme, score an assigned clip, mix it, submit audio and video — is genuinely the kind of test a self-taught producer could excel at. Funding also looks better than first thought: SEK 390,000 total rather than an unknown, with a real Lund University Global Scholarship route. But it is a C for him for one hard reason and two soft ones. Hard: the entry requirement is 'a Bachelor in Music 180 credits or equivalent' with no discretionary clause, and his BSc does not meet it. If he still wants it, the sequence is: confirm the biennial question first, then learn notation, then apply — that is a multi-year plan, not a September 2027 one.

_rec.program: Máster en Producción de Música Electrónica (accredited by UDIMA)
_rec.university: SAE Institute Spain (SAE Creative Media Education) with Universidad a Distancia de Madrid (UDIMA)
_rec.degree: Two optional routes, both via UDIMA: Máster de Formación Permanente in Electronic Music Production (25 ECTS) if you hold a university degree, or Máster Profesional if you do not but have 2+ years' professional experience. Either way you also receive SAE Creative Media Education's Professional Diploma.
_rec.institutionType: Private specialist creative-media academy, accredited through a private distance university
_rec.focus: Electronic Music Production; Music Production; Sound Design; mixing and mastering; live performance and artist-career management
_rec.durationEcts: VERIFIED: 8 months, two semesters, fully in person. Approximately 8 contact hours per week over 4 days (SAE notes this can vary by course and time of year). 25 ECTS on the Formación Permanente route. Individual studio practice bookable from day one via an online reservation system.
_rec.language: Spanish. VERIFIED international-applicant wording: "IDIOMA: Español — Para estudiar en SAE, requerimos evidenciar su capacidad para hablar, escuchar, leer y escribir en castellano." (You must evidence your ability to speak, listen, read and write in Spanish.) No specific certificate or CEFR level is named — the evidencing method is at SAE's discretion, so ask what they accept.
_rec.whatYouStudy: VERIFIED. Semester 1 (Producción de música electrónica): sound theory, music theory (chord construction, programming bass lines), cabling and connections, MIDI protocol, audio processing (dynamics processors, FX handling, EQ), hardware and software synthesisers, samplers, vocal recording and processing, mixing techniques, and two sequencers in depth — Ableton Live and Logic Pro X. Assessment: one exam plus four practical projects (MIDI-station integration exercise, a mix, a remix, a free original track). Semester 2 (Producción de música electrónica avanzada): advanced mixing and production, hardware and modular synthesis (Moog Sub 37, Prophet 12, Doepfer), sound design, advanced harmony, building a LIVE PERFORMANCE, mastering in the box, interactive installations and Max for Live, plus the industry block — how the industry works, managing an artist career, digital marketing for artists, copyright, contracts, press dossier and promotion channels, with guest producers from electrónica and urbana. Final deliverable: a complete, professionally mastered production. Named hardware/software partners: Native Instruments, Apple, Logic, Ableton, Universal Audio, Moog, Dave Smith, Doepfer, Elektron, Roland, Akai.
_rec.entryRequirements: VERIFIED (international tab): to obtain the Máster de Formación Permanente (25 ECTS) from UDIMA you must hold "un título universitario oficial de Grado, Licenciatura, Ingeniería Superior o Técnica, Arquitectura Superior o Técnica, Diplomatura o equivalente"; without one you receive the Máster Profesional from UDIMA provided you demonstrate at least 2 years of professional experience. Minimum age 18 for international students (16 on the national tab). Process: complete the admissions questionnaire and attend an access appointment/interview with an educational advisor, in person or by Zoom/Skype. Non-EU nationals must obtain a student stay authorisation or visa. International admissions also require the admission form, enrolment agreement, educational offer, passport photo, proof of the pre-registration transfer and a copy of the visa if applicable — all sent together; documents sent separately are not accepted.
_rec.portfolioSpec: No portfolio required as published. Admission is questionnaire plus access interview with an educational advisor.
_rec.auditionSpec: None. No audition and no jury. The only live element is the access appointment with an educational advisor, which can be held by Zoom or Skype.

The only academic condition is an official university degree, and the published list of qualifying titles ("Grado, Licenciatura, Ingeniería Superior o Técnica, Arquitectura Superior o Técnica, Diplomatura o equivalente") is defined by LEVEL, not subject. A BSc Software Engineering satisfies it outright and puts him on the higher Formación Permanente (25 ECTS) route rather than the fallback Máster Profesional route. This is the lowest academic barrier in the batch.

Request a written quote from the campus admissions department (barcelona@sae.edu / madrid@sae.edu). Expect private-academy pricing well above the Portuguese and Catalan public options.

_rec.applicationOpens: Rolling — no fixed opening date. Process: request information, an educational advisor contacts you, then questionnaire, access interview, pre-registration payment and document pack.

The Ableton Live production certificate is included and awarded by an official Ableton certifier; staff include César Berti, an Ableton Live Certified Trainer. Faculty are working practitioners — DJs, producers, beatmakers, a Befaco co-founder, the artistic director of Brunch in the Park, the Wololo Sound CEO — genuine industry proximity for someone targeting the electronic-music scene. Delivery is fully in person: "los cursos son íntegramente presenciales".
