Semester 2: advanced mixing, hardware synthesizers (Moog Sub 37, Prophet 12, Doepfer), sound design, live performance, mastering, plus music industry and artist management. DAWs: Ableton Live, Logic Pro X, FL Studio. Hardware: Moog, Roland, Akai, Elektron, Dave Smith, Doepfer. Plugins: Native Instruments, Universal Audio. Includes official Ableton Live Certification delivered by a certified official trainer.
_rec.durationEcts: 8 months. Roughly 8 contact hours per week spread over 4 days, fully in person. The UDIMA 'Máster de Formación Permanente' route is 25 ECTS.
_rec.language: Spanish. The course page requires demonstrated Spanish-language ability for international applicants. This is a hard barrier — no English-taught version.
_rec.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL. This is the classic Spanish 'título propio' trap: it is marketed as a 'Máster' but the accrediting route is UDIMA's own non-official award (Máster de Formación Permanente / Máster Profesional), not ANECA. No ANECA verification. It does not give access to a Spanish doctorate and is not automatically recognised outside SAE and UDIMA. SAE Spain's own FAQ separates its offering into 'proprietary training (private degrees without official recognition)' and the separate official Grado en Música (Barcelona only) — the masters sit in the first category.
_rec.visaEligible: UNVERIFIED for this specific course, and doubtful. SAE Spain does operate a real non-EU visa support process: it issues an Admission/Acceptance Certificate containing the information needed for the visa, matriculation only begins after a favourable visa resolution, and it publishes a detailed visa page (consulate route ≥3 months ahead, or in-country route). Required documents: valid passport, SAE admission certificate, private Spanish health insurance, proof of monthly means (page still cites €537.94/month, a 2019 figure), plus for courses over 6 months a medical certificate and criminal-record check. HOWEVER this course runs only ~8 contact hours per week, which is well below the full-time intensity a Spanish 'estancia por estudios' normally requires. SAE's visa page does not state a minimum weekly hours threshold. He must get this confirmed in writing before paying anything.
_rec.acceptsNonMusic: Yes, explicitly. Entry is 'a university degree (Grado, Licenciatura, Engineering, Architecture, Diplomatura) OR 2+ years of professional experience'. His BSc in Software Engineering satisfies this directly. No music degree required.
_rec.entryRequirements: University degree or 2+ years professional experience; demonstrated Spanish-language ability; minimum age 18 for international students (16 for Spanish); admission interview.
_rec.portfolioSpec: No portfolio requirement published — admission is by interview. UNVERIFIED whether a demo is requested informally.
_rec.auditionSpec: Admission interview. No audition or test published.
_rec.englishTest: Not applicable — the requirement is SPANISH, not English. IELTS is irrelevant here. The page requires 'demonstrated Spanish language ability' for international students; no specific DELE level is published (UNVERIFIED).
_rec.intakes: Two intakes per year. Madrid: February 2026 and October 2026 published. For a September/October 2027 start, treat published dates as PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
_rec.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — not published. Admission runs through a rolling advisor-interview process.
_rec.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. No published application deadline; SAE Spain uses rolling admissions via campus advisors with places subject to availability.
_rec.tuitionPerYear: UNVERIFIED. SAE Spain publishes NO prices anywhere on its website. Its FAQ states only: 'If you want to know more about prices, start dates or course content, request information.'
_rec.tuitionTotal: UNVERIFIED — no published figure for any SAE Spain programme.
_rec.otherFees: UNVERIFIED. A pre-enrolment fee exists (it is the only item payable by card per the FAQ), but its amount is not published. No published application, materials, exam or insurance fees.
_rec.equipmentRequired: None required. SAE Spain's FAQ is explicit: 'No, it is not necessary. Facilities are equipped with all equipment, software and tools you'll need during your studies.' An Ableton Live educational licence is included via the Ableton certification.
_rec.paymentPlans: Three plans confirmed by the FAQ: PLAN A single payment (carries an early-payment discount per a secondary source), PLAN B quarterly, PLAN C monthly direct debit (no discount). Amounts UNVERIFIED.
_rec.scholarships: SAE Spain publishes a scholarships page but almost nothing on it is reachable by a non-EU applicant. Spanish MEC grants and Generalitat de Catalunya grants are for Spanish residents. SAE's own Barcelona-campus discounts are: academic excellence 60% (requires 9.0+ Bachillerato GPA or 9.0+ after year 1), unemployment/ERTE 10%, large family 10%, disability ≥33% 30%, current/former SAE student 40%, relative of a student 20%, gender-violence survivor 40%, Ukrainian refugee 100%. NONE of these fit a Tunisian self-payer with a foreign BSc — the 'relative of a student' 20% is the only conceivable one and only if a family member also enrols. Yamaha Music Europe Foundation (€1,000–€2,000, under 25, students at professional music institutions, awards announced Feb–Mar) is Europe-wide and is the one genuinely open award. The 'Tu Futuro Digital' scholarships (7 places, partial tuition) are listed by a third-party funding guide — eligibility for non-EU applicants UNVERIFIED.
_rec.facilities: Hardware synth collection named on the course page: Moog Sub 37, Prophet 12, Doepfer modular, plus Roland, Akai, Elektron and Dave Smith gear. Plugin suites from Native Instruments and Universal Audio. Ableton certified training centre.
_rec.reputationSignals: SAE is the largest audio-school chain in the world and its industry partnerships are real. But the reputational signals here are mixed and the price opacity is itself a red flag — a school that will not publish a number before an advisor call is optimising for sales pressure. Broader SAE review evidence (Glassdoor, student forums, aggregator reviews) repeatedly raises: credits not transferring to other accredited institutions, disorganisation, and instructors' qualifications not matching the price. Specific complaints about the Madrid/Barcelona campuses were not found — UNVERIFIED. Note the contrast: SAE Barcelona also runs an official 'Título de Grado en Música' (Enseñanzas Artísticas Superiores), which shows SAE Spain CAN hold official accreditation — it simply has not sought it for the masters.
_rec.totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED — impossible to state. No tuition, pre-enrolment or fee figure is published by SAE Spain for any programme. He must request a written quote before this can be compared to anything. Do not treat any third-party figure as reliable.
_rec.recommendation: Content-wise this is one of the closest matches to what he says he wants — Ableton, hardware synths, sound design, live performance, DJ-adjacent, taught on real Moogs and Prophets, with an Ableton certification thrown in. Three things kill it. First, it is taught in SPANISH and requires demonstrated Spanish ability, which he does not have and cannot realistically acquire to class level by September 2027 while also preparing IELTS. Second, the award is a título propio dressed as a 'Máster' — a 25-ECTS UDIMA Máster de Formación Permanente is not a master's degree in any meaningful sense and will not be recognised as one outside Spain. Third, at ~8 contact hours a week over 8 months, the student-visa case is weak and unproven. Refusing to publish a price compounds all of this. Verdict: do not commit. If he still wants it, treat it as a skills course, get the price and the visa position in writing first, and never call it a master's degree on a CV.

_rec.publicPrivate: PRIVATE. A vakıf (foundation) university — established and owned by the Bahçeşehir Uğur Eğitim Vakfı, a private educational foundation, not state-funded. Foundation universities in Turkey are nonetheless YÖK-supervised and award state-recognised degrees; they charge full tuition to everyone, Turkish and foreign alike.

_rec.qualification: Yüksek Lisans (master's). The university's own Bologna information package states the award sits at TYYÇ level 7 / QF-EHEA level 2 / EQF-LLL level 7 — a real second-cycle degree, valid for a student residence permit.
_rec.accreditationStatus: State-recognised, YÖK-authorised foundation university; the master's is listed in BAU's official AKTS/Bologna information package with its TYYÇ level. IMPORTANT WARNING attached to this institution: BAU also markets non-degree audio training through 'BAU IDEA' (bauidea.com, 'Audio & Sound Design'), which is a certificate operation and NOT a master's degree — do not confuse the two. Separately, BAU's conservatory graduate page still links a 'Ses Teknolojileri (Türkçe, Tezli/Tezsiz)' master's, but that link 404s on BAU's own site and the programme does NOT appear in BAU's live AKTS master's catalogue, so it appears dormant or discontinued even though 'Ses Teknolojisi Tezli/Tezsiz Yüksek Lisans Diploması' still exists as a registered qualification in the Turkish Qualifications Framework.
_rec.language: Turkish. BAU's own AKTS page for the programme states the language of instruction is Turkish; the conservatory's graduate offer is listed as Turkish-medium throughout. (By contrast BAU's undergraduate Music Technology department and many BAU engineering masters are English-medium — the graduate music programme is not.)
_rec.languageRequirement: Turkish proficiency required for a Turkish-medium programme; BAU's published general rule is an ALES or equivalent score for master's applicants and an English certificate only for English-medium programmes. _rec.whatYouStudy: Musicology plus performance practice, thesis/project work, academic ethics and research method. BAU's Conservatory Music department does carry a 'Müzik Teknolojileri' sub-module and BAU runs an undergraduate Müzik Teknolojisi department teaching recording, audio editing, mixing and mastering, but the master's as described is research-and-performance oriented, not a production course.

BAU's graduate fee page (2026-2027) did not render the figure for the Music programme when opened; the page confirms only that fees include VAT and that a 10% up-front discount applies. Ask BAU Student Services or apply through aday.bau.edu.tr for the exact Müzik tezli/tezsiz figure. _rec.scholarships: Türkiye Bursları's Art Scholarship does NOT cover Bahçeşehir (only Ankara MGÜ, Ankara Hacı Bayram Veli and İTÜ). BAU offers its own graduate discounts/early-payment reductions; scale UNVERIFIED. For a candidate who strongly prefers full funding, this is a poor fit.

_rec.recommendation: Report as a caution rather than a target. Three findings matter here. (1) The programme that would have suited him — 'Ses Teknolojileri' (Sound Technologies) master's, thesis and non-thesis, Turkish — is still advertised on BAU's conservatory graduate page but its own page 404s and it is absent from BAU's live Bologna catalogue, so it appears dormant; the qualification title nevertheless survives in the Turkish national qualifications register. If he is interested, ask BAU in writing whether Ses Teknolojileri will admit for 2027-28; do not apply on the strength of the stale web page. (2) What is actually live is a Turkish-taught Müzik master oriented to musicology and performance — the wrong shape for a producer with no music degree. (3) BAU IDEA's 'Audio & Sound Design' offering is a private certificate, NOT a degree and NOT a basis for a student residence permit as a master's — exactly the kind of product the brief warns about. Overall: skip unless BAU confirms Ses Teknolojileri is reopening, and even then the private fees conflict with his funding preference.
